# Tapir commands: Element Commands

The 198 commands of this group, with their parameters, results and examples. Every group and how a command is sent: [commands.md](https://archicad-api.com/commands.md).

## Element Commands

### GetSelectedElements

Gets the list of the currently selected elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 0.1.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSelectedElements

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Grasshopper: `ChangeSelectionComponent`, `GetSelectedElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSelectedElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSelectedElements.py): Prints the elements currently selected in Archicad with GetSelectedElements. Select some elements in Archicad before running it.

### GetElementsByType

Returns the identifier of every element of the given type on the plan. It works for any type. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Without databases it lists the current database: in a section or elevation window the model elements of the type that the window shows, the same elements GetAllElements reports there; pass the floor plan's database (GetDatabases) to list every one.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByType

Parameters:

- `elementType` (ElementType, required)
- `filters` (array of ElementFilter)
- `databases` (Databases)


Grasshopper: `GetElementsByTypeComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementsByType.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementsByType.py): Lists the walls of the project with GetElementsByType: all of them, then only the editable ones on the current story.

### GetAllElements

Returns the identifier of all elements on the plan. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Without databases it lists the current database: in a section or elevation window the model elements that the window shows (and its own 2D elements); pass the floor plan's database (GetDatabases) to list every model element.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAllElements

Parameters:

- `filters` (array of ElementFilter)
- `databases` (Databases)


Grasshopper: `ElementMetadata`, `GetAllElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetAllElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetAllElements.py): Lists every element of the project with GetAllElements, then only the ones visible in 3D.

### CaptureElementState

Captures the current state of the elements of the project and returns a stateId for it, so that GetElementChangesSince can later list what was created, modified and deleted since. The optional type selects how changes are detected (modification stamps by default, or the 3D model). The state is kept in a file in the temporary folder for the Archicad session only: it is lost when the project is closed or Archicad restarts, and ReleaseElementState frees it earlier.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CaptureElementState

Parameters:

- `type` (string ("ModificationStamp", "3DModel")): How GetElementChangesSince finds the changed elements between this state and another one. ModificationStamp (the default) compares the modification stamps of the elements, so any change to a tracked element counts. 3DModel compares the 3D model of the elements, so only a change that alters the 3D model counts, and capturing it generates the 3D model of the project. Two states can only be compared when they were captured with the same type. With either type the changes come from Archicad's element difference generator, which tracks the model elements: 2D elements such as texts, labels and hatches can be missing from the result even when they were created, modified or deleted.

Returns:

- `stateId` (object, required): The identifier of the captured state, accepted by GetElementChangesSince and ReleaseElementState. It is only valid in the Archicad session and project it was captured in.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `type` (string ("ModificationStamp", "3DModel"), required): The type the state was captured with.

Grasshopper: `CaptureElementStateComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CaptureElementState.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CaptureElementState.py): Captures the current state of the project's elements with CaptureElementState. GetElementChangesSince can compare a later state to it. The script releases the state at the end.

### GetElementChangesSince

Returns the new, modified and deleted elements between a state captured by CaptureElementState and either another captured state (toStateId) or the current state of the project. Scripts that keep an external copy of the model use it to sync only what changed instead of re-reading every element. The changes come from Archicad's element difference generator, which tracks the model elements: 2D elements such as texts, labels and hatches can be missing from the lists, so read those directly. Fails for a stateId that is unknown - never captured, released, or lost because the project was closed or Archicad restarted.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementChangesSince

Parameters:

- `stateId` (object, required): The state to compare from, as returned by CaptureElementState.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `toStateId` (object): The state to compare to, as returned by CaptureElementState with the same type as stateId. If omitted, the current state of the project is used, so the response lists what changed since stateId was captured.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)

Returns:

- `newElements` (Elements, required): The elements that exist in the later state but not in the earlier one.
- `modifiedElements` (Elements, required): The elements that exist in both states and changed between them.
- `deletedElements` (Elements, required): The elements that exist in the earlier state but not in the later one. They cannot be read any more, only their identifiers are known.

Grasshopper: `GetElementChangesSinceComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementChangesSince.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementChangesSince.py): Lists what changed since a captured state with GetElementChangesSince. Captures a state, creates a wall, reads the changes (the new wall), then deletes the wall and releases the state.

### ReleaseElementState

Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState. Every state is freed anyway when the project is closed or Archicad quits.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ReleaseElementState

Parameters:

- `stateId` (object, required): The state to free, as returned by CaptureElementState.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)


Grasshopper: `ReleaseElementStateComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ReleaseElementState.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ReleaseElementState.py): Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState with ReleaseElementState. States are freed anyway when the project is closed; releasing them earlier frees their temporary file.

### GetMarquee

Gets the marquee of the current window: its shape (rectangle, rotated rectangle or polygon), whether it is multi-story, and its outline as a polygon. Returns the type 'none' when there is no marquee.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetMarquee

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `type` (string ("none", "rectangle", "rotatedRectangle", "polygon"), required): The shape of the marquee in the current window, or 'none' when there is no marquee.
- `multiStory` (boolean): True for a multi-story (thick) marquee, false for a single-story (thin) one. Absent when there is no marquee.
- `box` (BoundingBox2D): The rectangle of a 'rectangle' or 'rotatedRectangle' marquee. For a rotated rectangle it is given as Archicad stores it: in the coordinate system rotated by rotationAngle around the project origin, not around the box itself. Use polygon for the corners on the plan.
- `rotationAngle` (number): The rotation angle (radians) of a 'rotatedRectangle' marquee.
- `polygon` (array of Coordinate2D): The vertices of the marquee outline on the plan, each listed once: the four corners of a 'rectangle' or 'rotatedRectangle' marquee, the vertices of a 'polygon' marquee.

Grasshopper: `GetMarqueeComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetMarquee.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetMarquee.py): Reads the marquee of the current window with GetMarquee: its shape, whether it is multi-story, and its outline. The type is 'none' when there is no marquee.

### SetMarquee

Draws a marquee in the current window from a polygon or a box (optionally rotated), single- or multi-story. Called without polygon and box it removes the marquee.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetMarquee

Parameters:

- `polygon` (array of Coordinate2D): The vertices of a polygon marquee, in order. The polygon is closed automatically; a repeated first vertex at the end is accepted. Give either polygon or box.
- `box` (BoundingBox2D): A rectangle marquee. With rotationAngle it is a rotated rectangle, and the box is read the way Archicad stores it (see GetMarquee): in the coordinate system rotated by rotationAngle around the project origin. Give either polygon or box.
- `rotationAngle` (number): Rotation angle (radians) of the box around the project origin. Only together with box. The default is 0: a horizontal rectangle.
- `multiStory` (boolean): True for a multi-story (thick) marquee, false for a single-story (thin) one. The default is false.


Grasshopper: `SetMarqueeComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetMarquee.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetMarquee.py): Draws a 10 x 10 m rectangle marquee around the origin with SetMarquee, then reads it back. The original marquee (or no marquee) is restored at the end.

### FilterElements

Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices), element type (elementTypes) and hotlink (fromHotlink, hotlinkIds). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#FilterElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `filters` (array of ElementFilter): Optional. Archicad's own flag filters. An element is kept only when it fulfills all of them.
- `layerIndices` (array of integer): Optional. An element is kept only when it is on one of these layers (the layerIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).
- `floorIndices` (array of integer): Optional. An element is kept only when its home story is one of these (the floorIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).
- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType): Optional. An element is kept only when its type is one of these.
- `fromHotlink` (boolean): Optional. true keeps only the elements that came in through a placed hotlink (they are read-only), false only the project's own elements.
- `hotlinkIds` (array of ElementId): Optional. An element is kept only when it came in through one of these placed hotlink instances (the hotlinkId field of GetDetailsOfElements, elements of type Hotlink).

Returns:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Grasshopper: `FilterElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/FilterElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/FilterElements.py): Keeps only the editable walls and slabs of all elements with FilterElements.

### GetElementsByCriteria

Returns the elements, or with countOnly only their number, that match all the given criteria: element types, home stories, layers, Archicad's element filter flags and property criteria (a value compared in internal units, or a value status such as hasValue, isUserUndefined, isNotAvailable, isDefault or hasCustomValue). An unknown type, property or operator is an error, not ignored. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. It searches the current database, as GetElementsByType does (in a section or elevation window the model elements the window shows), or the given databases.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByCriteria

Parameters:

- `types` (array of ElementType): Optional filter for element types (e.g. ['Wall', 'Column']).
- `floorIndices` (array of integer): Optional filter for story/floor indices (e.g. [0, 1]).
- `layerIndices` (array of integer): Optional filter for layer attribute indices.
- `filters` (array of ElementFilter): Optional Archicad API element filter flags. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs, railings and curtain walls) are left out unless IncludeSubElemObjects is given, as in GetElementsByType and GetAllElements.
- `propertyCriteria` (array of object): Optional list of property evaluation criteria. All criteria must match (AND condition).
  - `propertyId` (PropertyId)
  - `propertyName` (string): Case-insensitive property definition name, as shown in the project's language. An error is returned when it matches no property, or properties in more than one group and propertyGroupName is not given. Prefer propertyId in scripts that must work in any language.
  - `propertyGroupName` (string): Case-insensitive property group name, to choose between properties of the same name in different groups.
  - `operator` (string ("equals", "notEquals", "contains", "greaterThan", "lessThan", "greaterOrEqual", "lessOrEqual", "hasValue", "hasAnyValue", "isUndefined", "isUserUndefined", "isNotAvailable", ...)): Evaluation operator. Default is 'equals'. hasValue (alias hasAnyValue) matches a property with a value, isUserUndefined (alias isUndefined) one set to undefined by the user, isNotAvailable one that does not apply to the element. isDefault matches a property whose value comes from its default, hasCustomValue one whose value was set on the element (also to undefined). Archicad gives the default status only together with the evaluated value, so isDefault and hasCustomValue take as long as reading the value, also for expression properties.
  - `value` (string): Expected value as a string. Required for the comparison operators. For number, integer, length, area, volume and angle properties, equals, notEquals and the range operators compare numbers in internal units (m, m², m³, rad) written with a decimal point, independent of the project's display settings; other properties compare the displayed text, case-insensitively.
- `countOnly` (boolean): If true, only returns the count of matching elements without listing their GUIDs. Minimizes token usage.
- `limit` (integer): Maximum number of matching elements to list. The count is still the total number of matches.
- `databases` (Databases): Optional. The databases to search, as GetDatabases lists them; an element found in more than one is counted once. If omitted, the current database is searched: the floor plan, or in a section or elevation window the model elements it shows.

Returns:

- `count` (integer, required): Total number of matching elements.
- `elements` (Elements): List of matching elements.
- `executionResultForDatabases` (ExecutionResults): Only when databases is given: whether each database could be searched, in the order of databases.

Grasshopper: `GetElementsByCriteriaComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementsByCriteria.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementsByCriteria.py): Finds walls by story and by a property value with GetElementsByCriteria, first counting them only. The property criterion compares the wall thickness in metres, whatever the project's display units.

### GetDetailsOfElements

Gets the details of elements (geometry parameters etc). When elements is omitted, all elements matching the optional server-side filter (types, floorIndices, layerIndices) are queried; an empty elements list returns no details. Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need (e.g. elementId, type, id, floorIndex) and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). Use the optional additionalFields parameter to also get the info string, the compound info string, the library part unique ID and the creator tool unique ID. The components of a Railing (posts, inner posts, rails, top rails, handrails, balusters, baluster sets, panels, patterns, rail ends, rail connections and end finishes, as GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists them) return their owner, library part and settings. A Stair returns the structure settings of each part and side (structures, with the monolith or side stringer data of its type), and a StairStructure subelement returns the same keys. A Stair also returns its plan outline (its left and right boundary lines) and its walking lines. An element of another database (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index, layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDetailsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements): Optional list of elements to get details for. When omitted, all elements in the current database (optionally filtered by the filter parameter) are used; an empty list returns no details.
- `fields` (array of ElementDetailsField): Optional filter for the fields to return for each element. When omitted, every field is returned. Fields not listed are not computed at all, so listing only what you need skips in particular the floorPlanPolygons extraction, which regenerates each element's 2D drawing primitives and can dominate the execution time of batch reads.
- `filter` (ElementTypeFloorLayerFilter): Optional server-side filter. Without elements, only the elements matching it are returned. A listed element that does not match it gets an error entry in its place.
- `additionalFields` (array of ElementDetailsAdditionalField): Optional extra fields to return for each element, on top of the ones selected by fields. None of them is returned unless listed here, so callers that do not give this parameter get the same response as before.

Returns:

- `detailsOfElements` (array of DetailsOfElement or ElementHeaderFromOtherDatabase or ErrorItem, required): One entry per input element, in the same order as the input elements array. An element that cannot be read, or that does not match the filter, gets an error entry in its place, so the position of an entry tells which input element it belongs to. Without elements, one entry per element that matches the filter.

### SetDetailsOfElements

Sets the details of the given elements. Every element type: Element ID (id), story (floorIndex), layer (layerIndex) and display order (drawIndex). In typeSpecificDetails: Wall - start and end point, height, base offset, and the start and end thickness of a trapezoid wall; Zone - the ZoneSettings fields (the same as ModifyZones); Line - start and end point, pen, line type, room separator; Arc and Circle - origin, radius, angle, ratio, start and end angle (arcs only), reflected, pen, line type, room separator; Polyline - points and arcs, pen, line type, room separator; Spline - pen, line type, room separator; Hatch - outline, holes, contour pen, fill pen and background pen or colors, fill or building material, area display, room special, fill orientation, fill category and contour line type; Hotspot - position, height, pen; Text - text, position, angle, height, justification; Label - the text of a text label; Drawing - position, angle, ratio, model offset, clip polygon (isCutWithFrame), name, ID and numbering, scale in Autotext, border, title library part, pen table (penTableUsageMode, penTableIndex), colorMode, isTransparentBackground, rasterizeDPI and the anchor (anchorPoint, useOwnOriginAsAnchor). Not written, because the Archicad API does not take them: the geometry of a Spline, the source of a Drawing (use ChangeDrawingLink), the Drawing Manager's update type and stored in project, and often a placed Drawing's drawingScale, which comes from its source view (the element's result then names the kept value). Other wall, slab, column, beam, stair and object settings are written by their Modify commands, and the name, ID and clip polygon of Detail and Worksheet markers by ModifyDetailMarkers: typeSpecificDetails given for a Detail or Worksheet marker fail the item, and nothing of it is changed. An element Archicad does not let you edit (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not reserved by you in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason; a Drawing setting Archicad kept unchanged is named in a failed execution result too.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetDetailsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementsWithDetails` (array of object, required): The elements with parameters.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `details` (object, required): Details of an element.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Needs at least one editable Wall. The keys of typeSpecificDetails depend on the element type, for example a Drawing takes {'penTableUsageMode': 'ModelPenTable', 'colorMode': 'Grayscale', 'isTransparentBackground': True, 'anchorPoint': 'BottomLeft'}; the command's description lists them for every type. GetDetailsOfElements returns the same keys.

### GetCategoryValuesOfElements

Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, optionally only for the given category types. An element that has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCategoryValuesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `categories` (array of ElementCategoryType): The categories to read. Left out: every category the element has.

Returns:

- `categoryValuesOfElements` (array of ElementCategoryValues or ErrorItem, required): The category values of each element, in the order of the input. A category the element does not have is left out of its list; an element that does not exist or has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) is represented by an error object.

Grasshopper: `GetCategoryValuesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCategoryValuesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCategoryValuesOfElements.py): Reads the Structural Function and Position of the first walls with GetCategoryValuesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. Without categories every category of the elements is returned.

### GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults

Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the tool defaults of the given element types, the values new elements of the type get, optionally only for the given category types. A category the default has no value in is listed without categoryValueId; an element type without any of the requested categories gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults

Parameters:

- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType, required): The element types whose tool defaults (the settings new elements get) are read.
- `categories` (array of ElementCategoryType): The categories to read. Left out: every category of the project.

Returns:

- `categoryValuesOfDefaults` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The category values of the tool defaults of each element type, in the order of the input. A category Archicad cannot read for the type is left out of its list; an invalid element type, or one with none of the requested categories, is represented by an error object.

Grasshopper: `GetCategoryValuesOfDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults.py): Reads the category values new walls, slabs and columns get from their tool defaults, with GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults.

### SetCategoryValuesOfDefaults

Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the tool defaults of the given element types: the values new elements of the type get, as the Renovation palette does for the Renovation Status. Every given category value is set for every given element type, in a single undoable step, and read back. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them. The executionResults have one item per element type and category value: for each element type, in the order of the input, one per item of categoryValues, in their order. An element type without that category, or a value Archicad did not keep, gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the default's value in the category now (oldValue) and the value a real run would set (newValue).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetCategoryValuesOfDefaults

Parameters:

- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType, required): The element types whose tool defaults (the settings new elements get) are set.
- `categoryValues` (array of object, required): The category values to set for every element type: one category per item.
  - `type` (ElementCategoryType, required)
  - `categoryValueId` (ElementCategoryValueId, required): A value of the category given by type, as GetElementCategories lists them.
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)
- `executionResults` (ChangeExecutionResults, required): One result per element type and category value: for each element type, in the order of the input, one result per item of categoryValues, in their order. A real run reads each value back after setting it, and a value Archicad did not keep gets a failed execution result. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the element type is valid, the category and the value exist, and the tool defaults of the type have the category) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the default's value in the category now and newValue the value a real run would set, both as GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults gives them (type, categoryId, categoryValueId and name; oldValue has only type and categoryId when the default has no value in the category). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetCategoryValuesOfDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetCategoryValuesOfDefaults.py): Sets the Renovation Status new walls, slabs and windows get, like the Renovation palette, with SetCategoryValuesOfDefaults, reads it back, then restores it. A dry run first shows what would change. The values are identified by their categoryValueId, never by their localized names.

### SetCategoryValuesOfElements

Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, one element and one category per item, in a single undoable step. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them; an element without that category gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's value in the category now (oldValue) and the value a real run would set (newValue).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetCategoryValuesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementCategoryValues` (array of ElementCategoryValueData, required): The category values to set: one element and one category per item. The same element can appear in several items, one per category.
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)
- `executionResults` (ChangeExecutionResults, required): One result per item of the input, in the same order. On a dry run an item that passes every check made before writing (the category and the value exist, the element exists and has the category) gets wouldChange: oldValue is the element's value in the category now and newValue the value a real run would set, both as GetCategoryValuesOfElements gives them (type, categoryId, categoryValueId and name; oldValue has only type and categoryId when the element has no value in the category). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them.

Grasshopper: `SetCategoryValuesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetCategoryValuesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetCategoryValuesOfElements.py): Changes the Structural Function of a wall with SetCategoryValuesOfElements, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Wall.

### Get3DBoundingBoxes

Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements. An element without 3D geometry of its own gets an error item instead of a bounding box. Walls, Slabs, Roofs, Zones and Stairs are measured on their 3D model, so the box of a Wall includes its connections to other walls. The current window does not need to show the element: it works with a layout or a section open as well.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DBoundingBoxes

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `boundingBoxes3D` (BoundingBoxes3D, required)

Grasshopper: `Get3DBoundingBoxesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get3DBoundingBoxes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get3DBoundingBoxes.py): Reads the 3D bounding boxes of the first walls with Get3DBoundingBoxes. Needs at least one Wall.

### Get2DBoundingBoxes

Get the 2D bounding box of elements as Archicad draws them, in the coordinates of the database the element is in: the floor plan, a section, a worksheet, a layout or a master layout. Works for 2D elements (Line, PolyLine, Arc, Hatch, Text, Label, Dimension, Drawing ...) as well as for model elements; a Text's box covers its drawn lines, a Drawing's box its frame with the title. The current window does not need to show the element. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get2DBoundingBoxes

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `boundingBoxes2D` (BoundingBoxes2D, required)

Grasshopper: `Get2DBoundingBoxesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get2DBoundingBoxes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get2DBoundingBoxes.py): Reads the 2D bounding boxes of the first walls, as Archicad draws them on the floor plan, with Get2DBoundingBoxes. Needs at least one Wall.

### GetLibPartTransformations

Gets the placement transformation of library part instances (Window, Door, Object, Lamp, Zone) as Archicad computes it: the location, the rotation angle and the x/y scaling. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetLibPartTransformations

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `transformations` (array of ElementLibraryPartTransformation or ErrorItem, required): The placement transformation of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetLibPartTransformationsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetLibPartTransformations.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetLibPartTransformations.py): Reads the location, rotation angle and scaling of the first placed objects, windows and doors with GetLibPartTransformations. Needs at least one Object, Window or Door.

### GetSnapPointsOfElements

Gets the snap points (hotspots) of the given elements, of any element type: the points of an element that the cursor snaps to and dimensions attach to (for example the endpoints of a Wall's reference line or the vertices of a Slab), in world coordinates, each with the neig kind and subindex identifying which point of the element it is. For the 2D hotspots of library part instances see GetHotspotsOfElements. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSnapPointsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `snapPointsOfElements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The snap points (hotspots) of each element, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetSnapPointsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSnapPointsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSnapPointsOfElements.py): Reads the snap points (hotspots) of a wall with GetSnapPointsOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.

### ConvertRevealOffsets

Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ConvertRevealOffsets

Parameters:

- `openings` (array of OpeningRevealOffsetData, required): Windows and doors placed in walls, each with exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset.

Returns:

- `revealOffsets` (array of OpeningRevealOffsets or ErrorItem, required): The reveal depth offset of each opening in both references, aligned with the input, or an error.

Grasshopper: `ConvertRevealOffsetsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ConvertRevealOffsets.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ConvertRevealOffsets.py): Converts a reveal depth offset of 0 measured from the wall's core skin to the wall side reference with ConvertRevealOffsets. Needs at least one Window or Door placed in a wall. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### Get3DGeometryOfElements

Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DGeometryOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `geometries3D` (array of ElementGeometry3D or ErrorItem, required): The 3D geometry of each element, aligned with the input: the solid bodies of its 3D model, or an error.

Grasshopper: `Get3DGeometryOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get3DGeometryOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get3DGeometryOfElements.py): Reads the 3D geometry (vertices and faces of the solid bodies) of a wall with Get3DGeometryOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.

### GetElementConnections

Gets the connections among the given elements: each pair of touching elements once, with the polygons of the surface where they touch, in world coordinates. The 3D model of the elements is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. Also returns, aligned with the input array of elements, whether each element was found. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementConnections

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to search connections among. Only connections between two of these elements are returned.

Returns:

- `connections` (array of object, required): The connected pairs of the given elements. Each pair appears once.
  - `elementId1` (ElementId, required)
  - `elementId2` (ElementId, required)
  - `polygons` (array of object, required): The polygons of the surface where the two elements touch, in world coordinates. The last point of a polygon repeats its first.
- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): Aligned with the input array of elements: whether the element was found and taken into the search.

Grasshopper: `GetElementConnectionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementConnections.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementConnections.py): Finds where the walls and slabs of the project touch each other with GetElementConnections. Needs Walls or Slabs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetBodyMaterialsOfElements

Gets the building material of each body of the 3D model of the given elements. The 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetBodyMaterialsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `bodyMaterials` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The bodies of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetBodyMaterialsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetBodyMaterialsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetBodyMaterialsOfElements.py): Reads the building material of each body of the 3D model of the first walls with GetBodyMaterialsOfElements. A composite wall has one body per skin. Needs at least one Wall. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### GetCutPolygonsOfElements

Cuts each body of the 3D model of the given elements with a plane and returns, for each body, its building material, the area of the cut surface and its polygons (outline and holes) in 2D coordinates of the plane. From Archicad 28 the 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. Before Archicad 28 the bodies are those of the element's 3D model (a composite structure is one body) and their building materials are left out. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCutPolygonsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `cutPlane` (object, required): The cutting plane. axisX, axisY and axisZ should be unit vectors perpendicular to each other; axisZ is the normal of the plane.
  - `basePoint` (Coordinate3D, required): A point of the plane, the origin of the returned 2D coordinates.
  - `axisX` (Coordinate3D, required): The direction of the x axis of the returned 2D coordinates.
  - `axisY` (Coordinate3D, required): The direction of the y axis of the returned 2D coordinates.
  - `axisZ` (Coordinate3D, required): The normal of the plane.

Returns:

- `cutPolygons` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The cut of each body of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetCutPolygonsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCutPolygonsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCutPolygonsOfElements.py): Cuts the first walls with a horizontal plane 1 m above project zero with GetCutPolygonsOfElements. Returns the building material, cut area and cut polygons of each body. Needs at least one Wall. On Archicad 25-27 the building materials are left out.

### GetElementAtCoordinate

Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementAtCoordinate

Parameters:

- `elementType` (ElementType, required): The type of the element to look for. Only polygonal element types can be searched, for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch.
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D, required): The point to search at, in the project's coordinates, on the floor plan of the current database.
- `z` (number): Optional. The elevation of the search point, handed to Archicad together with the coordinate. Archicad finds the highest element whose top is below z. Default is 0; without z a point 1 mm higher is also tried, so an element whose top is at 0 (for example a slab at the story level) is found, and then the topmost element on the active story, so an element whose top is above the story level is found too, like a click on the floor plan.
- `filters` (array of ElementFilter): Optional. Only an element passing every given filter is found (the same values as FilterElements accepts).

Returns:

- `found` (boolean, required): True when an element of the given type was found at the coordinate.
- `elementId` (ElementId): The identifier of the found element. Absent when nothing was found.

Grasshopper: `GetElementAtCoordinateComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementAtCoordinate.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementAtCoordinate.py): Finds the Slab at a point of the floor plan, the way a click there would, with GetElementAtCoordinate. The point is the average of the first slab's outline vertices. Needs at least one Slab.

Returns:

- `skylightHolePolygons` (array of SkylightHolePolygon or ErrorItem, required): The hole each Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell, aligned with the input: its polygon, or an error (for example for an element that is not a Skylight).

Grasshopper: `GetSkylightHolePolygonsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSkylightHolePolygons.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSkylightHolePolygons.py): Reads the hole each Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell with GetSkylightHolePolygons. Needs at least one Skylight.

Checks whether elements have a visible skin in a given Partial Structure Display mode (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly), e.g. a finish-only slab has none in CoreOnly. The current window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `structureDisplay` (string ("EntireStructure", "CoreOnly", "WithoutFinishes", "StructureOnly"), required): The Partial Structure Display mode to check the elements in. The current window is not changed.

Returns:

- `visibleSkinStatuses` (array of VisibleSkinStatus or ErrorItem, required): Whether each element has a visible skin in the given Partial Structure Display mode, aligned with the input, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetVisibleSkinStatusComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetVisibleSkinStatus.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetVisibleSkinStatus.py): Checks which slabs still show a skin in the Core Only Partial Structure Display mode with GetVisibleSkinStatus. The current window is not changed. Needs at least one Slab.

### GetRoofPlanes

Gets the single planes of roofs, without changing the roofs. A multi-plane roof is decomposed by Archicad into its planes, each returned with its part identifier and its details as a single-plane roof (slope, pivot line, level, outline with arcs and holes); a single-plane roof is returned as its only plane. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetRoofPlanes

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `roofPlanesOfElements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The planes of each roof, aligned with the input, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetRoofPlanesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetRoofPlanes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetRoofPlanes.py): Reads the single planes of the first roofs with GetRoofPlanes; a multi-plane roof comes back plane by plane. Needs at least one Roof.

### GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottoms

Gets the absolute bottom level of curtain walls or their subelements (segments, frames, panels, junctions, accessories). The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottoms

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `absoluteBottoms` (array of CurtainWallAbsoluteBottom or ErrorItem, required): The absolute bottom of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottomsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottoms.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottoms.py): Reads the absolute bottom level of the curtain walls of the project with GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottoms. Needs at least one Curtain Wall. Its subelements (panels, frames ...) are accepted too.

### GetQuantitiesOfElements

Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment, Stair. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate the elements of each type in one Archicad call.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetQuantitiesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `minOpeningSize` (number): Optional minimum opening size in square meters. Openings smaller than this are not subtracted from the conditional surfaces of a Wall (referenceSideSurfaceConditional and oppositeSideSurfaceConditional). Archicad only uses it for walls; the conditional volume follows the project's calculation rules instead. Default value is 0, so every opening is subtracted.
- `calculateInOneCall` (boolean): Optional. When true, Archicad calculates the quantities of all the supported elements of one type in one call (one call per element type, because Archicad only calculates elements of the same type together) instead of one call per element, which can be faster for many elements. The output has the same format. If the call of a type fails, every element of that type gets the same error. Default value is false.

Returns:

- `quantitiesOfElements` (array of ElementQuantityDetails or ErrorItem, required): The quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Lengths are in meters, areas in square meters and volumes in cubic meters.

Grasshopper: `GetQuantitiesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetQuantitiesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetQuantitiesOfElements.py): Reads the quantities Archicad calculates (volumes, surfaces, lengths ...) of the first walls with GetQuantitiesOfElements. Openings smaller than 0.5 m2 are not subtracted. Needs at least one Wall.

### TriangulatePolygonsOfElements

Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. With convex: true, the faces of the 3D model of the elements (of any type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, given by the 3D coordinates of their vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#TriangulatePolygonsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `convex` (boolean): Optional. When true, the faces of the 3D model of each element (its own bodies, any element type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, as Archicad does it, and returned as convexPolygons. Default value is false.

Returns:

- `triangulations` (array of ElementTriangulation or ElementConvexPolygons or ErrorItem, required): The triangulation of the polygon of each element, aligned with the input: its triangles (or with convex: true its convex polygons), or an error (for example for an element type that has no polygon).

Grasshopper: `TriangulatePolygonsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/TriangulatePolygonsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/TriangulatePolygonsOfElements.py): Triangulates the plan polygon of the first slabs with TriangulatePolygonsOfElements. Needs at least one Slab.

### GetTextureCoordinates

Gets the texture coordinates (u, v) of the faces of the 3D model of the given elements: per solid body, per face, at the first vertex of the face. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `textureCoordinates` (array of ElementTextureCoordinates or ErrorItem, required): The texture coordinates of each element, aligned with the input: per solid body of its 3D model, or an error.

Needs at least one Wall.

### GetSurfaceTypesOfElements

Gets the surface type of every polygon of the 3D model of the given elements, as ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType returns it: for each element its polygons with their body index, polygon index, polygon id and the numeric API_SurfaceTypeID value. The model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28.

Needs at least one Wall. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

### Get3DModelCounts

Gets the number of components of each type (bodies, polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices, normal vectors, materials and lights) in the 3D model Archicad currently holds. Bodies, materials and lights are counted with ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetNum; the polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices and normal vectors, which that function refuses to count, are summed over the bodies. A type that cannot be counted gets an error item. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DModelCounts

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `counts` (array of Model3DCount or ErrorItem, required): The number of components of each type in the 3D model Archicad currently holds, one item per type, or an error for a type that could not be counted.

Grasshopper: `Get3DModelCountsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get3DModelCounts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/Get3DModelCounts.py): Prints how many bodies, polygons, edges, vertices etc. the current 3D model has, with Get3DModelCounts. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### DeleteUserDataOfElements

Deletes the user data this add-on stored on the given elements. Archicad keeps the user data of an element per add-on, so the data of other add-ons is left as it is. All deletions are one undo step. The output has one execution result per element, aligned with the input array of elements. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that exists gets wouldDelete.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteUserDataOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)
- `executionResults` (DeletionExecutionResults, required): One result per element, aligned with the input. On a dry run an element that exists gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse to delete its user data.

Grasshopper: `DeleteUserDataOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteUserDataOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteUserDataOfElements.py): Deletes the user data the Tapir Add-On stored on a wall with DeleteUserDataOfElements. The user data of other add-ons is kept. Needs at least one Wall.

### GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements

Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to get the surface quantities of.
- `coverElements` (Elements): Optional covering elements: the area where one of them overlaps a surface of an element is subtracted from that surface, so for example a slab on a wall takes its footprint off the top surface of the wall. When omitted, every Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Stair and Curtain Wall of the project is a covering element. Pass an empty array to get the whole surfaces with nothing subtracted. An element never covers itself.

Returns:

- `surfaceQuantitiesOfElements` (array of ElementSurfaceQuantities or ErrorItem, required): The surface quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Areas are in square meters.

Grasshopper: `GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements.py): Reads the exposed surface areas of the first walls, with the slabs as covering elements, with GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. Without coverElements every construction element covers the surfaces.

Gets the owner of each given element in its hierarchical element: the root (e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing of a frame, tread or post) or the immediate parent. Also returns whether the given element is a main element, a subelement or not part of a hierarchical element.

### GetElementFieldDefinitions

Lists every field of an element type's struct in the Archicad API (e.g. API_AngleDimensionType) that GetElementFields reads and SetElementFields writes (and GetFieldsOfElementDefaults and SetFieldsOfElementDefaults in the tool defaults): its path, JSON type, C++ kind, size and whether it is read-only. The list is generated from the Archicad 29 and 30 DevKit headers; other Archicad versions answer that it is not available.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementFieldDefinitions

Parameters:

- `elementType` (ElementType, required): The element type whose fields are listed.

Returns:

- `structName` (string, required): The C++ struct of the element type in the Archicad API, e.g. API_AngleDimensionType.
- `fields` (array of object, required): Every field GetElementFields reads and SetElementFields writes for this element type.
  - `path` (string, required): The field's path in the struct, as in C++: e.g. note.noteFont, u.planeRoof.angle or defHandrailEnd[0].x.
  - `type` (string ("number", "boolean", "integer", "string", "object"), required): The JSON type of the field's value: object for an OverriddenPen or OverriddenAttribute (see ElementFieldOptionalValue).
  - `kind` (string ("Real", "Bool", "SignedInt", "UnsignedInt", "CString", "UString", "AttributeIndex", "Guid", "OverriddenPen", "OverriddenAttribute", "UniStringPointer"), required): The C++ kind of the field: an enum is a SignedInt, an AttributeIndex is the index of an attribute (pen tables excepted, pens are plain integers). OverriddenPen and OverriddenAttribute are the optional pens and attributes of the API (API_OverriddenPen, API_OverriddenAttribute, e.g. cutFillPen and refMat of a wall), read and written as an object with hasValue and value. A UniStringPointer is a GS::UniString* through which Archicad passes a text (e.g. note.contentUStr, the text of a dimension note): it is read and written as a string, the commands pointing it to a string of their own.
  - `size` (integer, required): The size of the field in bytes (for a string, the room in bytes including the closing zero; for a UniStringPointer, the size of the pointer).
  - `readOnly` (boolean, required): True for the owners and counts that Archicad computes, and for the fields that choose the shape of an element (a roof's roofClass, a shell's shellClass, a label's labelClass, a stair structure's structType, also in the default structures of a stair such as structure[0][0].structType, a wall's type: changing one without the data of the other shape made Archicad 29 quit): SetElementFields refuses them.
  - `variant` (string): For a field in a union, the member it is in, e.g. u.revolvedShell, u.planeRoof or structure[0][1].data.monolith. Only the member the element uses holds values (a roof's roofClass, a shell's shellClass, a label's labelClass, a stair structure's structType, the structType of that default structure of a stair): GetElementFields leaves the others out and SetElementFields refuses them.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementFieldDefinitions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementFieldDefinitions.py): Lists the fields GetElementFields and SetElementFields know for angle dimensions, with their types. Needs nothing in the project.

### GetElementFields

Reads fields of elements by their path in the element's struct in the Archicad API (e.g. note.noteFont of an angle dimension, u.planeRoof.angle of a roof): every field, or only the given ones. Reaches the settings the other commands do not return.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementFields

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `fields` (array of string): The paths of the fields to read (see GetElementFieldDefinitions), e.g. ["note.noteFont", "note.frame"]. Every field of the element is read when it is left out. A path the element type does not have is listed in the element's missingFields.

Returns:

- `elementFields` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The fields of each element, aligned with the input.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementFields.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementFields.py): Reads the text settings of the first angle dimension with GetElementFields. Needs at least one Angle Dimension.

### SetElementFields

Writes fields of elements by their path in the element's struct in the Archicad API (see GetElementFieldDefinitions), with ACAPI_Element_Change and a mask of exactly the given fields, in one undoable command. Each value is read back afterwards: one Archicad did not keep is reported as a failure that names the field and the value Archicad kept.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetElementFields

Parameters:

- `elementsWithFields` (array of object, required): The elements to change and the fields to write to each.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `fields` (object, required): The new value of each field, by its path (see GetElementFieldDefinitions), e.g. {"note.noteFont": 3, "note.frame": true, "note.contentUStr": "A"}, or {"refMat": {"hasValue": true, "value": 12}} for a wall. Only these fields change: they are written with ACAPI_Element_Change and a mask of exactly their bytes, then read back.
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per element, aligned with the input. An element whose fields Archicad did not all keep fails with the fields and the values Archicad kept; the other fields of that element are changed. On a dry run, a successful result has wouldChange with the oldValue and newValue of the given fields.
- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetElementFields.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetElementFields.py): Frames the text of the first angle dimension and gives it an opaque background with SetElementFields. Needs at least one Angle Dimension.

### GetFieldsOfElementDefaults

Reads fields of the tool defaults of element types, the settings new elements of the type get, by their path in the element's struct in the Archicad API (see GetElementFieldDefinitions), e.g. thickness of the wall defaults: every field, or only the given ones. Reaches the default settings the other commands do not return. The list is generated from the Archicad 29 and 30 DevKit headers; other Archicad versions answer that it is not available.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetFieldsOfElementDefaults

Parameters:

- `elementTypes` (array of ElementType, required): The element types whose tool defaults are read.
- `fields` (array of string): The paths of the fields to read (see GetElementFieldDefinitions), e.g. ["thickness", "height"]. Every field of the defaults is read when it is left out. A path the element type does not have is listed in missingFields.

Returns:

- `fieldsOfElementDefaults` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The fields of the tool defaults of each element type, in the input order, or an error when the type has no fields in the table or no tool defaults.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetFieldsOfElementDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetFieldsOfElementDefaults.py): Reads the thickness, height and pen of the Wall and Slab tool defaults with GetFieldsOfElementDefaults.

### SetFieldsOfElementDefaults

Writes fields of the tool defaults of element types by their path in the element's struct in the Archicad API (see GetElementFieldDefinitions), with ACAPI_Element_ChangeDefaults and a mask of exactly the given fields: the elements created afterwards get them. Like the settings dialogs of the tools, it is not undoable. Each value is read back afterwards: one Archicad did not keep is reported as a failure that names the field and the value Archicad kept. A change Archicad refuses can still have written some of the given fields (seen with libInd, the library part, which Archicad refuses in the tool defaults): the failure names them.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetFieldsOfElementDefaults

Parameters:

- `fieldsOfElementDefaults` (array of object, required): The element types whose tool defaults change and the fields to write to each.
  - `elementType` (ElementType, required)
  - `fields` (object, required): The new value of each field, by its path (see GetElementFieldDefinitions), e.g. {"thickness": 0.25, "height": 2.7, "cutFillPen": {"hasValue": true, "value": 5}}. Only these fields change: they are written with ACAPI_Element_ChangeDefaults and a mask of exactly their bytes, then read back.
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per item, in the input order. Tool defaults whose fields Archicad did not all keep fail with the fields and the values Archicad kept; the other fields are changed. On a dry run, a successful result has wouldChange with the oldValue and newValue of the given fields.
- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetFieldsOfElementDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetFieldsOfElementDefaults.py): Gives the Wall tool defaults pen 5 for the contour with SetFieldsOfElementDefaults, then puts the old pen back. The walls created in between get pen 5.

### EditHierarchicalElement

Opens the given hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) in its hierarchical 3D editing mode, as the Edit button of the element does. Fails when Archicad is already in an editing mode. Limitation: while the editing mode is open, Archicad refuses every JSON command, this add-on's included, with error 4001 (ongoing user input), FinishHierarchicalEditing included, so the mode can only be left in Archicad, with the button of its edit mode palette (reported for Archicad 29). Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#EditHierarchicalElement

Parameters:

- `elementId` (ElementId, required): The hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) to open in hierarchical editing mode.


Grasshopper: `EditHierarchicalElementComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/EditHierarchicalElement.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/EditHierarchicalElement.py): Opens a curtain wall in its hierarchical editing mode with EditHierarchicalElement. While the mode is open, Archicad refuses every JSON command with error 4001 (ongoing user input), so the script cannot leave it: leave it yourself in Archicad, with the button of the edit mode palette. Needs at least one Curtain Wall. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### FinishHierarchicalEditing

Finishes the current hierarchical editing mode (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column): accept true keeps the changes (OK), accept false discards them (Cancel). The accept parameter is required, so changes are never discarded silently. Fails when Archicad is not in such an editing mode. Limitation: while an editing mode is open, Archicad refuses JSON commands with error 4001 (ongoing user input) before they run, so this command cannot leave a mode opened by EditHierarchicalElement or in Archicad (reported for Archicad 29); leave it in Archicad instead. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#FinishHierarchicalEditing

Parameters:

- `accept` (boolean, required): True to accept the changes made in the hierarchical editing mode (OK), false to discard them (Cancel).


Grasshopper: `FinishHierarchicalEditingComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/FinishHierarchicalEditing.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/FinishHierarchicalEditing.py): Tries to leave a hierarchical editing mode with FinishHierarchicalEditing, discarding the changes (Cancel). accept True would keep the changes (OK). Limitation: while an editing mode is open, Archicad refuses JSON commands with error 4001 (ongoing user input) before they run, so this call is refused then; leave the mode in Archicad, with the button of the edit mode palette. When no editing mode is open, it fails with "not in a hierarchical editing mode". Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### GetConnectedElements

Gets the elements hosted by (connected to) the given owner elements, filtered to the given element type: for example the Windows or Doors of a Wall, the frames, panels, junctions and accessories of a Curtain Wall, the risers, treads and structures of a Stair, or the posts, rails and panels of a Railing.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetConnectedElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The owner (host) elements whose connected elements are collected, e.g. Walls, Curtain Walls, Stairs or Railings.
- `connectedElementType` (ElementType, required): The type of the connected elements to collect, e.g. Window or Door for a Wall owner, or a subelement type of a Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing owner.


Grasshopper: `GetConnectedElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetConnectedElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetConnectedElements.py): Lists the windows placed in the first walls with GetConnectedElements. Needs at least one Wall.

### GetElementsInDrawOrder

Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in Archicad's drawing order (the order set by Bring to Front and Send to Back), as ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext walks it. Use the optional elementType and filters parameters for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Items of the drawing order whose element Archicad cannot read are left out too, so every returned identifier can be used with the other commands.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsInDrawOrder

Parameters:

- `elementType` (ElementType): Optional. Only elements of this type are returned, still in drawing order. If omitted, every element is returned.
- `filters` (array of ElementFilter): Optional. The filters an element must pass to be returned, the same as for GetElementsByType.
- `databases` (Databases): The databases to list the elements of, each in its own drawing order. If omitted, the current database is used.


Grasshopper: `GetElementsInDrawOrderComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementsInDrawOrder.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetElementsInDrawOrder.py): Lists the fills of the current database in Archicad's drawing order (Bring to Front / Send to Back) with GetElementsInDrawOrder.

### GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements

Returns the 2D drawing primitives (points, lines, arcs, texts, polylines, triangles, polygons, pictures) Archicad draws each given floor plan element from, in drawing order, as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrimsExt decomposes it on every story and unclipped. Control items (type Ctrl_*) mark the beginning and the end of sub-parts such as hatches and texts. Texts are returned with their content, the text as Archicad displays it (for example the lines of a zone stamp with their values filled in), which each element's texts list also collects in drawing order; polylines are returned without their vertices. A Ctrl_ElementRef item names the element it refers to: the drawing of a Wall ends with one for each Window and Door in it, while Windows and Doors give no primitives of their own. The floor plan must be the current database. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `drawingPrimitivesOfElements` (array of ElementDrawingPrimitives or ErrorItem, required): The drawing primitives of each element, in the order of the input elements.

### LinkElements

Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#LinkElements

Parameters:

- `links` (array of ElementLinkData, required): The links to create, each from one element to another.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result per link, aligned with the input.

Grasshopper: `LinkElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/LinkElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/LinkElements.py): Links the first wall to the second one with LinkElements, reads the link back, then removes it. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way. Needs at least two Walls.

### UpdateZones

Updates Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements): the selected Zones, every Zone when nothing is selected, or the Zones given in zones. Archicad runs the update right after the command has returned, on the Zones selected at that moment, so the new geometry can only be read with a later command.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.4. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#UpdateZones

Parameters:

- `keepStampPosition` (boolean): Keep the position of the Zone Stamps. The default is true.
- `undoTopTrim` (boolean): Undo the trimming of the top of the Zones. The default is false.
- `undoBottomTrim` (boolean): Undo the trimming of the bottom of the Zones. The default is false.
- `zones` (Elements): Optional list of the Zones to update, on any story. They are selected instead of the current selection and stay selected: Archicad updates the selected Zones right after the command has returned, not during it, and clears the selection when it is done. So do not change the selection until then, and read the new geometry with a later command. Every Zone is checked first; if one cannot be updated (not a Zone, listed twice, hidden or locked layer, not editable), nothing is selected or updated. An empty list updates nothing. Without the list the current selection is updated, or every Zone when nothing is selected.


Grasshopper: `UpdateZonesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/UpdateZones.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/UpdateZones.py): Updates the first zone of the project (geometry, Zone Stamp and connected elements) with UpdateZones. Changes the zone, as Design > Update Zones does. Archicad updates it right after the command has returned and clears the selection.
