### AlignElements

Aligns elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view to one edge of their plan bounding boxes (left, right, top or bottom) or to their middle (centerX, centerY), either of the whole set or of a reference element, by moving them in one undo step. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still aligned.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#AlignElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to align: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text or Hotspot, in the current database.
- `alignTo` (string ("left", "right", "top", "bottom", "centerX", "centerY"), required): The edge of the plan bounding boxes to align: left (smallest X), right (largest X), bottom (smallest Y), top (largest Y), centerX (the middle in X, so the elements line up on one vertical line) or centerY (the middle in Y, on one horizontal line).
- `reference` (ElementId): Optional element to align to; it is not moved itself. Without it the elements are aligned to the outermost edge of the whole set (its leftmost left edge, its topmost top edge, ...), or for centerX and centerY to the middle of the bounding box of the whole set.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `AlignElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/AlignElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/AlignElements.py): Aligns the left edges of three walls with AlignElements, prints their bounding boxes, then moves them back. Needs at least two editable Walls on the floor plan.

### DistributeElements

Distributes 3 or more elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view evenly along X (horizontal) or Y (vertical), with equal distances between the middles of their plan bounding boxes (centers) or equal space between the boxes (gaps), by moving them in one undo step. The elements are taken in the order of their middles along the direction, and the two outermost stay where they are. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still distributed.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DistributeElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): At least 3 elements to distribute: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text or Hotspot, in the current database. Their order does not matter: they are distributed in the order of the middles of their plan bounding boxes along the direction.
- `direction` (string ("horizontal", "vertical"), required): horizontal distributes the elements along X, vertical along Y. They are not moved in the other direction.
- `mode` (string ("centers", "gaps"), required): centers makes the distances between the middles of the plan bounding boxes equal, gaps makes the empty space between neighbouring bounding boxes equal (the gap is negative, so the boxes overlap, when the elements are wider together than the space between the two outermost elements).

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DistributeElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DistributeElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DistributeElements.py): Distributes up to five walls along X with equal gaps using DistributeElements, prints their new left edges, then moves them back. Needs at least three editable Walls on the floor plan.

### SplitElements

Splits each given element along a line (the infinite line through its begin and end point, like Archicad's Split command). The original element keeps one part, copies of it (Drag a Copy, so they keep the layer, classifications, properties and every other setting) get the others; all are returned, the original first. Supports straight walls without doors, windows or openings, straight unslanted single segment beams without holes or openings, and lines (their arrows stay at the original ends), which are split in two, the original keeping the part from its begin point; and slabs, meshes without level lines or points, fills and single contour polylines, whose polygon (holes and arcs included) or points are cut along the line into one part per piece, the original keeping the largest piece (a polyline: the piece with its begin point). Slab edges keep their trim and side surface, the edges along the line are vertical; the corners a mesh gets on the line take their height from the edge they lie on. An element the line does not cross is reported as notCut, an unsupported one as an error naming its type. One undo step.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SplitElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to split. Supported: straight walls (not polygonal, without doors, windows or openings), straight beams (not slanted or curved, one segment, without holes or openings), lines, slabs, meshes (without level lines or points), fills and polylines (one contour). Other types are reported with their type name.
- `line` (object, required): The split line in project coordinates: the infinite line through begin and end, as the split line of Archicad's Split command.
  - `begin` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `end` (Coordinate2D, required)

Returns:

- `results` (array of object or object or ErrorItem, required): One item per given element, in the same order.

Grasshopper: `SplitElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SplitElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SplitElements.py): Creates a 6 m wall and a 6 m x 5 m slab with a hole, splits both with SplitElements along the line x = 2, then deletes the parts. The wall gives two parts: the original wall (0 to 2 m) and a copy with the same settings (2 to 6 m). The slab gives two slabs with the same settings: the original keeps the larger piece (2 to 6 m, with the hole), the copy gets the rest.

### CopyElementsToDatabase

Copies 2D elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, hotspots, texts, hatches, independent labels) from one database into another, e.g. from a worksheet into another worksheet, a detail or a layout, optionally moved by an offset. Returns the new elements in the order of the given ones.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CopyElementsToDatabase

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The 2D elements to copy: Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hotspot, Text, Hatch or Label (not associated with an element). Drawings are not copied yet: created from their own data they lose the link to their source view.
- `sourceDatabaseId` (DatabaseId): The database the elements are in. Default is the current database.
- `targetDatabaseId` (DatabaseId, required): The database to copy the elements into, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases).
- `offset` (Coordinate2D): Optional vector the copies are moved by in the target database. Without it they keep the coordinates of the originals.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required): The new element of each given element, in the same order, or the reason it was not copied.

Grasshopper: `CopyElementsToDatabaseComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CopyElementsToDatabase.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CopyElementsToDatabase.py): Copies a polyline from the floor plan into a new worksheet, moved by 1 m, with CopyElementsToDatabase. Run it with the floor plan open. The polyline and the worksheet are created by the script and deleted at the end.

### ElevateElements

Moves elements vertically by a given offset in meters, like Edit > Move > Elevate. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `elevation` (number, required): The vertical offset in meters to move the element by, like Edit > Move > Elevate. A positive value moves the element up, a negative value moves it down. The home story of the element does not change.
  - `copy` (boolean): Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be elevated. By default it's false.

Needs at least one editable Wall.

Needs at least one editable Wall. The angle is the one between origin-beginPoint and origin-endPoint.

### CopyElements

Copies elements by an offset, like dragging a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is moved by n times the offset, which makes a linear array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy (a part of a curtain wall, stair or railing, a locked element or one on a hidden or locked layer, ...) gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CopyElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to copy.
- `offset` (Coordinate3D, required): The vector in meters the first copy is moved by from its element.
- `count` (integer): Optional number of copies of each element. Copy n is moved by n times the offset, so more than one makes a linear array. By default it's 1.

Returns:

- `copies` (array of object, required): One item for each given element, in the same order.
  - `elements` (Elements, required): The new elements made from this element, the first copy first. When the element is in a group and Suspend Groups is off, Archicad copies the whole group, and the copies of the other members are listed too.
  - `error` (Error): Why the element, or some of its copies, could not be made. The copies made before the error are still listed in elements.

Grasshopper: `CopyElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CopyElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CopyElements.py): Makes a linear array of 5 copies of a wall, 2 m apart along the X axis, with CopyElements, then deletes the copies. Needs at least one editable Wall. Copy n is moved by n times the offset; the response lists the new elements of each given element in the order of the given ones.

### RotateCopyElements

Copies elements rotated around a center on the floor plan by an angle in radians, like rotating a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is rotated by n times the angle, which makes a circular array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RotateCopyElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to copy.
- `center` (Coordinate2D, required): The center of the rotation on the floor plan.
- `angle` (number, required): The angle in radians the first copy is rotated by from its element, counterclockwise.
- `count` (integer): Optional number of copies of each element. Copy n is rotated by n times the angle, so more than one makes a circular array. By default it's 1.

Returns:

- `copies` (array of object, required): One item for each given element, in the same order.
  - `elements` (Elements, required): The new elements made from this element, the first copy first. When the element is in a group and Suspend Groups is off, Archicad copies the whole group, and the copies of the other members are listed too.
  - `error` (Error): Why the element, or some of its copies, could not be made. The copies made before the error are still listed in elements.

Grasshopper: `RotateCopyElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RotateCopyElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RotateCopyElements.py): Makes a circular array of 3 copies of a wall around the project origin, 90 degrees apart, with RotateCopyElements, then deletes the copies. Needs at least one editable Wall. The angle is in radians, counterclockwise; copy n is rotated by n times the angle.

### ScaleElements

Scales elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view by a factor around a center point with Archicad's Resize edit, in one undo step. Resize scales X and Y by the same ratio, so factorY, if given, must equal factor. Elevations are kept: a beam, whose absolute elevation Resize would scale too, gets its story and level back after the resize. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch and Hotspot. An element of another type (library parts such as objects, lamps, doors and windows, stairs, railings, curtain walls, shells, morphs, texts, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still scaled.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ScaleElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to scale: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch or Hotspot, in the current database.
- `center` (Coordinate2D, required): The fixed point of the scaling on the floor plan; every point of the elements moves away from it (factor > 1) or towards it (factor < 1).
- `factor` (number, required): The scale factor, greater than 0: 2 doubles the distances from the center, 0.5 halves them.
- `factorY` (number): Optional scale factor in Y. Archicad's Resize scales X and Y by one ratio, so it must be the same as factor (or left out); a different value is refused.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ScaleElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ScaleElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ScaleElements.py): Scales a slab by 2 around the centre of its bounding box with ScaleElements, prints its bounding box before and after, then scales it back by 0.5. Needs at least one editable Slab. The bounding box after scaling should be twice as wide and deep, with the same centre.

### DeleteElements

Deletes elements, each in the database that contains it (the floor plan, a section, a worksheet, a layout, ...), whichever window is the current one; the current window stays. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) or a guid that is not in the project gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently, and does not stop the other elements from being deleted. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before deleting gets wouldDelete, so a script can preview a deletion before making it.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required): The elements to delete, of any database (the floor plan, a section, a worksheet, a layout, ...): each is deleted in the database that contains it, whichever window is the current one, and the current window stays. The zones among them are deleted before all the others, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding elements is gone before its boundary is. Deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found around the clicked point' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad.
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)
- `executionResults` (DeletionExecutionResults, required): One result for each input element, in the order of the input. On a dry run an element that passes every check made before deleting (it exists, its layer is not locked, it is editable) gets wouldDelete; Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

Grasshopper: `DeleteElementsComponent`, `ElementMetadata`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteElements.py): Creates a wall and deletes it again with DeleteElements, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.

### DeleteSelectedElements

Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true and lists the selected elements, with wouldDelete when there is at least one, or fails when one of them cannot be edited (Archicad then deletes none of them).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteSelectedElements

Parameters:

- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)
- `success` (boolean, required)
- `error` (Error)
- `wouldDelete` (boolean): Only on a dry run that passed the checks: true when at least one element is selected.
- `elements` (Elements): Only on a dry run: the selected elements (for a marquee, the ones it touches). A real run deletes them, together with the other members of their groups when Suspend Groups is off and the elements linked to them (labels, dimensions, ...).

Grasshopper: `DeleteSelectedElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteSelectedElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/DeleteSelectedElements.py): Creates a wall, selects only it and deletes it with DeleteSelectedElements, the same as pressing the Delete key. The original selection is restored at the end. Run it with the floor plan open.

Returns an execution result for each input element. The refresh cannot be undone.

The refresh cannot be undone.

### GetGDLParametersOfElements

Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements. parameterNames returns only the named parameters, and includePossibleValues false leaves out the value lists (which for font parameters list every installed font), for a much smaller answer. For the railing components GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists (posts, rails, balusters, panels ...), which have no parameter session in the Archicad API, the parameters are read from the component itself: isLocked is then always false and possibleValues is not given.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetGDLParametersOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `parameterNames` (array of string): Optional. Only the parameters with these GDL variable names are returned (case-insensitive), in the order of the library part. A name the element's library part does not have is left out. All parameters are returned when it is not given.
- `includePossibleValues` (boolean): Optional, true by default. When false, possibleValues (the value lists of the Parameter Script, e.g. every installed font for a font parameter) is left out of the answer, which makes it much smaller.

Returns:

- `gdlParametersOfElements` (array of GDLParameterList, required): The GDL parameters of elements.

Grasshopper: `GetGDLParametersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGDLParametersOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGDLParametersOfElements.py): Lists the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of a placed object with GetGDLParametersOfElements. includePossibleValues false leaves out the value lists of the Parameter Script, which keeps the answer small; parameterNames (e.g. ['A', 'B']) would return only the named parameters. Needs at least one Object.

### SetGDLParametersOfElements

Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. On a Curtain Wall Frame, A, B, ac_frameWidth and ac_frameDepth mirror the frame's contour, which Archicad derives from the frame's settings, so they are rejected instead of reporting a change that does not take effect; a frame without a library part (an invisible Boundary frame, for example) has no GDL parameters. The parameters are read back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label, or one the object's Parameter Script sets back) gives a failed execution result naming it: each given value (a whole array too, but not A, B or a single array item) is compared with the value read back. With dryRun true no element is changed and no undo step is created: the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before changing it gets wouldChange, listing the parameters a real run would change (the given ones and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them) with their old and new values. The railing components GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists (posts, rails, balusters, panels ...) have no parameter session in the Archicad API: their parameters are written to the component itself, no Parameter Script runs (a dry run lists only the given parameters), array parameters are not supported, and a value Archicad does not keep (one the railing's settings set) gives a failed execution result naming it.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetGDLParametersOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementsWithGDLParameters` (array of object, required): The elements with GDL parameters dictionary pairs.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `gdlParameters` (SetGDLParameterArray, required)
- `dryRun` (DryRun)

Returns:

- `dryRun` (DryRunFlag)
- `executionResults` (ChangeExecutionResults, required): One result for each item of elementsWithGDLParameters, in the order of the input. On a dry run the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, but the element is not changed. An element that passes every check made before changing it (the element and its parameters exist, every value is valid for its parameter, the element is editable) gets wouldChange: oldValue and newValue list the parameters a real run would change - the ones given and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them - before and after, each with name, index, type and value as GetGDLParametersOfElements gives them. Archicad can still refuse an element that passes them.

Grasshopper: `SetGDLParametersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetGDLParametersOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetGDLParametersOfElements.py): Widens a placed object by 0.1 m through its GDL parameter A with SetGDLParametersOfElements, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Object.

The marker of a Change Marker is its marker head, e.g. with the texts typed into it; a Change Marker with only a cloud has no marker and gets an error. Grasshopper: `GetMarkerParametersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetMarkerParametersOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetMarkerParametersOfElements.py): Reads the marker library part and parameters of the first windows, doors and change markers with GetMarkerParametersOfElements. ### ChangeLibraryPartOfElements

Changes the library part of the given Object, Lamp, Window, Door, Skylight, Zone and symbol Label elements to another library part of the same type (Wall End parts for wall ends), given by name, index or guid, e.g. to replace missing library parts with ones from the loaded libraries. The elements themselves (guid, properties, classifications) are kept. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects. Optionally keeps the values of the GDL parameters with the same name and type, and the size (A and B).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeLibraryPartOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementsWithLibraryPart` (array of object, required): The elements with the library part to change them to. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `libraryPart` (object or object or object, required): The new library part, given by one of name, index or guid. It has to be a placeable library part of the element's type in the loaded libraries; a wall end (a Window whose library part is a Wall End part) only takes another Wall End part.
  - `keepParameters` (boolean): Copies the values of the element's GDL parameters to the parameters of the new library part that have the same name, type and array dimensions; the other parameters get the new part's defaults. Default: true.
  - `keepSize` (boolean): Keeps the size (A and B) of the element; when false, the element gets the new part's default size. Default: true.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ChangeLibraryPartOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.py): Sets the first object to the library part it already uses with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements. Needs at least one Object. Giving the part it already has leaves the project unchanged; give the name of another library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it.

### GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements

Gets the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Curtain Wall Frame, Panel, Junction and Accessory elements as Archicad calculated them for their place in the curtain wall. GetGDLParametersOfElements returns the parameters the sub-element was set up with instead.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `calculatedParametersOfElements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The calculated parameters of each given element, in the order of the input, or an error for an element that is not a curtain wall frame, panel, junction or accessory.

Grasshopper: `GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements.py): Prints the GDL parameters of the first curtain wall panel as Archicad calculated them, with GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements. Needs at least one Curtain Wall.

### GetHotspotsOfElements

Gets the 2D hotspots of the given library part instances (Objects, Lamps, Windows, Doors, Skylights, Zones, Curtain Wall parts, etc.), in the library part's own coordinate system. For their positions in the project use GetSnapPointsOfElements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetHotspotsOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `hotspotsOfElements` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The hotspots of the given library part instances, in the order of the input.

Grasshopper: `GetHotspotsOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetHotspotsOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetHotspotsOfElements.py): Prints the 2D hotspots of the first object with GetHotspotsOfElements. Needs at least one Object.

### SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements

Changes which library part the marker of the given Window and Door elements uses, given by its name (find the available ones with GetAvailableLibraryParts); only a marker library part for the opening's type is accepted. The marker gets the new library part's default parameters, which SetMarkerParametersOfElements can change afterwards; the opening's own settings are left as they are.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements

Parameters:

- `elementsWithMarkerLibraryPart` (array of object, required): The elements with the library part their marker should use.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `libraryPartName` (string, required): The name of the library part the marker should use, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements and GetAvailableLibraryParts report it. It has to be a marker library part: Archicad's marker parent for windows or doors, or a library part derived from it. Any other library part is refused.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements.py): Sets the marker of the first window or door to the library part it already uses with SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements. Needs at least one Window or Door. Give the name of another marker library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it. The marker gets the library part's default parameters.

Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RunParameterScriptOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `RunParameterScriptOfElementsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RunParameterScriptOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RunParameterScriptOfElements.py): Runs the parameter script of every object with RunParameterScriptOfElements. Needs at least one Object. Parameters that depend on other parameters are recalculated.

### CreateColumns

Creates Column elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill as ModifyColumns, besides the position, size, top link (relativeTopStory, topOffset), slant, cross section and veneer; settings not given come from the Column tool defaults or the favorite. ModifyColumns writes single column segments (its segments list). Not written by either command: the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateColumns

Parameters:

- `columnsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Columns.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `coordinates` (object, required): 3D coordinate.
  - `height` (number): Optional explicit column height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or of the tool defaults. Cannot be combined with a non-zero relativeTopStory.
  - `relativeTopStory` (integer): Optional link of the column's top to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above); 0 means an explicit height. With a non-zero value Archicad computes the height from the story levels and topOffset. The linked story must exist. Cannot be combined with height. When omitted, the top link of the favorite or of the tool defaults is kept.
  - `topOffset` (number): Optional offset of the column's top from the level of the linked top story (negative is below it). Only has an effect when the top is linked (relativeTopStory non-zero, given here or kept from the favorite or the tool defaults).
  - `axisRotationAngle` (number): Optional column rotation angle in radians.
  - `slantAngle` (number): Optional slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also makes the column slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.
  - `isSlanted` (boolean): Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.
  - `slantDirectionAngle` (number): Optional rotation angle of the slanted column on the horizontal plane in radians.
  - `width` (number): Cross section width of the column, the diameter of a round one. Applied to all segments. A custom profile (profileId, or a tool default or favorite that uses one) sets the size itself and Archicad ignores the width; give buildingMaterialId to make a basic cross section of this size.
  - `depth` (number): Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments. Only effective for rectangular columns. A custom profile (profileId, or a tool default or favorite that uses one) sets the size itself and Archicad ignores the depth; give buildingMaterialId to make a basic cross section of this size.
  - `coreAnchor` (ColumnCoreAnchor)
  - `circleBased` (boolean): True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.
  - `isWidthAndHeightLinked` (boolean): When true, width and depth are kept equal (a round cross section too): a width, or else a depth, given alone sets both. A width and a depth given together with different values make them independent, unless this is given too. When omitted, the tool default (or favoriteName) is used. Applied to all segments.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.
  - `profileId` (AttributeId): Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.
  - `veneer` (ColumnVeneer): Veneer of the column (type, thickness, building material); the fields not given come from the tool defaults or favoriteName, thickness 0 creates the column without veneer. Applied to all segments.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.
  - `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.
  - `coverFill` (CoverFill): The cover fill of the column in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `ColumnsComponent`, `CreateColumnsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateColumns.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateColumns.py): Creates three columns with CreateColumns: one with the Column tool defaults, one round, 3 m high column with its own cut fill pens, and one whose top is linked to the story above, 15 cm below its level. Coordinates are in meters; z is the elevation of the column base. CreateColumns takes the same cut fill pens (written from Archicad 27), cover fill and top link (relativeTopStory, topOffset) as ModifyColumns. A linked column gets its height from the story levels, so it is not given a height; the story above must exist.

### CreateWalls

Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same wall settings as ModifyWalls, applied by the same code, including geometryType (Straight or Trapezoid, with begThickness and endThickness), profileType (Normal, Slanted or Trapez) and the slant angles, so a trapezoid or slanted wall is made in one call; only bottomOffset differs, which comes from zCoordinate. A slantAlpha or slantBeta that the wall's profileType cannot take fails the item instead of being dropped. Neither command can write a Polygonal outline (it needs an outline polygon, which these commands do not take), connectionPriority or junctionSequence (Archicad ignores writes to them; GetDetailsOfElements reads them), and on Archicad 29 any story visibility other than 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories'.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateWalls

Parameters:

- `wallsData` (array of object, required)
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Wall favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (structure, reference line location, top link, offsets, ...) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. With a favorite only begCoordinate and endCoordinate are needed.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Story index (as returned by GetStories). When provided, zCoordinate is interpreted as bottomOffset relative to the floor. Takes priority over zCoordinate for floor assignment.
  - `zCoordinate` (number): Absolute Z when floorIndex is absent; bottomOffset relative to the floor when floorIndex is provided.
  - `height` (number): Optional explicit height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or the tool default. When omitted, the height and top link of the favorite (or of the Wall tool defaults) are kept.
  - `thickness` (number): Optional thickness. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's thickness is kept. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Without structureType the new wall keeps the structure of the favorite (or the wall tool default), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.
  - `offset` (number): Optional reference line offset. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's offset is kept. Unavailable when the wall's referenceLineLocation is Center or CoreCenter (Archicad keeps 0 there): a non-zero value on such a wall fails it instead of being dropped.
  - `arcAngle` (number): Arc angle in radians; non-zero creates a curved wall (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).
  - `referenceLineLocation` (WallReferenceLineLocation): Optional. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's reference line location is kept. The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall.
  - `flipped` (boolean): Optional. True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped). When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's side is kept, which for a Profile wall mirrors its whole cross section.
  - `geometryType` (WallModificationGeometryType): Plan outline of the wall. Trapezoid makes begThickness and endThickness the wall's thickness at its begin and end point. Polygonal is not settable here; it is read-only via GetDetailsOfElements. CreateWalls makes a Straight wall when this is omitted. This is unrelated to slantAlpha/slantBeta - see profileType for the cross section shape those depend on.
  - `begThickness` (number): Thickness at begCoordinate, the same value as thickness (applied after it, so it wins when both are given). Together with endThickness it shapes a Trapezoid wall (geometryType). Like thickness, it only takes effect on a Basic wall.
  - `endThickness` (number): Thickness at endCoordinate. Only takes effect on a Trapezoid wall (geometryType); a Straight wall has one thickness. Like thickness, it only takes effect on a Basic wall.
  - `profileType` (WallModificationProfileType): Cross section shape of the wall. slantAlpha needs Slanted or Trapez, slantBeta needs Trapez. When omitted, CreateWalls keeps the favorite's or the Wall tool default's and ModifyWalls the wall's own.
  - `slantAlpha` (number): Angle of the slanted face in radians (pi/2 is vertical). Only takes effect when the wall's profileType is Slanted or Trapez, after this item is applied: any other value than the wall's current one or pi/2 on another wall fails the item instead of being dropped.
  - `slantBeta` (number): Angle of the second slanted face of a double slanted wall, in radians (pi/2 is vertical). Only takes effect when the wall's profileType is Trapez, after this item is applied: any other value than the wall's current one or pi/2 on another wall fails the item instead of being dropped.
  - `topOffset` (number): Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `relativeTopStory` (number): Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' for the same wall: whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `zoneRel` (WallZoneRelation)
  - `visibility` (StoryVisibility): Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.
  - `referenceMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
  - `oppositeMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
  - `sideMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial)
  - `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen): Pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen): Background pen of the cut fill. Archicad 27 and later; ignored on older versions.
  - `structureType` (WallStructureType): Optional. When neither this nor one of the attribute ids below is given, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's structure is kept.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `compositeId` (AttributeId)
  - `profileId` (AttributeId)
  - `contourPen` (integer): Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen.
  - `contourPen3D` (integer): Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).
  - `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.
  - `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).
  - `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.
  - `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
  - `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation): Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).
  - `useCompositePriority` (boolean): When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings): When newCreationMode is true, homeStoryDifference overrides the home story selected by floorIndex or derived from zCoordinate.
  - `inheritEndSurface` (boolean): The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.
  - `alignTexture` (boolean): Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.
  - `polyCanChange` (boolean): The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).
  - `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface materials are chained.
  - `logHeight` (number): Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.
  - `logDetails` (WallLogDetails)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateWallsComponent`, `WallsApiComponent`, `WallsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWalls.py): Creates a straight and a curved wall with CreateWalls. Fields not given (structure, top link, ...) come from the Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName. CreateWalls takes the same wall settings as ModifyWalls: the second wall also sets how it relates to zones and overrides the surface of its reference side.

### CreateBeams

Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens, cover fill and holes as ModifyBeams, besides the position, shape, slant and cross section; settings not given come from the Beam tool defaults or the favorite. Both commands take the same segments array, which sets the cross section, taper and length of single segments. Not written by either command: the surfaces of the beam segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateBeams

Parameters:

- `beamsData` (array of object, required)
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.
  - `zCoordinate` (number, required): Absolute Z of the beam's reference line. Which point of the cross section lies on the reference line is set by anchorPoint: with a Top anchor the beam hangs below zCoordinate, so zCoordinate 10 and height 0.1 span 9.9 to 10; MiddleLeft, Center and MiddleRight center it on zCoordinate; Bottom anchors stand it on top. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given.
  - `offset` (number): Horizontal distance of the beam from its reference line, in meters; positive moves the beam to the left of the line, looking from begCoordinate to endCoordinate.
  - `slantAngle` (number): Slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also switches the beam to slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.
  - `isSlanted` (boolean): Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.
  - `profileAngle` (number): Rotation angle of the profile around the beam's center line, in radians.
  - `arcAngle` (number): Optional arc angle in radians. A non-zero value makes a horizontally curved beam.
  - `verticalCurveHeight` (number): Optional rise of a vertically curved beam. A non-zero value makes a vertically curved beam; it wins over arcAngle.
  - `width` (number): Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments. A custom profile (profileId, or a tool default or favorite that uses one) sets the size itself and Archicad ignores the width; give buildingMaterialId to make a basic cross section of this size.
  - `height` (number): Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments. A custom profile (profileId, or a tool default or favorite that uses one) sets the size itself and Archicad ignores the height; give buildingMaterialId to make a basic cross section of this size.
  - `anchorPoint` (BeamAnchorPoint): The point of the cross section that lies on the reference line (begCoordinate to endCoordinate at zCoordinate). Top anchors hang the beam below zCoordinate, Bottom anchors stand it on top, MiddleLeft, Center and MiddleRight center it. Left and Right anchors put the line on the beam's left or right edge, looking from begCoordinate to endCoordinate; TopCenter, Center and BottomCenter keep it on the beam's axis.
  - `circleBased` (boolean): True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.
  - `isWidthAndHeightLinked` (boolean): When true, width and height are kept equal (a round cross section too): a width, or else a height, given alone sets both. A width and a height given together with different values make them independent, unless this is given too. When omitted, the tool default (or favoriteName) is used. Applied to all segments.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.
  - `profileId` (AttributeId): Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.
  - `segmentCount` (integer): Optional number of segments of the new beam, e.g. one per beam when beams with different cross sections are merged into one (segments then gives each its cross section and length). Added segments copy the last segment of the Beam tool defaults or the favorite, with a Basic structure; the joints between segments are vertical cuts. When the number changes, every segment gets the same proportional length unless segments sets its length. The beam is read back, and when Archicad did not keep the number it is deleted again and the item fails. Not taken by ModifyBeams: an existing beam keeps its number of segments.
  - `segments` (array of BeamSegmentModification): Optional changes to single segments of the new beam, which has the segments of the Beam tool defaults or the favorite, or segmentCount segments: their cross section, taper and length. Applied after segmentCount and the cross section given for all segments, so a segment given here keeps its own values. A segmentIndex the beam does not have is an error and the beam is not created.
  - `holes` (array of BeamHoleModification): Optional holes of the new beam, in the shape ModifyBeams takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns them (centerX along the beam from begCoordinate). They are written right after the beam is created; a hole Archicad refuses fails the item and the beam is not created. When omitted, no holes are written.
  - `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.
  - `coverFill` (CoverFill): The cover fill of the beam in the floor plan, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `BeamsComponent`, `CreateBeamsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateBeams.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateBeams.py): Creates a 6 m long beam at 3 m height with its own cut fill pen and two holes with CreateBeams. With the TopCenter anchor the beam hangs below its reference line at zCoordinate. CreateBeams takes the same cut fill pens (written from Archicad 27), cover fill and holes as ModifyBeams; centerX of a hole is measured along the beam from begCoordinate.

### CreateStairs

Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters, optionally with the segment type of each baseline edge and the turn at each baseline point (landings and winders), and with curved baseline edges (baseLineArcs) for curved and spiral stairs. Accepts the same settings as ModifyStairs: the step values with their locks, the top link (relativeTopStory, topOffset), the Rules and Standards, the headroom, the finish and structure visibility, the extra treads, the walking line, the numbering, the walking direction, and the tread, riser and structure settings of the flights and the landings (with the monolith data of a Monolith structure and the stringer data of a Side one), and the floor plan and reflected ceiling plan display (shown stories and components, the symbol on each story, the break line and the line type, pen and fill overrides), and the line types, pens and fills of the structure symbols (structureSymbols, monolithStructureSymbols) with their visibility on the stories (structureVisibilityOnStories); settings not given come from the Stair tool defaults or the favorite. Archicad lays out the boundaries and the walking lines from the baseline and the flight width, and the API cannot write them: an item that gives one is refused with an error that says so.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateStairs

Parameters:

- `stairsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Stair elements.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `baseLinePoints` (array of Coordinate2D, required): 2D coordinates of the stair baseline polyline. Whether the baseline runs along the left edge, the right edge or the center of the flight is the Stair tool's baseline position, taken from baselinePosition, or else from the tool defaults or favoriteName: with the baseline on the left edge, the flight lies to the right of it, looking from the first point to the last. The first point is kept; the length of the flight comes from the riser count and going, so the flight does not necessarily end at the last point given. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.
  - `baselinePosition` (string ("Left", "Right", "Center")): Optional. Where the baseline runs on the flight, looking from the first point to the last. Left: along the left edge, the flight lies to the right of the baseline. Right: along the right edge, the flight lies to the left of it. Center: along the middle of the flight. Without it the baseline position of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is used.
  - `baselineOffset` (number): Optional. The offset of the baseline from the flight edge that baselinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center. Without it the offset of the Stair tool defaults (or of favoriteName) is kept.
  - `zCoordinate` (number, required): The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.
  - `totalHeight` (number): Total height of the stair.
  - `flightWidth` (number): Width of the stair flight.
  - `stepNum` (integer): Number of risers (steps). Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not have this many risers.
  - `riserHeight` (number): Height of each riser. Advisory: Archicad computes the step layout from totalHeight and the stair rules, so the created stair may not use this riser height.
  - `treadDepth` (number): Depth (going) of each tread. Pinned as a fixed going in the stair rules, so the run length follows from the number of treads; the standard's combined riser/going rules (2R+G, R+G, R/G) are not applied to this stair.
  - `baseLineEdges` (array of StairBaseLineEdge): Optional. The segment type of each baseline edge, one item per edge (baseLinePoints.length - 1 items; edge i runs from point i to point i + 1). A U-shaped stair with a half landing is Flight, Landing, Flight with landing turns at both inner points. When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineVertices is given, every edge is a flight. Combinations Archicad cannot build fail like any other invalid stair.
  - `baseLineVertices` (array of StairBaseLineVertex): Optional. The turn at each baseline point, one item per point (baseLinePoints.length items). When neither baseLineEdges nor baseLineVertices is given, Archicad decides the segments and turns itself; when only baseLineEdges is given, the first and last points get no turn and every other point a landing turn. Winders use Archicad's default winder settings.
  - `baseLineArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional. The curved edges of the baseline, for a curved or spiral stair, in the format GetDetailsOfElements returns them: begIndex and endIndex are 0-based indices of baseLinePoints, and an arc bends one edge, so endIndex = begIndex + 1. arcAngle is the angle of the arc in radians, not 0 and less than a full turn; it is positive if the arc is on the right-hand side of the straight edge. At most one arc per edge; the edges without an arc are straight.
  - `relativeTopStory` (integer): Links the top of the stair to a story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above); 0 unlinks it. With a top link Archicad computes totalHeight from the story levels and topOffset, so a totalHeight given in the same call is not kept. Archicad does not return the link when the stair is read, so GetDetailsOfElements does not report it; read the resulting totalHeight back instead.
  - `topOffset` (number): The offset of the top of the stair from the level of the linked top story (for example -0.15 for 15 cm below it). Only used when the stair's top is linked (relativeTopStory not 0).
  - `rules` (StairRules): The Rules and Standards of the stair: only the given limits and applied flags are written, the others are kept. Archicad lays the steps out within the applied limits, so read the riser count and going back with GetDetailsOfElements. In CreateStairs and ModifyStairs a treadDepth pins the going limits and releases the 2R+G, R+G and R/G rules first; the rules given here are written after that. An unknown key is refused, and ModifyStairs reads the given rules back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `headroom` (StairHeadroom): The headroom of the stair (Stair Settings > Headroom): only the given fields are written, the others are kept. An unknown key is refused, and ModifyStairs reads the given fields back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `treadDepthLocked` (boolean): Whether the going lengths are locked.
  - `totalHeightLocked` (boolean): Whether the total height is locked.
  - `finishVisible` (boolean): Whether the tread and riser finishes of the stair are shown; false models only the structure (e.g. a monolith). The treads and risers of each part can also be switched on and off with treads and risers.
  - `extraTopTread` (boolean): Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top.
  - `extraBottomTread` (boolean): Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom.
  - `walkingLinePosition` (string ("Left", "Right", "Center", "Auto")): Where the walking line runs on the flight: offset from the left or the right side (walkingLineOffset), centered, or placed by Archicad (Auto).
  - `walkingLineOffset` (number): The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center and Auto.
  - `walkingLineSymbolPosition` (string ("Auto", "Center", "Custom")): Where the symbol of the walking line is placed (API_StairType::walkLineSymbPos): by Archicad (Auto), centered, or where it was placed by hand (Custom).
  - `numberingType` (string ("Treads", "Risers")): Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers.
  - `inputDirection` (string ("Upward", "Inverse")): The walking direction along the baseline: upward from its first point, or inverse (downward).
  - `uniformFinish` (boolean): Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.
  - `uniformMonolithAttributes` (boolean): Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.
  - `uniformDrainings` (boolean): Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.
  - `structureVisibility` (boolean): Whether the structure of the stair is shown.
  - `stairDisplayType` (string ("Custom", "ByModelViewOptions")): Whether the floor plan display of the stair is set in the stair itself (Custom) or comes from the Model View Options (ByModelViewOptions). While it is ByModelViewOptions, Archicad may show the stair by the Model View Options instead of floorPlanLayout and reflectedCeilingPlanLayout; give Custom in the same call to use them.
  - `floorPlanLayout` (StairLayoutSettings): The floor plan display of the stair: the stories it is shown on, its visible components, the symbol on each story, the break line and the line type, pen and fill overrides. Independent of reflectedCeilingPlanLayout.
  - `reflectedCeilingPlanLayout` (StairLayoutSettings): The reflected ceiling plan display of the stair: the stories it is shown on, its visible components, the symbol on each story, the break line and the line type, pen and fill overrides. Independent of floorPlanLayout.
  - `structureSymbols` (array of StairStructureSymbolSettings): The line types, pens and fills of the structure symbol, per structure type (UnderStructure, Stringer) and view (FloorPlan, CeilingPlan), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given fields of the given items are changed; ModifyStairs reads them back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `monolithStructureSymbols` (array of StairMonolithStructureSymbolSettings): The line types, pens and fills of the monolithic structure's symbol, per view (FloorPlan, CeilingPlan) and part (Visible, Hidden), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given fields of the given items are changed; ModifyStairs reads them back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `structureVisibilityOnStories` (array of StairStructureVisibilitySettings): Which structure symbols are shown on which of the stair's relevant stories, per view (FloorPlan, CeilingPlan), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements returns: whether one representation is used on every story, and per story range the visible structures, fills and monolithic parts. Only the given fields of the given items are changed; ModifyStairs reads them back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `treads` (array of object): The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back in treads.
  - `risers` (array of object): The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back in risers.
  - `structures` (array of object): The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side: the left and right side structures and the structure under the stair, with the keys GetDetailsOfElements reads in structures. Only the given fields of the given parts and sides are changed. ModifyStairs reads the given monolith and sideStair data back and reports a value Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `leftBoundary` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the left boundary of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `rightBoundary` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the right boundary of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `walkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `customWalkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the custom walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `centerWalkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the center walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateStairsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateStairs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateStairs.py): Creates a straight stair, a U-shaped stair with a half landing and a curved stair with CreateStairs. Two baseline points make a straight stair; more points make an L- or U-shaped one. baseLineArcs bends baseline edges into arcs (0-based point indices, as GetDetailsOfElements returns them). The straight stair's baseline runs along the middle of its flight (baselinePosition), and its treads and structure are set with the same tread, riser and structure settings ModifyStairs accepts. Fields not given come from the Stair tool defaults.

### SolveStairBaseline

Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines (straight or with curved edges) and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving, and the Rules and Standards (riser height and going limits, 2R+G, R+G, R/G, pitch) CreateStairs would lay the steps out by, with a given treadDepth pinned as CreateStairs pins it. The solver checks the baseline only: it does not lay out the steps, so stepNum, riserHeight and treadDepth are the given values or the tool defaults, and CreateStairs picks the riser count and height for totalHeight within the rules. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SolveStairBaseline

Parameters:

- `stairsData` (array of StairBaselineData, required): Array of Stair data to check, with the same fields as the items of CreateStairs (without favoriteName). Nothing is created.

Returns:

- `solutions` (array of StairBaselineSolution or ErrorItem, required): The results of the stair solver, aligned with the input stairsData.

Grasshopper: `SolveStairBaselineComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SolveStairBaseline.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SolveStairBaseline.py): Checks an L-shaped stair baseline with SolveStairBaseline, without creating a stair. Prints whether the baseline is Correct, Solved (with the solved baseline) or NotSolved. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateSlabs

Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same surfaces (top, side, bottom), cut fill pens, floor fill and floor plan and section display (contour, section contour and hidden contour pens and line types, the story visibility of the contour and the fill, materialsChained, linkToSettings) as ModifySlabs, besides the outline, holes, level and structure; settings not given come from the Slab tool defaults or the favorite. The Edge Angle and the surface of single edges are written afterwards with ModifySlabs (edgeTrim, edgeTrims, edgeSideMaterials). Not written by either command: the cut fill pens before Archicad 27; of the floor fill orientation Archicad applies only the type through the API.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.0.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateSlabs

Parameters:

- `slabsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Slabs.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `level` (number, required): The Z coordinate value of the reference line of the slab.
  - `thickness` (number): Optional slab thickness. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType, buildingMaterialId or compositeId the new slab keeps the structure of the slab tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.
  - `structureType` (SlabStructureType): Optional structure of the slab. If omitted, derived from buildingMaterialId or compositeId when one is given, otherwise the slab tool default (or the favorite) is kept.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): Building material of a Basic slab. Cannot be combined with compositeId.
  - `compositeId` (AttributeId): Composite attribute of a Composite slab. Cannot be combined with buildingMaterialId.
  - `referencePlaneLocation` (SlabReferencePlaneLocation): For a basic (homogeneous) slab only 'Top' or 'Bottom' are valid.
  - `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the edge of the slab.
  - `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Polygon outline arcs of the slab.
  - `holes` (Holes2D)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.
  - `topMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): Overrides the surface of the top of the slab.
  - `sideMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): Overrides the surface of the sides of the slab.
  - `bottomMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): Overrides the surface of the bottom of the slab.
  - `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the background pen of the cut fill. Written from Archicad 27.
  - `floorFill` (FloorFill): The cover fill of the slab in the floor plan. Only the given fields change; of the orientation Archicad applies only its type through the API, read it back with GetDetailsOfElements.
  - `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface materials are chained.
  - `contourPen` (integer): Pen of the slab's contour in the floor plan.
  - `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the slab's contour in the floor plan.
  - `sectionContourPen` (integer): Pen of the slab's contour where it is cut in sections.
  - `sectionContourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the slab's contour where it is cut in sections.
  - `hiddenContourLinePen` (integer): Pen of the slab's hidden contour lines in the floor plan.
  - `hiddenContourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the slab's hidden contour lines in the floor plan.
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): Archicad 29 and later: when true, Archicad recomputes visibility and fillVisibility from the slab's elevation and ignores the values given for them. Giving visibility or fillVisibility without this key turns it off. Before Archicad 29 a slab has no such setting, and the item fails when this key is given.
  - `visibility` (StoryVisibility): The stories the slab's contour is shown on. Only the given fields change.
  - `fillVisibility` (StoryVisibility): The stories the slab's cover fill is shown on. Only the given fields change.
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings): How the slab is linked to its home story.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateSlabsComponent`, `SlabsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateSlabs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateSlabs.py): Creates a 6 m x 5 m slab with a 1 m x 1 m hole, a top surface and a floor fill with CreateSlabs. level is the elevation of the slab's reference plane, in meters. CreateSlabs takes the same surfaces, cut fill pens (written from Archicad 27) and floor fill as ModifySlabs.

### CreateWindows

Creates Window elements in host walls based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateWindows

Parameters:

- `windowsData` (array of object, required)
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `ownerWallId` (ElementId, required)
  - `width` (number)
  - `height` (number)
  - `sillHeight` (number)
  - `centerOffset` (number, required)
  - `reflected` (boolean)
  - `refSide` (boolean)
  - `oSide` (boolean)
  - `reveal` (boolean): Turn the reveal on or off.
  - `revealDepthOffset` (number): Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
  - `pen` (integer): Pen of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.
  - `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the opening's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.
  - `cutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut lines of the opening.
  - `sectionFillId` (AttributeId): Fill of the section of the opening; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.
  - `sectionFillPen` (integer)
  - `sectionFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `sectionContourPen` (integer)
  - `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen of the overhead lines ("Overhead Line Pens").
  - `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the overhead lines ("Overhead Lines").
  - `belowViewLinePen` (integer): Pen of the uncut lines of the opening.
  - `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the uncut lines ("Uncut Lines").
  - `useObjectPens` (boolean): Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.
  - `useObjectLineTypes` (boolean): Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.
  - `useObjectSectionAttributes` (boolean): Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.
  - `verticalLink` (WindowDoorVerticalLink)
  - `verticalLinkStoryIndex` (integer): The index of the story the opening is anchored to when verticalLink is 'SillToStory' or 'HeaderToStory' (API_VerticalLink::linkValue). When a story anchor is given without it, the opening keeps the story it is anchored to, or else its home story.
  - `subFloorThickness` (number): Sub-floor thickness: the floor build-up the sill height is given from (API_OpeningBaseType::subFloorThickness).
  - `revealDepthLocation` (WindowDoorRevealDepthLocation)
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId): The one surface of the whole window or door (API_OpeningBaseType::mat); used unless useObjectMaterials is true.
  - `useObjectMaterials` (boolean): Use the surfaces defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.
  - `directionType` (WindowDoorDirectionType)
  - `fixPoint` (WindowDoorFixPoint)
  - `libraryPartName` (string): Optional. Localized library part name (docu_UName) to place instead of the tool default/favorite, e.g. a shutter part that has no favorite. It has to be a window library part. Set on the created window only, with its A and B from `width` and `height` (or the tool default's width and height); the Window tool defaults are not changed.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional. Name of an existing Window favorite (as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`). Applied to the Window tool defaults before the create.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `WindowsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWindows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateWindows.py): Creates a wall and places a 1 m x 1.5 m window in it with CreateWindows. centerOffset is measured along the wall from its begin point. The library part comes from the Window tool defaults, or from libraryPartName or favoriteName. id sets the window's Element ID and layerIndex its layer; without them it gets the next automatic ID and the layer of the tool defaults.
