### GetOpeningDefault

Returns the settings of the Opening tool defaults: the extrusion parameters (as GetOpeningDetails returns them) and the floor plan parameters (as GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns them). Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetOpeningDefault

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `extrusionParameters` (object, required): The size and extrusion settings. A size Archicad does not give for the opening's shape is left out.
  - `constraint` (string ("ForcedVertical", "ForcedHorizontal", "Aligned", "Free")): How the opening's orientation is constrained.
  - `limitType` (string ("Infinite", "Finite", "HalfInfinite")): How far the opening's extrusion reaches.
  - `linkedStatus` (string ("Linked", "NotLinked")): Whether the opening's width and height are linked. Left out when Archicad gives none.
  - `shapeType` (string ("Rectangular", "Circular", "Polygonal")): The shape of the opening's polygon.
  - `width` (number)
  - `height` (number)
  - `anchor` (string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"), required): The anchor point of the opening's polygon.
  - `anchorAltitude` (number)
  - `extrusionStartOffset` (number)
  - `finiteBodyLength` (number)
  - `isExtrusionSurfaceOverridden` (boolean, required)
  - `extrusionSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the extrusion faces. Only given when it is overridden.
  - `isEndSurfaceOverridden` (boolean, required)
  - `endSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the end faces. Only given when it is overridden.
  - `areOverriddenSurfacesLinked` (boolean, required)
- `floorPlanParameters` (object, required)
  - `floorPlanDisplayMode` (string ("Symbolic", "SymbolicCut", "SymbolicOverhead", "Projected")): How the opening is shown on the floor plan.
  - `dividedOpeningMode` (string ("Disconnected", "Connected")): How the parts of an opening divided by the floor plan cut are shown.
  - `openEdgeStyle` (string ("Hide", "ShowUncut", "ShowOverhead")): How the open edges of the opening are shown on the floor plan.

### SetOpeningDefault

Changes the settings of the Opening tool defaults, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. Only the given settings change. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetOpeningDefault

Parameters:

- `extrusionParameters` (object): The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.

  - `limitType` (string ("Infinite", "Finite", "HalfInfinite")): How far the opening's extrusion reaches.
  - `linkedStatus` (string ("Linked", "NotLinked")): Whether the opening's width and height are linked. While they are linked, giving both width and height makes a square of the height; give NotLinked with them to get a different width and height.

  - `referenceAxisPen` (integer)
  - `referenceAxisLineTypeId` (AttributeId): The line type of the reference axis.
  - `referenceAxisOverhang` (number): How far the reference axis reaches beyond the opening.
  - `cutSurfacesUseLineOfCutElements` (boolean): Whether the cut surfaces use the line of the cut elements instead of cutSurfacesLinePen and cutSurfacesLineTypeId.
  - `cutSurfacesLinePen` (integer)
  - `cutSurfacesLineTypeId` (AttributeId)

  - `coverFillId` (AttributeId): The fill of the cover fills.
  - `coverFillPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillOrientation` (HatchOrientationType)
  - `coverFillTransformation` (CoverFillTransformation): The orientation and distortion of the cover fill. Left out when Archicad gives none.
  - `cutSymbolLibPartId` (Guid): The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the cut opening. Left out when the opening has no cut symbol.
  - `unCutSymbolLibPartId` (Guid): The id of the library part drawn as the symbol of the uncut opening. Left out when the opening has no uncut symbol.

### PlaceOpenings

Places openings with the Opening tool settings at points of their parent elements. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface. Each opening can be given its own extrusion and floor plan settings, which change only that opening and not the tool's settings. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#PlaceOpenings

Parameters:

- `openingsData` (array of object, required)
  - `parentElementId` (ElementId, required): The element to place the opening in.
  - `point` (Coordinate3D, required): Where to place the opening. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface.
  - `extrusionParameters` (object): The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.
  - `floorPlanParameters` (object): The floor plan settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. The ones left out are not changed.

The first opening uses the Opening tool settings, the second gets its own size and floor plan display (the tool settings are not changed). Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### SetOpeningDetails

Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetOpeningDetails

Parameters:

- `openingsWithDetails` (array of object, required): The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to change, each with the details to set. A detail that is left out stays as it is.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `parentElementId` (ElementId): The new element the opening belongs to.
  - `addCutElements` (array of ElementIdArrayItem): Elements the opening should cut as well.
  - `removeCutElements` (array of ElementIdArrayItem): Elements the opening should no longer cut.
  - `polygon` (array of Coordinate2D): The new shape of the opening, in the plane of the xAxis and yAxis returned by GetOpeningDetails. Archicad keeps only the shape: it places the polygon on the opening's anchor point by the opening's anchor (extrusionParameters.anchor), so with the Center anchor the polygon is centred on the anchor point, and an offset in the given coordinates is dropped. The polygon does not move the opening; GetOpeningDetails reads it back measured from the anchor point.
  - `transformation` (array of number): A transformation applied to the opening's geometry: a 3x4 matrix of 12 numbers, row by row, the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers being the translation along X, Y and Z. For example [1,0,0,1, 0,1,0,0, 0,0,1,0] is a translation by 1 along X. The matrix goes to Archicad as it is, and Archicad refuses a 3x3 part that is not orthogonal or that scales with the error 'Can transform only with ortogonal matrix with no scaling.' Archicad 29 has also been reported to refuse a pure translation with that error (#2957); the cause is not known yet.
  - `extrusionParameters` (object): The size and extrusion settings to change, with the names GetOpeningDetails returns. The ones left out are not changed.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetOpeningDetailsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetOpeningDetails.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetOpeningDetails.py): Moves the first opening 0.5 m along X with SetOpeningDetails, reads it back, then moves it back. Needs at least one Opening (made with the Opening tool). The transformation is a 3x4 matrix, row by row, with the translation in the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

### CreateMorphs

Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions or arbitrary bodies. Each item may name a favorite (favoriteName) to start from, a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id); the given geometry and floor are kept.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateMorphs

Parameters:

- `morphsData` (array of object, required)
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Morph favorite to base the new morph on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. The geometry (basePoint, size or body, axes) and the floor always come from this item, not from the favorite.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `basePoint` (Coordinate3D, required): Origin of the morph (the corner of a size box, the (0, 0, 0) of a body). Its z is absolute, measured from the project zero, unless level is given, which then decides the height instead.
  - `size` (Dimensions3D): Builds a simple axis-aligned box of this size. Mutually exclusive with `body` - give exactly one of the two.
  - `body` (MorphBody): Builds arbitrary geometry instead of a simple box. Mutually exclusive with `size` - give exactly one of the two.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `xAxis` (Coordinate3D)
  - `yAxis` (Coordinate3D)
  - `zAxis` (Coordinate3D)
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId)
  - `topExpansion` (number): Only used with `size` (box) morphs. Expands the top rectangle outwards on all four sides by this amount, creating a frustum (e.g. sloped excavation shape). 0 creates a cuboid.
  - `castShadow` (boolean)
  - `receiveShadow` (boolean)
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean)
  - `showContour` (StoryVisibility)
  - `showFill` (StoryVisibility)
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
  - `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation)
  - `cutFillPen` (integer)
  - `cutFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `cutLineType` (AttributeId)
  - `cutLinePen` (integer)
  - `uncutLineType` (AttributeId)
  - `uncutLinePen` (integer)
  - `overheadLineType` (AttributeId)
  - `overheadLinePen` (integer)
  - `useCoverFillType` (boolean)
  - `outlineContourDisplay` (boolean)
  - `coverFillType` (AttributeId)
  - `coverFillPen` (integer)
  - `coverFillBGPen` (integer)
  - `use3DHatching` (boolean)
  - `coverFillOrientation` (CoverFillOrientation)
  - `useDistortedCoverFill` (boolean)
  - `textureProjectionType` (TextureProjectionType)
  - `textureProjectionCoords` (array of Coordinate3D)
  - `level` (number): Optional height of the base point above the home story (floorIndex, or the story derived from basePoint's z when floorIndex is omitted), the same value GetDetailsOfElements reports as level. When given, it replaces basePoint's z.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional home story. If omitted, derived from the basePoint's z value.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateMorphsComponent`, `MorphsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateMorphs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateMorphs.py): Creates a 2 m box morph and a tetrahedron morph from vertices and faces with CreateMorphs. A body's vertices are local to the morph's basePoint; each face lists vertex indices counterclockwise as seen from outside. An item may also name a Morph favorite to start from (favoriteName), a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id), as the box does with its id.

### CreateRoofs

Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead. Each item may give a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id), and a multi-plane roof the planes of its edges (pivotEdges, e.g. gables), as ModifyRoofs takes them.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateRoofs

Parameters:

- `roofsData` (array of object, required)
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the tool defaults.
  - `level` (number, required)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.
  - `thickness` (number): Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType the new roof keeps the structure of the roof tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.
  - `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required)
  - `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc)
  - `holes` (Holes2D)
  - `pivotLine` (RoofPivotLine): If given, creates a single-plane roof instead of a multi-plane roof, tilted along this pivot line.
  - `angle` (number): Slope angle of the single-plane roof in radians. Only valid together with 'pivotLine'.
  - `eavesOverhang` (number)
  - `fitSkylightToCurve` (boolean): Multi-plane roofs only: whether skylights are placed tangentially to the curved surfaces of the roof rather than parallel to its individual segments, as GetDetailsOfElements reports it. When omitted the new roof gets the value of the roof tool default.
  - `levels` (array of RoofLevel)
  - `pivotEdges` (array of RoofPivotEdgeChange): Multi-plane roofs only: the roof planes of each edge of the pivot polygon, one item per edge in the order GetDetailsOfElements reports them (item i is the edge from vertex i to vertex i + 1 of polygonCoordinates, the last one closing the polygon; the edges of each hole follow), as ModifyRoofs takes them. They are written right after the roof is made from levels and eavesOverhang, and only the given fields change those planes; an item without levels keeps its edge. angleType Gable makes a gable roof in one call. If they cannot be written, the roof is not created.
  - `structureType` (RoofStructureType)
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `compositeId` (AttributeId)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateRoofsComponent`, `RoofsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRoofs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRoofs.py): Creates a multi-plane roof, a single-plane roof and a gable roof with CreateRoofs. A pivotLine makes a single-plane roof that rises on the left of the line; angles are in radians. pivotEdges sets the planes of the edges of a multi-plane roof (one item per edge, in the order of polygonCoordinates): angleType Gable makes a gable on that edge. id and layerIndex set the Element ID and the layer of the new roof.

### CreateShells

Creates extruded, revolved and ruled Shell elements from profile polylines, with thickness, structure, an optional clipping contour and holes.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateShells

Parameters:

- `shellsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Shells.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Shell favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `shellClass` (string ("Extruded", "Revolved", "Ruled"), required): Extruded: 'profile' swept along 'extrusionVector'. Revolved: 'profile' turned around 'axis'. Ruled: a surface ruled between 'profile' and 'secondProfile'.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional story index of the shell. Without it the shell is placed on the story of the Shell tool defaults.
  - `basePlane` (CoordinateSystem3D): Base plane of the shell, in project coordinates; the profiles, the extrusion, the axis and the contour and hole polygons are given in it. The project axes by default, except for a Revolved shell, whose default base plane stands upright (its Y axis is the project Z axis), so the profile's x is the radius and its y the height.
  - `profile` (ShellProfile, required): The profile polyline. Extruded: in the plane across the extrusion, x horizontal and y up. Revolved: in the base plane's XY plane. Ruled: in the XY plane of 'profilePlane'.
  - `thickness` (number): Only takes effect on a Basic shell; a Composite shell takes its thickness from the composite.
  - `isFlipped` (boolean): Applies the thickness to the other side of the reference surface.
  - `structureType` (RoofStructureType)
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId)
  - `compositeId` (AttributeId)
  - `extrusionVector` (Coordinate3D): Extruded only, required: the direction and length of the extrusion, in base plane coordinates.
  - `extrusionStart` (Coordinate3D): Extruded only: the point the extrusion starts from, in base plane coordinates.
  - `shapePlaneTilt` (number): Extruded only: tilt of the profile's plane, in radians.
  - `begPlaneTilt` (number): Extruded only: tilt of the start plane of the extrusion, in radians.
  - `endPlaneTilt` (number): Extruded only: tilt of the end plane of the extrusion, in radians.
  - `slantAngle` (number): Extruded and Revolved: slant of the extrusion vector or of the profile, in radians.
  - `axis` (CoordinateSystem3D): Revolved only: the coordinate system whose Z axis the profile is turned around, in base plane coordinates. By default the base plane's Y axis.
  - `revolutionAngle` (number): Revolved only: the angle the profile is turned through, in radians. 2*pi (a full turn) by default.
  - `beginAngle` (number): Revolved only: the angle the revolution starts at, in radians.
  - `distortionAngle` (number): Revolved only: shear of the revolution, in radians. pi/2 (no shear) by default.
  - `segmentsByCircle` (integer): Revolved only: the number of segments a full circle is resolved into.
  - `secondProfile` (ShellProfile): Ruled only, required: the second profile polyline, in the XY plane of 'secondProfilePlane'.
  - `profilePlane` (CoordinateSystem3D): Ruled only, required: the plane of 'profile', in base plane coordinates.
  - `secondProfilePlane` (CoordinateSystem3D): Ruled only, required: the plane of 'secondProfile', in base plane coordinates.
  - `morphingRule` (string ("Paired", "Smooth")): Ruled only: how the two profiles are joined, segment by segment (Paired) or smoothly.
  - `contour` (ShellCutPolygon): Optional clipping contour: only the part of the shell inside this polygon, seen along the Z axis of its plane, is kept. Its 'depth' is ignored.
  - `holes` (array of ShellCutPolygon): Optional holes, each requiring 'depth' to extrude its cutting polygon along the Z axis of its plane.
  - `begShapeEdgeTrim` (ShellEdgeTrim): Optional trim of the profile's edges at the start of the shell (the start plane of an extrusion, the begin angle of a revolution, the first profile of a ruled shell). Perpendicular at pi/2 by default, as the Shell tool draws it, also when favoriteName is given.
  - `endShapeEdgeTrim` (ShellEdgeTrim): Optional trim of the profile's edges at the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.
  - `begSideEdgeTrim` (ShellEdgeTrim): Optional trim of the edge that the profile's first point sweeps from the start to the end of the shell. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.
  - `endSideEdgeTrim` (ShellEdgeTrim): Optional trim of the edge that the profile's last point sweeps. Perpendicular at pi/2 by default.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateShells.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateShells.py): Creates an extruded barrel vault, a revolved dome and a ruled shell with CreateShells. The vault has a square opening, and the dome has a circular oculus. Profiles, placement planes and cutting polygons define the three shells.

### CreateSkylights

Creates Skylight elements with a roof or shell owner and a floor plan anchor position. It takes the same settings as ModifySkylights (anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display, pens, line types, section fill, surface and the library part flags) and optionally a library part; the settings not given come from the Skylight tool defaults or a favorite. Surface placement is handled by Archicad and has not yet been verified for this command.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateSkylights

Parameters:

- `skylightsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Skylights.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Skylight favorite to base the new element on.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element. When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `ownerId` (ElementId, required): The roof (single- or multi-plane) or shell the skylight is placed in.
  - `libraryPartName` (string): Optional localized name of a skylight library part to place instead of the tool default's.
  - `anchorPosition` (Coordinate2D, required): Global XY coordinates of the skylight's anchor point (API_SkylightType::anchorPosition). Archicad places the skylight on its owner roof or shell at this point; moving it onto another plane of a multi-plane roof has not been verified.
  - `anchorPoint` (string ("BottomCenter", "BottomLeft", "BottomRight", "TopCenter", "TopLeft", "TopRight")): Which point of the skylight anchorPosition places (API_SkylightType::anchorPoint).
  - `fixMode` (string ("Horizontal", "Vertical")): What the skylight keeps when the angle or the height of its owner changes (API_SkylightType::fixMode).
  - `width` (number)
  - `height` (number)
  - `azimuthAngle` (number): Rotation angle of the skylight in the horizontal plane, measured clockwise, in radians (API_SkylightType::azimuthAngle).
  - `elevationAngle` (number): Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians (API_SkylightType::elevationAngle). Archicad may set it again from the owner roof or shell.
  - `reflected` (boolean): Mirror the skylight (API_OpeningBaseType::reflected).
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
  - `pen` (integer): Pen of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectPens is true.
  - `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the skylight's floor plan symbol; used unless useObjectLineTypes is true.
  - `cutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut lines of the skylight.
  - `sectionFillId` (AttributeId): Fill of the section of the skylight; used unless useObjectSectionAttributes is true.
  - `sectionFillPen` (integer)
  - `sectionFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `sectionContourPen` (integer)
  - `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen of the overhead lines.
  - `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the overhead lines.
  - `belowViewLinePen` (integer): Pen of the uncut lines of the skylight.
  - `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the uncut lines.
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId): Surface of the skylight (API_OpeningBaseType::mat); used unless useObjectMaterials is true.
  - `useObjectPens` (boolean): Use the pens defined in the library part instead of 'pen'.
  - `useObjectLineTypes` (boolean): Use the line types defined in the library part instead of 'lineTypeId'.
  - `useObjectMaterials` (boolean): Use the surfaces defined in the library part instead of 'surfaceId'.
  - `useObjectSectionAttributes` (boolean): Use the section attributes defined in the library part instead of 'sectionFillId' and the section pens.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateSkylightsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateSkylights.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateSkylights.py): Requests three skylights in single-plane and multi-plane roof owners. Creates the roofs first, then uses their IDs and global XY anchor positions. Automatic surface placement still needs verification in a running Archicad.

### ModifySkylights

Modifies Skylight elements: anchor position and anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display option, pens, line types, section fill and pens, surface and the use-the-library-part's-settings flags - the same settings CreateSkylights takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given settings change. Not written by this command: the owner roof or shell, the anchor level and the vertical link (Archicad places the skylight on its owner), the plane of a multi-plane roof it sits on, the dimension marker (a separate element) and the library part's own parameters (use SetGDLParametersOfElements). Archicad may set the elevation angle again from the owner.

  - `elevationAngle` (number): Elevation angle of the owner's surface at the skylight, in radians (API_SkylightType::elevationAngle). Archicad may set it again from the owner roof or shell.

### CreateRailings

Creates Railing elements along a reference polyline. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite, from an existing railing (templateElementId) or from the Railing tool defaults; Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateRailings

Parameters:

- `railingsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Railings.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `templateElementId` (ElementId): Optional existing Railing whose settings the new railing takes instead of the tool defaults (or the favorite): its node and segment settings, from which the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters are generated, its story visibility, pens, bottom offset, layer and home story. floorIndex, bottomOffset and height given here override them. The reference line of a railing cannot be changed through the Archicad API, so a railing is given a new reference line by creating it again with itself as templateElementId and deleting the old one.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the railing on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.
  - `bottomOffset` (number): Optional base height of the railing relative to the floor level. When omitted, the value of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.
  - `height` (number): Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `RailingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRailings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRailings.py): Creates a 1.1 m high railing along three edges of a balcony with CreateRailings, then a second one with its settings. The posts, rails, handrails and infill come from the Railing tool defaults, or from favoriteName. The second railing takes every setting of the first through templateElementId; the reference line of a railing cannot be changed, so this is also how a railing gets a new one (create it again with itself as the template, then delete the old one).

### CreateRailingsFromPolyline

Creates Railing elements along a 3D reference polyline: each node has its own elevation and segments can be arcs. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateRailingsFromPolyline

Parameters:

- `railingsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Railings.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.
  - `polylineCoordinates` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The nodes of the reference line of the railing. z is the elevation of the node relative to the floor level of the home story, so the railing can climb or descend along its segments.
  - `polylineArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional arc segments of the reference line. begIndex and endIndex are indices into polylineCoordinates and must be consecutive (endIndex = begIndex + 1).
  - `height` (number): Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.
  - `templateElementId` (ElementId): Optional existing Railing whose settings the new railing takes instead of the tool defaults (or the favorite), as in CreateRailings: its node and segment settings, from which the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters are generated, its story visibility, pens, layer and home story. floorIndex and height given here override them. With itself as template, a railing is given a new 3D reference line by creating it again and deleting the old one.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateRailingsFromPolylineComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRailingsFromPolyline.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateRailingsFromPolyline.py): Creates a railing that climbs 1 m along its second segment and ends in a quarter arc with CreateRailingsFromPolyline. z of each node is its elevation above the home story. The posts, rails and infill come from the Railing tool defaults, or from favoriteName.

### CreateCurtainWalls

Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateCurtainWalls

Parameters:

- `curtainWallsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Curtain Walls.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `templateElementId` (ElementId): Optional existing Curtain Wall whose settings the new curtain wall takes instead of the tool defaults (or the favorite): its frame and panel classes, pattern, surfaces, boundary and corner frames, height, home story and base, layer and slant angle. The fields given here override them. With itself as template, a curtain wall is given a reference line with more or fewer segments by creating it again and deleting the old one (see RecreateCurtainWalls).
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment, so two coordinates give a single-segment curtain wall.
  - `zCoordinate` (number): Optional Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. When omitted, the base level of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) relative to the floor is kept.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. When omitted, derived from zCoordinate if that is given, otherwise the current story.
  - `height` (number): Optional height of the curtain wall. When omitted, the height of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) is kept.
  - `angle` (number): Optional slant angle of the curtain wall plane in degrees, measured from the horizontal: 90 is vertical, less than 90 leans to the left of the reference line (seen from its first coordinate), more than 90 to the right. It is the value GetDetailsOfElements returns as angle. A slanted curtain wall needs a straight reference line (exactly 2 coordinates); height stays its vertical height, and zCoordinate the elevation of its reference line (Archicad raises the bottom of the panels by offset times the cosine of the angle). Give it even with a slanted favorite: Archicad does not take the slant of a favorite or of the tool defaults on creation, so without angle the curtain wall comes out vertical (seen in Archicad 29).
  - `primaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): Optional column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segment (the primary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.
  - `secondaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): Optional row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.
  - `cells` (array of CurtainWallPatternCell): Optional assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit. The unit repeats along and up the segment, so an assignment applies to every repetition of that cell. A cell not listed here keeps the assignment of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) when the pattern is unchanged, otherwise the assignment of the first default cell.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateCurtainWallsComponent`, `CurtainWallsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateCurtainWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateCurtainWalls.py): Creates a 6 m long, 3 m high curtain wall with 1.5 m wide columns and two rows with CreateCurtainWalls, and a second one slanted at 75 degrees. The frame and panel classes come from the Curtain Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName. angle is in degrees from the horizontal (90 is vertical, less leans to the left of the reference line); a slanted curtain wall needs a straight reference line, and height stays its vertical height.

### CreateAssociativeDimensions

Creates associative dimensions from explicit witness point references: linear by default, or cumulative, baseline or elevation dimensions (appearance). A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateAssociativeDimensions

Parameters:

- `dimensionsData` (array of object, required)
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight, textPen and textFrame for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new dimension on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the dimension gets the layer of the favorite or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `textHeight` (number): Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).
  - `textPen` (integer): Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).
  - `textFrame` (boolean): Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.
  - `textStyle` (DimensionTextStyle): Optional font and style of the dimension texts (font, bold, italic, underline, width factor, spacing factor), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName). Only the fields given are changed.
  - `appearance` (string ("Linear", "Cumulative", "Baseline", "Elevation")): Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.
  - `elevationOrigin` (DimensionOrigin): Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.
  - `elevationMarker` (DimensionElevationMarker): Optional marker of an Elevation dimension (Elevation dimension in the Dimension Settings); give any of its form, arrowAngle, arrowFilled, arrowUp and plusSign. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `linePen` (integer): Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.
  - `marker` (DimensionMarker): Optional marker at the witness points; give any of its type, pen and size. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `textPlacement` (DimensionTextPlacement): Optional text placement method of the dimension texts, as in the Dimension Settings; give any of its fields. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `defaultWitnessForm` (string ("None", "Small", "Large", "Fix")): Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.
  - `defaultWitnessVal` (number): Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.
  - `staticDimension` (boolean): Optional Static dimension checkbox of the Dimension Settings (API defStaticDim). A new dimension is not static without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. The witness points are written as given either way (by elementId or by coordinate).
  - `onlyDimensionText` (boolean): Optional: show only the dimension texts, without the dimension and witness lines (API onlyDimensionText). Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `openingHeightsInChain` (boolean): Optional opening heights in the dimension chain, from the Dimension Details panel of the Dimension Settings (API detailedHoleDim): the heights of the doors and windows dimensioned are shown with the chain. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `openingHeightsNominal` (boolean): Optional: the opening heights are the nominal heights, without the oversize (API nominalHoleDim; false: with the oversize). Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `layeredElementDimensions` (LayeredElementDimensions): Optional automatic dimensioning of layered (composite) elements. Give any of the three; the others stay as they are. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `referencePoint` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `direction` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `floorIndex` (number)
  - `witnessPoints` (array of AssociativeWitnessPoint, required)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateAssociativeDimensionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateAssociativeDimensions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateAssociativeDimensions.py): Creates a wall and dimensions its length with CreateAssociativeDimensions. The dimension follows the wall: inIndex 1 and 2 are the end points of the wall's reference line. A witness point given only by a coordinate is static. direction is the direction of the dimension line.

  - `openingHeightsInChain` (boolean): Optional opening heights in the dimension chain, from the Dimension Details panel of the Dimension Settings (API detailedHoleDim): the heights of the doors and windows dimensioned are shown with the chain. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `openingHeightsNominal` (boolean): Optional: the opening heights are the nominal heights, without the oversize (API nominalHoleDim; false: with the oversize). Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `layeredElementDimensions` (LayeredElementDimensions): Optional automatic dimensioning of layered (composite) elements. Give any of the three; the others stay as they are. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `sectionElementId` (ElementId): The identifier of a single section element. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

### CreateWallThicknessDimensions

Creates associative wall thickness dimensions for the given walls.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateWallThicknessDimensions

Parameters:

- `dimensionsData` (array of object, required)
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight, textPen and textFrame for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new dimension on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the dimension gets the layer of the favorite or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `textHeight` (number): Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).
  - `textPen` (integer): Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).
  - `textFrame` (boolean): Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.
  - `textStyle` (DimensionTextStyle): Optional font and style of the dimension texts (font, bold, italic, underline, width factor, spacing factor), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName). Only the fields given are changed.
  - `appearance` (string ("Linear", "Cumulative", "Baseline", "Elevation")): Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.
  - `elevationOrigin` (DimensionOrigin): Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.
  - `elevationMarker` (DimensionElevationMarker): Optional marker of an Elevation dimension (Elevation dimension in the Dimension Settings); give any of its form, arrowAngle, arrowFilled, arrowUp and plusSign. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `linePen` (integer): Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.
  - `marker` (DimensionMarker): Optional marker at the witness points; give any of its type, pen and size. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `textPlacement` (DimensionTextPlacement): Optional text placement method of the dimension texts, as in the Dimension Settings; give any of its fields. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `defaultWitnessForm` (string ("None", "Small", "Large", "Fix")): Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.
  - `defaultWitnessVal` (number): Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.
  - `staticDimension` (boolean): Optional Static dimension checkbox of the Dimension Settings (API defStaticDim). A new dimension is not static without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. The witness points are written as given either way (by elementId or by coordinate).
  - `onlyDimensionText` (boolean): Optional: show only the dimension texts, without the dimension and witness lines (API onlyDimensionText). Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `openingHeightsInChain` (boolean): Optional opening heights in the dimension chain, from the Dimension Details panel of the Dimension Settings (API detailedHoleDim): the heights of the doors and windows dimensioned are shown with the chain. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `openingHeightsNominal` (boolean): Optional: the opening heights are the nominal heights, without the oversize (API nominalHoleDim; false: with the oversize). Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `layeredElementDimensions` (LayeredElementDimensions): Optional automatic dimensioning of layered (composite) elements. Give any of the three; the others stay as they are. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `wallId` (ElementId, required)
  - `referencePoint` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `direction` (Coordinate2D, required)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

The dimension line runs across the wall (direction) through referencePoint.

### ModifyAssociativeDimensions

Changes the settings of existing linear dimensions (the Dimension tool's elements, also in sections): the dimension type, the elevation origin and elevation marker, the line pen, the marker type, pen and size, the text placement method, the text height, pen, frame, font and style (bold, italic, underline) and the witness line form and value, with the same keys as the dimension creation commands. The text and witness line settings are applied to every witness point. witnessPointTexts sets the text of single witness points: the measured value or a custom text (which can contain the measured value), superscript, the text position and the reset to the automatic text position; GetDetailsOfElements reads them back with the same keys. Not written: the witness points, the dimension line position and direction (use MoveElements), the witness extension line and the hole and composite wall dimensioning settings.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyAssociativeDimensions

Parameters:

- `dimensionsWithDetails` (array of object, required): The linear dimensions to change (the Dimension tool's elements, also those placed in sections), each with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `witnessPointTexts` (array of DimensionWitnessPointText): Optional texts of single witness points, as the dimension text of a selected witness point in Archicad: the measured value or a custom text, superscript, and the text's position (moved and fixed, or reset to the automatic position). Only the given fields of the given witness points are changed. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back for every witness point with the same keys (witnessPointTexts), so the list read can be sent back; GetDimensionData reads them too.
  - `textHeight` (number): Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).
  - `textPen` (integer): Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName).
  - `textFrame` (boolean): Optional frame around the dimension texts (true: framed, false: not framed), applied to every witness point. Without it a new dimension gets the Dimension tool's setting.
  - `textStyle` (DimensionTextStyle): Optional font and style of the dimension texts (font, bold, italic, underline, width factor, spacing factor), applied to every witness point (on creation after favoriteName). Only the fields given are changed.
  - `appearance` (string ("Linear", "Cumulative", "Baseline", "Elevation")): Optional dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings. A new dimension is Linear without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. Elevation gives level marks, e.g. on a vertical chain in a section.
  - `elevationOrigin` (DimensionOrigin): Optional level an Elevation dimension measures from. A new dimension gets the one of favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults without it.
  - `elevationMarker` (DimensionElevationMarker): Optional marker of an Elevation dimension (Elevation dimension in the Dimension Settings); give any of its form, arrowAngle, arrowFilled, arrowUp and plusSign. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `linePen` (integer): Optional pen of the dimension and witness lines.
  - `marker` (DimensionMarker): Optional marker at the witness points; give any of its type, pen and size. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `textPlacement` (DimensionTextPlacement): Optional text placement method of the dimension texts, as in the Dimension Settings; give any of its fields. The others stay as they are (on creation: as favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults give them).
  - `defaultWitnessForm` (string ("None", "Small", "Large", "Fix")): Optional witness line form, as in the Dimension Settings, applied to every witness point.
  - `defaultWitnessVal` (number): Optional value that goes with the witness line form, in meters (for Fix the length of the witness lines), applied to every witness point.
  - `staticDimension` (boolean): Optional Static dimension checkbox of the Dimension Settings (API defStaticDim). A new dimension is not static without it, whatever favoriteName or the Dimension tool defaults say. The witness points are written as given either way (by elementId or by coordinate).
  - `onlyDimensionText` (boolean): Optional: show only the dimension texts, without the dimension and witness lines (API onlyDimensionText). Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `openingHeightsInChain` (boolean): Optional opening heights in the dimension chain, from the Dimension Details panel of the Dimension Settings (API detailedHoleDim): the heights of the doors and windows dimensioned are shown with the chain. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `openingHeightsNominal` (boolean): Optional: the opening heights are the nominal heights, without the oversize (API nominalHoleDim; false: with the oversize). Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.
  - `layeredElementDimensions` (LayeredElementDimensions): Optional automatic dimensioning of layered (composite) elements. Give any of the three; the others stay as they are. Without it a new dimension gets the setting of favoriteName or of the Dimension tool defaults.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyAssociativeDimensions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyAssociativeDimensions.py): Creates a linear dimension, then changes its pens, marker, texts and witness lines with ModifyAssociativeDimensions. The keys are the ones the dimension creation commands take, and GetDetailsOfElements returns them, so the settings read from one dimension can be written to others. The text settings (height, pen, frame and textStyle: font, bold/italic/underline, width factor) and the witness line settings are applied to every witness point; witnessPointTexts changes the text of single witness points (here the second one gets a custom text, which GetDimensionData reads back). In a custom text, {MeasuredValue} stands for the measured value (Archicad 26 and later), so "approx. {MeasuredValue}" adds a prefix to it. Run it with a floor plan window active.

### GetDimensionData

Gets the data of existing dimension chains: the line pen, the marker type, pen and size, the text placement method and the default witness line, and per witness point the coordinates, measured value, witness line, the text height, pen, frame, font and style, and the text content (measured value or custom text), superscript and whether the text was moved by hand.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDimensionData

Parameters:

- `elements` (array of object, required): The identifier of the dimension elements.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)

Returns:

- `dimensionsData` (array of DimensionDataOrError, required)

Grasshopper: `GetDimensionDataComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetDimensionData.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetDimensionData.py): Prints the pens, markers and witness points of every linear dimension with GetDimensionData. Needs at least one Dimension. The witness point fields are the ones CreateAssociativeDimensions takes, so a dimension placed by hand can be read to rebuild it.

### GetOpeningTransformations

Gets the placement of Opening elements, Windows, Doors and Skylights without changing them: a global-to-local transformation matrix, its inverse, and the origin and axes in world coordinates derived from the inverse. For Windows, Doors and Skylights the local-to-global matrix is the one Archicad returns, and mirrored ones give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). For Opening elements it is built from the opening geometry (Archicad 29 and later): origin at the anchor point, the X and Y axes of the opening and Z = X × Y, which points against the extrusion direction. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetOpeningTransformations

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)

Returns:

- `openingTransformations` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The transformation of each given Opening, or an error, in the order of the input elements.

Grasshopper: `GetOpeningTransformationsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetOpeningTransformations.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetOpeningTransformations.py): Prints the placement (transformation matrices, origin and axes) of every window with GetOpeningTransformations. Needs at least one Window; Doors, Skylights and Openings work the same way (Openings from Archicad 29). Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### CreateZones

Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same zone settings as ModifyZones (name, number, category, zone stamp, stamp pen, levels, letter size (roomLSize, in millimetres), contour line, cover fill, 3D surface, polygon display and area reduction), applied by the same helpers; the polygon or reference point, and the layer (layerIndex), are only set here. An item whose area would overlap an existing Zone on the same story fails with an error naming that Zone instead of opening Archicad's modal overlap warning, unless its allowOverlap is true.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.8. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateZones

Parameters:

- `zonesData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Zones.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `floorIndex` (number): Optional story index of the new zone. An automatic zone (geometry.referencePosition) is found around its reference point on this story, which is made active in the floor plan while the zone is created; the previously active story is restored afterwards.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
  - `name` (string, required): Name of the zone.
  - `numberStr` (string, required): Zone number.
  - `categoryAttributeId` (AttributeId): The identifier of the zone category attribute.
  - `stampPosition` (Coordinate2D): Position of the origin of the zone stamp.
  - `stampAngle` (number): Optional zone stamp rotation angle in radians.
  - `fixedStampAngle` (boolean): If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.
  - `contourLine` (ZoneContourLine): Optional contour line of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.
  - `coverFill` (ZoneCoverFill): Optional cover fill of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.
  - `surface` (ZoneSurface): Optional 3D surface of the zone (the Model panel). Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.
  - `polygonDisplay` (ZonePolygonDisplay): Optional zone polygon display: Gross uses the reference line of the bounding walls, Net their inner edges. Only has an effect for a zone whose boundary is the reference line of the walls. When omitted, the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults is kept.
  - `stampPen` (ZoneStampPen): Optional pen of the zone stamp. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.
  - `reducePercent` (ZoneReducePercent): Optional percentage the calculated area of the zone is reduced by; 0 means no reduction. When omitted, the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults is kept.
  - `allowOverlap` (boolean): Optional, defaults to false. Archicad answers a new zone whose area overlaps an existing zone on the same story with a modal warning dialog that blocks the API until it is dismissed, so by default such an item fails with an error naming the overlapping zone and no element is created for it. Set it to true to skip this check and create the zone anyway; the dialog may then appear. Zones that only touch (a shared edge or corner) do not overlap; curved edges are checked by their chords, and an automatic zone counts as overlapping when its referencePosition lies inside an existing zone.
  - `height` (number): Optional height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height); when omitted, the height and top link of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults are kept. Do not combine with relativeTopStory.
  - `bottomOffset` (number): Optional base level of the zone relative to its home story level.
  - `topOffset` (number): Optional offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `relativeTopStory` (number): Optional top link: non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not combine with height.
  - `floorThickness` (number): Optional thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.
  - `roomLSize` (number): Optional letter size of the zone (roomLSize of the Archicad API) in millimetres, not in metres like the other lengths. The zone stamps of the current Archicad libraries size their texts with their own parameters (GetGDLParametersOfElements, SetGDLParametersOfElements), so this value may not change how the stamp looks.
  - `geometry` (ZoneCreationGeometry, required)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateZonesComponent`, `ZonesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateZones.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateZones.py): Creates a 6 m x 5 m zone named Office from its outline with CreateZones, with its contour line drawn. A zone that would overlap an existing zone on the same story fails with an error instead (unless allowOverlap is true). Give 'geometry': {'referencePosition': {'x': ..., 'y': ...}} instead to create an automatic zone in the room around that point. contourLine and coverFill take the same keys in ModifyZones; fields left out keep the Zone tool defaults.

### CreatePolylines

Creates Polyline elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.5. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreatePolylines

Parameters:

- `polylinesData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Polylines. The settings left out come from the Polyline tool defaults, or from the favorite given by favoriteName.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new polyline. Polylines have no Element ID in Archicad 29: Archicad refuses it with error -2130313103 (APIERR_BADELEMENTTYPE, element has no info string), and the item then answers with that error and creates no polyline. Leave it out unless your Archicad version keeps it (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as id).
  - `floorInd` (number): The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index to place the polyline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.
  - `linePenIndex` (integer): Pen index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter.
  - `lineTypeIndex` (integer): Line type attribute index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, ignored when lineTypeId is given.
  - `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): Optional line type attribute of the polyline contour, as CreateLineElements and SetDetailsOfElements take it and GetDetailsOfElements returns it. Takes precedence over lineTypeIndex.
  - `roomSeparator` (boolean): Is this a zone boundary line? Optional parameter.
  - `drawSegmentMode` (PolylineDrawSegmentMode)
  - `startArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional arrowhead at the start. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; by default the tool's (or the favorite's) arrowhead is kept.
  - `endArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional arrowhead at the end. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; by default the tool's (or the favorite's) arrowhead is kept.
  - `linkedArrowAttributes` (LinkedArrowAttributes): Optional: link (true) or unlink (false) the size and pen of the two arrowheads. By default the tool's (or the favorite's) setting is kept, and ends given a different size or pen are unlinked.
  - `penWeightMm` (number): Optional pen weight override in mm, greater than 0; -1 uses the weight of the pen.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the polyline.
  - `arcs` (array of PolyArc): The arcs of the polyline.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreatePolylinesComponent`, `PolylinesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreatePolylines.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreatePolylines.py): Creates a polyline of two straight segments and one arc segment with CreatePolylines. arcAngle is in radians; arcs refer to the indices of the coordinates. drawSegmentMode Continuous runs the line type's dashes over the whole polyline instead of restarting them on every segment (SegmentBySegment).

### ModifyPolylines

Changes existing Polyline elements with the keys CreatePolylines takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns: the pen, the line type, zone boundary (roomSeparator), the dash mode (drawSegmentMode), the arrowheads at both ends, and the polygon (coordinates with its arcs, replaced as a whole; the polyline keeps its GUID). Only the given settings are changed. With databaseId the polylines are looked for in that database, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout. The polyline is read back, so a value Archicad did not keep is reported as a failure.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyPolylines

Parameters:

- `polylinesWithDetails` (array of object, required): The Polylines to change, each with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed; the keys are those CreatePolylines takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns. coordinates replaces the whole polygon, with its arcs. The pen weight override (penWeightMm of CreatePolylines) is not taken: Archicad did not keep a pen weight changed on an existing polyline.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `linePenIndex` (integer): Pen index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter.
  - `lineTypeIndex` (integer): Line type attribute index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, ignored when lineTypeId is given.
  - `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): Optional line type attribute of the polyline contour, as CreateLineElements and SetDetailsOfElements take it and GetDetailsOfElements returns it. Takes precedence over lineTypeIndex.
  - `roomSeparator` (boolean): Is this a zone boundary line? Optional parameter.
  - `drawSegmentMode` (PolylineDrawSegmentMode)
  - `startArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional new arrowhead at the start. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; the type, size and pen left out are kept.
  - `endArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional new arrowhead at the end. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; the type, size and pen left out are kept.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D): The new points of the polyline, replacing all of its points, as CreatePolylines takes them and GetDetailsOfElements returns them. Optional parameter.
  - `arcs` (array of PolyArc): The arcs of the new polygon, with indices into coordinates (endIndex is begIndex + 1). Only taken with coordinates; without it the new polygon has straight segments only.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database the polylines are in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return), as CreatePolylines takes it. The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the polylines are looked for in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is changed and the call fails.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyPolylines.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyPolylines.py): Creates a polyline, then changes its pen, dash mode, end arrowhead and points with ModifyPolylines. The settings have the keys CreatePolylines takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns; only the given ones are changed. coordinates replaces all the points of the polyline (arcs only come with it); the polyline keeps its GUID.

Creates Arc elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateArcs

Parameters:

- `arcsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Arcs.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new arc. Arcs have no Element ID in Archicad 29: Archicad refuses it with error -2130313103 (APIERR_BADELEMENTTYPE, element has no info string), and the item then answers with that error and creates no arc. Leave it out unless your Archicad version keeps it (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as id).
  - `floorInd` (number): The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index to place the arc on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.
  - `origin` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `radius` (number, required)
  - `begAngle` (number, required): Beginning angle of the arc in radians.
  - `endAngle` (number, required): End angle of the arc in radians.
  - `angle` (number): Optional angle of the ellipse's 'a' axis in radians. Defaults to 0.0.
  - `ratio` (number): Optional 'a/b' ratio of the ellipse, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it. Defaults to 1.0, a circular arc.
  - `reflected` (boolean): Optional: is the ellipse reflected onto its smaller axis? By default the tool's (or the favorite's) setting is kept.
  - `startArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional arrowhead at the start. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; by default the tool's (or the favorite's) arrowhead is kept.
  - `endArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional arrowhead at the end. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; by default the tool's (or the favorite's) arrowhead is kept.
  - `linkedArrowAttributes` (LinkedArrowAttributes): Optional: link (true) or unlink (false) the size and pen of the two arrowheads. By default the tool's (or the favorite's) setting is kept, and ends given a different size or pen are unlinked.
  - `roomSeparator` (boolean): Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.
  - `linePenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.
  - `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `ArcsComponent`, `CreateArcsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateArcs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateArcs.py): Creates a half elliptic arc with a 2 m radius and an a/b ratio of 2 with CreateArcs. Angles are in radians, counterclockwise from the X axis. Leave out ratio (or give 1.0) for a circular arc; angle turns the ellipse's 'a' axis.
