### CreatePictures

Creates Picture elements from PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF or BMP images, given as a file path or as base64 text, at an exact size in model units: give the width, the height or both (one of them keeps the image's proportions). The image is placed by its anchor point at position, and can be rotated, mirrored and drawn with transparent white pixels. With databaseId the pictures are placed in that database, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout, instead of the current one. GetDetailsOfElements reads the settings of a placed picture.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreatePictures

Parameters:

- `picturesData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Pictures.
  - `path` (string): The full path of a PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF or BMP image file. The image is copied into the project: the picture does not change when the file changes or is deleted later.
  - `imageData` (string): The PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF or BMP image file as base64 text, instead of path.
  - `name` (string): Optional name of the picture. By default the file name of path, or empty for imageData.
  - `position` (Coordinate2D, required): Where the anchor point of the picture is placed, in model units (on a layout in layout units).
  - `anchorPoint` (PictureAnchorPoint): The point of the picture's box that is placed at position and that the picture is rotated around. BottomLeft by default.
  - `width` (number): The width of the picture in model units. When only height is given, the width keeps the proportions of the image.
  - `height` (number): The height of the picture in model units. When only width is given, the height keeps the proportions of the image.
  - `angle` (number): The rotation angle of the picture in radians, around its anchor point. 0 by default.
  - `mirrored` (boolean): Mirror the picture to its local vertical axis. false by default.
  - `transparent` (boolean): Draw the white pixels of the picture transparent. false by default.
  - `floorInd` (number): The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index to place the picture on. Optional parameter, by default the layer of the Picture tool defaults is used.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database to create the pictures in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the pictures are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreatePictures.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreatePictures.py): Places a picture 4 m wide with CreatePictures (the height keeps the image's proportions) and reads its settings back with GetDetailsOfElements. A scanned plan is placed the same way from its file: {'path': 'C:/Scans/site_plan.png', ...}.

### CreateHatches

Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters. A hatch can have holes, in the same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts for hatches, and takes its fill orientation, fill category (drafting, cut or cover), contour pen and line type, background (a pen, transparent or the window background) and the percentage it subtracts from the zone area in the same call.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHatches

Parameters:

- `hatchesData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Hatches. The settings left out come from the Fill tool defaults, or from the favorite given by favoriteName.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `floorInd` (number): The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index to place the hatch on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the hatch outline. The first point may be repeated at the end, as in the closed outline GetDetailsOfElements returns; that last point is then ignored.
  - `arcs` (array of PolyArc): The arcs of the hatch outline.
  - `holes` (Holes2D): Optional holes of the hatch, each with its polygonOutline and optional polygonArcs (arc indices are relative to the hole's own outline). The same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts and GetDetailsOfElements returns for hatches.
  - `contourPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the contour; 0 switches the contour off.
  - `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Optional line type of the contour.
  - `fillPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the fill. It switches off the RGB color of the fill foreground (foregroundColor), unless that is given too.
  - `fillBackgroundPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the fill background; 0 makes the background transparent and -1 gives it the window background color. It switches off the RGB color of the fill background (backgroundColor), unless that is given too.
  - `foregroundColor` (ColorRGB): Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill foreground, used instead of fillPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillPenIndex when both are given. The same format as the colors returned by GetZoneCategories and GetPenTables.
  - `backgroundColor` (ColorRGB): Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill background, used instead of fillBackgroundPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillBackgroundPenIndex when both are given.
  - `fillId` (AttributeId): Optional fill attribute. Given without buildingMaterialId, it makes the hatch a fill hatch; given with it, the hatch keeps its type (fill or building material) and both are written.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): Optional building material attribute, whose cut fill the hatch shows. Given without fillId, it makes the hatch a building material hatch.
  - `roomSpecial` (integer): The percentage (1 to 100) of the hatch's area subtracted from the area of the zone it lies in (Subtract from zone area); a negative value switches it off.
  - `showArea` (boolean): Optional: show the area text of the hatch.
  - `fillOrientation` (HatchOrientation): Optional orientation, origin and distortion of the fill pattern, as SetDetailsOfElements writes it. Omitted properties keep the current ones (the tool defaults for a new hatch). A given origin detaches the fill from the project origin, and a Global fill becomes Rotated unless a type is given as well. Archicad ignores the orientation of Solid fills.
  - `fillCategory` (HatchFillCategory): Optional fill category: Drafting, Cut or Cover.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateHatchesComponent`, `FillsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateHatches.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateHatches.py): Creates a 4 m x 4 m hatch with a 1 m x 1 m hole and a red foreground with CreateHatches. Don't repeat the first point at the end of the outline. Colors are RGB values between 0 and 1. The fill pattern is rotated by 45 degrees in the same call, the hatch is a cut fill, and its background is transparent (background pen 0; -1 is the window background color).

### ModifyHatches

Changes existing Hatch (Fill) elements with the keys CreateHatches takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns: the contour pen and line type, the fill pen and background pen or their RGB colors, the fill or building material, the fill category, the fill orientation, the area text and the percentage subtracted from the zone area, and the polygon (coordinates with its arcs and holes, replaced as a whole; the hatch keeps its GUID). Only the given settings are changed. With databaseId the hatches are looked for in that database, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout. The hatch is read back, so a value Archicad did not keep is reported as a failure.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyHatches

Parameters:

- `hatchesWithDetails` (array of object, required): The Hatches (Fills) to change, each with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed; the keys are those CreateHatches takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns. coordinates replaces the whole polygon, with its arcs and holes.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D): The new outline of the hatch, replacing the whole polygon, as CreateHatches takes it. The first point may be repeated at the end, as in the closed outline GetDetailsOfElements returns; that last point is then ignored. Optional parameter.
  - `arcs` (array of PolyArc): The arcs of the new outline, with indices into coordinates. Only taken with coordinates; without it the new outline has straight edges only.
  - `holes` (Holes2D): The holes of the new polygon, each with its polygonOutline and optional polygonArcs (arc indices are relative to the hole's own outline), in the format GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only taken with coordinates; without it the new polygon has no holes.
  - `contourPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the contour; 0 switches the contour off.
  - `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Optional line type of the contour.
  - `fillPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the fill. It switches off the RGB color of the fill foreground (foregroundColor), unless that is given too.
  - `fillBackgroundPenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index for the fill background; 0 makes the background transparent and -1 gives it the window background color. It switches off the RGB color of the fill background (backgroundColor), unless that is given too.
  - `foregroundColor` (ColorRGB): Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill foreground, used instead of fillPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillPenIndex when both are given. The same format as the colors returned by GetZoneCategories and GetPenTables.
  - `backgroundColor` (ColorRGB): Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill background, used instead of fillBackgroundPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillBackgroundPenIndex when both are given.
  - `fillId` (AttributeId): Optional fill attribute. Given without buildingMaterialId, it makes the hatch a fill hatch; given with it, the hatch keeps its type (fill or building material) and both are written.
  - `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): Optional building material attribute, whose cut fill the hatch shows. Given without fillId, it makes the hatch a building material hatch.
  - `roomSpecial` (integer): The percentage (1 to 100) of the hatch's area subtracted from the area of the zone it lies in (Subtract from zone area); a negative value switches it off.
  - `showArea` (boolean): Optional: show the area text of the hatch.
  - `fillOrientation` (HatchOrientation): Optional orientation, origin and distortion of the fill pattern, as SetDetailsOfElements writes it. Omitted properties keep the current ones (the tool defaults for a new hatch). A given origin detaches the fill from the project origin, and a Global fill becomes Rotated unless a type is given as well. Archicad ignores the orientation of Solid fills.
  - `fillCategory` (HatchFillCategory): Optional fill category: Drafting, Cut or Cover.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database the hatches are in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return), as CreateHatches takes it. The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the hatches are looked for in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is changed and the call fails.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyHatches.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyHatches.py): Creates a 4 m x 4 m hatch, then gives it a hole, a red background and a cut fill category with ModifyHatches. The settings have the keys CreateHatches takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns; only the given ones are changed. coordinates replaces the whole polygon (arcs and holes only come with it); the hatch keeps its GUID. Colors are RGB values between 0 and 1.

### CreateSplines

Creates Spline elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.6. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateSplines

Parameters:

- `splinesData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Splines. Only auto-smoothed curves are supported (bezier handle positions are calculated automatically by Archicad from the point positions).
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new spline. Splines have no Element ID in Archicad 29: Archicad refuses it with error -2130313103 (APIERR_BADELEMENTTYPE, element has no info string), and the item then answers with that error and creates no spline. Leave it out unless your Archicad version keeps it (GetDetailsOfElements returns it as id).
  - `floorInd` (number): The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Layer attribute index to place the spline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the spline points. Do not repeat the first point at the end even for a closed spline.
  - `closed` (boolean): Is this a closed curve? Optional, defaults to false.
  - `startArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional arrowhead at the start. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; by default the tool's (or the favorite's) arrowhead is kept.
  - `endArrow` (LineArrowhead): Optional arrowhead at the end. Given, it is shown unless its visible is false; by default the tool's (or the favorite's) arrowhead is kept.
  - `linkedArrowAttributes` (LinkedArrowAttributes): Optional: link (true) or unlink (false) the size and pen of the two arrowheads. By default the tool's (or the favorite's) setting is kept, and ends given a different size or pen are unlinked.
  - `roomSeparator` (boolean): Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.
  - `linePenIndex` (integer): Optional pen index. By default the current pen is used.
  - `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): Optional line type attribute. By default the current line type is used.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database to create the elements in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are created in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateSplinesComponent`, `SplinesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateSplines.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateSplines.py): Creates an open and a closed spline through the given points with CreateSplines. Archicad smooths the curve through the points itself.

### CreateObjects

Creates Object elements based on the given parameters. A library part named in libraryPartName starts from its own default size and GDL parameters, not from those of the part the Object tool holds; the dimensions and the GDL parameters given (by name, in parameters) override them. layerIndex places the element on a layer. With databaseId the objects are placed in that database, e.g. a worksheet, instead of the current one.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateObjects

Parameters:

- `objectsData` (array of object, required): Array of data to create Objects.
  - `libraryPartName` (string, required): The name of the library part to use.
  - `coordinates` (Coordinate3D, required)
  - `dimensions` (Dimensions3D)
  - `angle` (number)
  - `pen` (integer)
  - `lineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId): Material/Surface override (API_ObjectType.mat).
  - `sectionFillId` (AttributeId)
  - `sectionFillPen` (integer)
  - `sectionFillBackgroundPen` (integer)
  - `sectionContourPen` (integer)
  - `useObjectPens` (boolean)
  - `useObjectLineTypes` (boolean)
  - `useObjectMaterials` (boolean)
  - `useObjectSectionAttributes` (boolean)
  - `reflected` (boolean)
  - `useFixSize` (boolean)
  - `fixPoint` (integer): 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).
  - `offset` (Coordinate2D): Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType.
  - `useFixedAngle` (boolean): Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean)
  - `visibility` (StoryVisibility)
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `parameters` (array of object): Optional GDL parameters to set by name, after dimensions. The value is a number, a boolean or a string; array parameters are not supported. A or B also set the size. An unknown name or a value of the wrong type fails the item, and nothing is created for it.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database to place the elements in, e.g. a worksheet or a detail (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return), for a legend of symbols. The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are placed in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateObjectsComponent`, `ObjectsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateObjects.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateObjects.py): Places the first Object library part of the loaded libraries at the origin with CreateObjects, then once more in a new worksheet. Give any loaded library part name in libraryPartName, e.g. one listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts. The object starts from the library part's own default size and parameters; 'dimensions' and the GDL 'parameters' given (by name, e.g. A and B, the size) override them, and 'layerIndex' puts it on a layer (here the first layer of the project). With 'databaseId' (here the one CreateWorksheets returns) the object is placed in that database, e.g. for a legend of symbols in a worksheet, and the front window stays as it is. The example worksheet is deleted again at the end.

  - `reflected` (boolean)
  - `useFixSize` (boolean)
  - `fixPoint` (integer): 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).
  - `offset` (Coordinate2D): Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType.
  - `useFixedAngle` (boolean): Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean)
  - `visibility` (StoryVisibility)
  - `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
  - `lightColor` (ColorRGB): Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state, as opposed to the color) does not have this problem.
  - `lightIsOn` (boolean)
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.
  - `id` (string): Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.
  - `parameters` (array of object): Optional GDL parameters to set by name, after dimensions. The value is a number, a boolean or a string; array parameters are not supported. A or B also set the size. An unknown name or a value of the wrong type fails the item, and nothing is created for it.
  - `layerIndex` (integer): Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database to place the elements in, e.g. a worksheet or a detail (see GetDatabases, or the databaseId CreateWorksheets and CreateDetails return), for a legend of symbols. The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the elements are placed in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is created and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateLampsComponent`, `LampsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateLamps.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateLamps.py): Places the first Lamp library part of the loaded libraries 2.5 m above the floor, switched on, with CreateLamps. Give any loaded lamp library part name in libraryPartName, e.g. one listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts. The lamp starts from the library part's own default size and parameters; GDL 'parameters' given by name override them, and 'layerIndex' puts it on a layer (here the first layer of the project). A top-level 'databaseId' (e.g. the one CreateWorksheets returns) places the lamps in that database instead of the current one, as in the CreateObjects example.

### GetGridElementDefaults

Returns the Grid Tool defaults: library part, size and GDL parameters of a new grid element. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetGridElementDefaults

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `elementId` (ElementId): The grid element. The zero GUID for the tool defaults.
- `variation` (string, required): Four-character variation of the object: 'GREL' for a grid element.
- `floorIndex` (integer, required): Home story index.
- `layerIndex` (integer, required): Layer attribute index.
- `pos` (Coordinate2D, required): Insertion point: the start of the grid line.
- `angle` (number, required): Direction of the grid line in radians.
- `length` (number, required): Length of the grid line: the GDL parameter AC_Length of the Grid Tool's grid marker, or the object's A size for a library part without it.
- `xRatio` (number, required): The object's xRatio as stored: its A size with useXYFixSize on, otherwise the A size divided by the library part's own A.
- `yRatio` (number, required): The object's yRatio as stored, like xRatio for the B size.
- `useXYFixSize` (boolean, required): Whether xRatio and yRatio hold the sizes themselves.
- `level` (number, required): Elevation of the object from its home story.
- `libInd` (integer, required): Library part index.
- `libraryPartName` (string, required): Localized name of the library part.
- `parameters` (array of object, required): GDL parameters, separators left out. Only when requested.
  - `name` (string, required)
  - `displayName` (string, required)
  - `type` (string, required): Integer, Length, Angle, RealNum, LightSwitch, ColorRGB, Intensity, LineType, Material, FillPattern, PenColor, String, Boolean, Title, BuildingMaterial, Profile, Dictionary or Unknown.
  - `value` (any): Number for numeric and boolean types, string for String and Title. Not given for arrays.
  - `dimension1` (integer): First dimension of an array parameter.
  - `dimension2` (integer): Second dimension of an array parameter.

Grasshopper: `GetGridElementDefaultsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGridElementDefaults.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetGridElementDefaults.py): Prints the library part, size and GDL parameters a new grid element gets from the Grid Tool defaults, with GetGridElementDefaults. Requires Archicad 26 or later.
