  - `lightColor` (ColorRGB): Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state, as opposed to the color) does not have this problem.
  - `lightIsOn` (boolean)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `LampsComponent`, `ModifyLampsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyLamps.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyLamps.py): Places a lamp, then raises it, switches it off and makes its light blue with ModifyLamps. The lamp is the first Lamp library part of the loaded libraries. Colors are RGB values between 0 and 1.

### ModifyTexts

Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyTexts

Parameters:

- `textsWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Text elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content (one paragraph per line, as SetDetailsOfElements does), and on a multi-run text applies that style to every run; a text that wraps keeps its wrap width through the rebuild unless the same item gives a width. The other style fields and a width leave the content as it is.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `coordinate` (Coordinate3D): The new placement position. As in CreateTexts, the z value selects the floor when floorIndex is omitted.
  - `position` (Coordinate2D): The new placement position as GetDetailsOfElements reads it (position), so a text read can be sent back: the same as coordinate without z, so the text stays on its floor (floorIndex still moves it). Ignored when coordinate is given.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Optional. Moves the text to this floor; when omitted and a coordinate is given, the floor is derived from its z value.
  - `text` (string): The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.
  - `runs` (array of TextRunDetails)
  - `style` (TextStyleSettableDetails)
  - `width` (number): Optional box width in mm (paper size, like height). Greater than 0 turns word wrap on: the text wraps within this width ('Wrap Text' in the Text settings, nonBreaking false). 0 turns word wrap off: the text is auto-width and grows with its content; on a wrapped text this rebuilds the content, so like a pen change it is refused for content with an autotext run. Given alone it leaves the content and its runs (and any autotext in them) as they are. When the content is rebuilt in the same item, the width is applied after the rebuild. When omitted, the current wrap setting is kept, also through a rebuild of the content. Read back by GetDetailsOfElements with the same key (width, 0 when word wrap is off), and as style.boxWidth with style.nonBreaking false.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyTextsComponent`, `TextsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyTexts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyTexts.py): Creates a text, then replaces its content, makes it bold and 5 mm high, and moves it with ModifyTexts. Then it gives the text a fixed width of 20 mm, so it wraps, without changing its content. Only the given fields change; text replaces the whole content (see ChangeTextContent to change a part). A text that wraps keeps its wrap width when its content or style is rebuilt; width 0 turns word wrap off.

### ModifyPictures

Modifies Picture elements: moves them to a new position, resizes them to a width and height in model units (one of them keeps the picture's proportions), changes the anchor point, the angle, mirrored, transparent and the name. Only the given settings are changed and the image stays as it is. Archicad cannot change a picture in place, so a changed picture is replaced by a new one with the same image, layer, story and ID, and the new elementId is returned; labels, dimensions, properties and classifications of the original are not carried over. With databaseId the pictures are looked for in that database, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout. GetDetailsOfElements reads the settings back.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyPictures

Parameters:

- `picturesWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Picture elements to modify, with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed; the others are left as they are. The image itself is not changed. Archicad cannot change a picture in place, so a picture with a change is replaced by a new picture with the same image, layer, story and ID, and the original is deleted: the new picture has a new elementId (returned in elements), and labels, dimensions, properties and classifications of the original are not carried over.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `position` (Coordinate2D): Where the anchor point of the picture is moved to, in model units (on a layout in layout units). When omitted, the anchor point stays where it is. GetDetailsOfElements reads it back with the same key, so the position read can be sent back.
  - `anchorPoint` (PictureAnchorPoint): The new anchor point: the point of the picture's box that is placed at position, that stays in place when the size changes, and that the picture is rotated around. When given without position, the picture's box stays where it is and only the anchor point changes; on a rotated picture the rotation is then around the new anchor point, which can move the picture. When omitted, the anchor point is kept.
  - `width` (number): The new width of the picture in model units. When only width is given, the height changes in proportion, so the picture keeps its current proportions.
  - `height` (number): The new height of the picture in model units. When only height is given, the width changes in proportion, so the picture keeps its current proportions.
  - `angle` (number): The new rotation angle of the picture in radians, around its anchor point.
  - `mirrored` (boolean): Mirror the picture to its local vertical axis. The picture's box stays where it is drawn.
  - `transparent` (boolean): Draw the white pixels of the picture transparent.
  - `name` (string): The new name of the picture.
- `databaseId` (DatabaseId): Optional database the pictures are in, e.g. a worksheet, a detail or a layout (see GetDatabases). The front window stays as it is: a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened is opened once on Archicad 27 and later, and the front window is brought back. Without it the pictures are looked for in the current database. If Archicad cannot switch to it, nothing is changed and the call fails.

Returns:

- `elements` (array of ElementIdOrError, required): One result per item of picturesWithDetails, in the same order. On success elementId is the picture's identifier after the change: a new one when a setting was changed (the picture is replaced), the given one when nothing was to change.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyPictures.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyPictures.py): Places a picture with CreatePictures, then with ModifyPictures scales it to 6 m wide around its center (the height keeps the proportions), rotates it by 90 degrees and makes its white pixels transparent, and reads its settings back with GetDetailsOfElements. Archicad cannot change a picture in place, so ModifyPictures replaces it and returns the new elementId.

### ModifyLabels

Modifies Label elements based on the given parameters: the text and its style, the symbol label's style, the leader line, and the leader line's coordinates, which move or re-point the label.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.9. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyLabels

Parameters:

- `labelsWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Label elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. The label's class (Text/Symbol) cannot be changed after creation. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content (one paragraph per line), which makes the label's text auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run label applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `text` (string): The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.
  - `runs` (array of TextRunDetails)
  - `style` (TextStyleSettableDetails)
  - `symbolStyle` (LabelSymbolStyleSettableDetails)
  - `leaderLine` (LabelLeaderLineSettableDetails)
  - `textWay` (LabelTextDirection): The new text direction, for a Text or a Symbol label. Refused together with symbolStyle.textWay.
  - `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The new begin coordinate of the leader line: the point the label points at (where the arrow is). Only the leader line's begin moves; the label's text or symbol stays where it is.
  - `midCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The new mid coordinate of the leader line (its break point).
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The new end coordinate of the leader line, where the label's text or symbol sits: the text or symbol moves by as much as this point moves. To move the whole label, give all three coordinates moved by the same offset. GetDetailsOfElements returns the current ones.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `LabelsComponent`, `ModifyLabelsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyLabels.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyLabels.py): Creates a wall with a text label, then changes the label's text, frame and arrow with ModifyLabels, and moves it. Only the given fields change. begCoordinate re-points the leader line; endCoordinate moves the text with the end of the leader line.

### ModifyCurtainWalls

Modifies Curtain Wall elements in place, keeping their GUID, properties and classifications: the height, the bottom elevation and story, the reference line (with the same number of segments), and the column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern with its cell assignments, in the fields of CreateCurtainWalls; the side of the reference line (flipped), the panel offset from the reference line and the nominal width; and the floor plan display settings GetDetailsOfElements reads: story visibility, display option, view depth, cut, uncut and overhead projection modes, and the pens and line types of the frame and panel cut lines and of the uncut and overhead lines.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCurtainWalls

Parameters:

- `curtainWallsWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Curtain Wall elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the others, and the frames and panels not affected by them, are left as they are. The fields are those of CreateCurtainWalls, plus flipped, offset and nominalWidth, so a curtain wall can be changed in place instead of being deleted and recreated, keeping its GUID, properties and classifications, and the floor plan display fields GetDetailsOfElements returns for a curtain wall, under the same names. Every given field is read back, and one Archicad did not apply fails the item.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D): The new 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates is one straight segment, so the number of coordinates must be the current number of segments plus one: the segments can be moved and resized, but not added or removed (a curved segment becomes straight).
  - `zCoordinate` (number): The new Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given too.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): The new home story index. On its own it moves the curtain wall to that story, keeping its bottom offset from the story; with zCoordinate it pins the story the bottom elevation is measured from.
  - `height` (number): The new height of the curtain wall. It is applied before the other fields and read back. When Archicad ignores it (Archicad 29 does), the top edges of the contours of the segments are moved to the new height instead. When neither applies it, the item fails and no other field is changed.
  - `flipped` (boolean): The new side of the reference line the curtain wall is on (API_CurtainWallType::flipped, the flipped value GetDetailsOfElements returns). Changing it mirrors the curtain wall to the other side of its reference line; the reference line itself stays where it is.
  - `offset` (number): The new offset of the panels from the reference line (API_CurtainWallType::offset, the offset value GetDetailsOfElements returns), e.g. 0.1 for 10 cm.
  - `nominalWidth` (number): The new nominal width (thickness) of the curtain wall (API_CurtainWallType::nominalWidth, the nominalWidth value GetDetailsOfElements returns).
  - `primaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): The new column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segments (the primary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.
  - `secondaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): The new row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.
  - `cells` (array of CurtainWallPatternCell): Assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit of every segment, as in CreateCurtainWalls. Without a pattern change, a cell not listed here keeps its current assignment; with one, it takes the assignment of the first current cell.
  - `visibility` (StoryVisibility): The stories the curtain wall is shown on (API_CurtainWallType::visibility), as GetDetailsOfElements returns it; for example only showOnHome true shows it on its home story only. Archicad only keeps it while isAutoOnStoryVisibility is false, so setting it without isAutoOnStoryVisibility also turns that off. The fields not given are false or 0. Confirmed live on Archicad 26 and 28 (#2529): showRelAbove 1 on a curtain wall in an empty project read back as 0, and the command then fails and names the visibility Archicad kept.
  - `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true, Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the vertical extent of the curtain wall and ignores a visibility given together with it.
  - `displayOption` (DisplayOption): The floor plan display of the curtain wall (API_CurtainWallType::displayOption).
  - `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation): How far the curtain wall is shown on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::viewDepthLimitation).
  - `cutProjectionMode` (ElemProjectionMode): Projection mode of the cut part of the curtain wall on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::cutProjectionMode).
  - `uncutProjectionMode` (ElemProjectionMode): Projection mode of the uncut part (below the cut plane) of the curtain wall on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::uncutProjectionMode).
  - `overheadProjectionMode` (ElemProjectionMode): Projection mode of the overhead part (above the cut plane) of the curtain wall on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::overheadProjectionMode).
  - `pen` (integer): The pen index of the curtain wall (API_CurtainWallType::pen).
  - `frameCutLinePen` (integer): Pen index of the cut part of the frames on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::frameCutLinePen). The frames only use it while useFrameTypesAttributes is false.
  - `frameCutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut part of the frames on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::frameCutLineType). The frames only use it while useFrameTypesAttributes is false.
  - `panelCutLinePen` (integer): Pen index of the cut part of the panels on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::panelCutLinePen). The panels only use it while usePanelTypesAttributes is false.
  - `panelCutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut part of the panels on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::panelCutLineType). The panels only use it while usePanelTypesAttributes is false.
  - `useFrameTypesAttributes` (boolean): True makes the frames use the attributes of their frame types instead of frameCutLinePen and frameCutLineTypeId. Confirmed live on Archicad 26 and 28 (#2529): false written on a new curtain wall read back as true, and the command then fails with useFrameTypesAttributes not applied.
  - `usePanelTypesAttributes` (boolean): True makes the panels use the attributes of their panel types instead of panelCutLinePen and panelCutLineTypeId.
  - `belowViewLinePen` (integer): Pen index of the uncut lines, the curtain wall's view below the cut plane on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::uncutLinePen).
  - `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the uncut lines, the curtain wall's view below the cut plane on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::uncutLineType).
  - `aboveViewLinePen` (integer): Pen index of the overhead lines, the curtain wall's view above the cut plane on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::overheadLinePen).
  - `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the overhead lines, the curtain wall's view above the cut plane on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::overheadLineType), for example a dashed one.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `CurtainWallsComponent`, `ModifyCurtainWallsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWalls.py): Creates a curtain wall, then makes it 4 m high with 1 m wide columns, flips it to the other side of its reference line and sets a 0.10 m panel offset with ModifyCurtainWalls. The curtain wall keeps its GUID, properties and classifications.

### ModifyCurtainWallFrames

EXPERIMENTAL. Modifies single Curtain Wall Frames by their GUID: the frame contour (a1, a2, b1, b2), the frame class and the frame type. The frame element itself is changed, and read back to check that Archicad applied the change. A frame given its own contour or type without a classIndex is made a customized frame (GetDetailsOfElements reports its type as Custom) when Archicad does not keep the change on a frame of a class.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCurtainWallFrames

Parameters:

- `framesWithDetails` (array of object, required): Curtain Wall Frames to modify (the GUIDs from GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements), with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed. EXPERIMENTAL.
  - `frameId` (ElementId, required)
  - `frameContour` (object): The contour of the frame, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it. Only the given keys are changed.
  - `classIndex` (integer): The frame class (classID) of the frame: 0 to 3 for the built-in classes, 4 and up for the frame classes of the owner curtain wall.
  - `type` (CurtainWallFrameObjectType): The object type of the frame (API_CWFrameObjectTypeID), which GetDetailsOfElements reads as objectType. Not the frame class that GetDetailsOfElements reads as type: that one is classIndex here.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyCurtainWallFramesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWallFrames.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWallFrames.py): EXPERIMENTAL: changes the contour and the type of the first frame of a new curtain wall with ModifyCurtainWallFrames. The frame is found by its GUID, which GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements returns.

### ModifyCurtainWallPanels

Assigns a panel class to single Curtain Wall Panels by their GUID; the panel takes the settings of the class (thickness, surfaces, building material, cut line, panel type). ACAPI_Element_Change does not take a panel on its own, so the change is written through the memo of the owner curtain wall, and read back to check that Archicad applied it.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCurtainWallPanels

Parameters:

- `panelsWithDetails` (array of object, required): Curtain Wall Panels to modify (the GUIDs from GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements), with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed.
  - `panelId` (ElementId, required)
  - `classIndex` (integer): The panel class to assign, numbered as Archicad numbers them (as in the cells of CreateCurtainWalls): 1 is the first panel class of the owner curtain wall (as listed in its Curtain Wall Settings), 2 the second and so on. The panel takes the settings of the class: its thickness, surfaces, building material, cut line and panel type (generic or GDL object). GetDetailsOfElements returns the classIndex and className of a panel.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWallPanels.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyCurtainWallPanels.py): Assigns a panel class to the first panel of a new curtain wall with ModifyCurtainWallPanels, then reads its class back. The panel is found by its GUID, which GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements returns. classIndex 1 is the first panel class of the curtain wall, 2 the second and so on, as listed in its Curtain Wall Settings.

### ModifyStairs

Modifies Stair elements in place, keeping their baseline and position: the flight width, total height, number of steps, riser height and going with their locks, the top link to a story with its offset, the Rules and Standards (each limit and whether it is applied), the headroom (generation method, height and left and right offset; read back, and one Archicad did not apply is reported as an error), the finish and structure visibility, the extra top and bottom treads, the walking line position and offset, the step numbering, the walking direction, the uniform finish, monolith and draining settings, and for the flights and the landings the tread and riser settings (presence, thickness, offset, nosing, riser cross section and position) and the structure of each side (presence, type, underside shape and thickness, the monolith data of a Monolith structure: thinning, thickness, bottom oversize, building material and fill, surfaces, pens, line types and drainings, and the stringer data of a Side structure: width, height above tread and how it is measured; the monolith and stringer data are read back, and one Archicad did not apply is reported as an error), and the floor plan display: whether it is Custom or by the Model View Options, and for the floor plan and the reflected ceiling plan separately the stories the stair is shown on and whether its walking line, numbering, up/down text, description and structure are shown, the symbol on each story (above, top, middle, bottom and below the relevant stories), the break line (angle, gap and position) and the line type, pen and symbol fill overrides, and the line types, pens and fills of the structure symbols per structure type and view (structureSymbols) and of the monolithic structure per view and visible or hidden part (monolithStructureSymbols), and which structures, fills and monolithic parts are shown on each range of the relevant stories, per view (structureVisibilityOnStories); these are read back, and one Archicad did not apply is reported as an error. CreateStairs accepts the same settings. Only the given settings are changed. Archicad solves the stair again within its baseline, so it may adjust the step values; read them back with GetDetailsOfElements. A given going (treadDepth) is pinned in the Rules and Standards as CreateStairs pins it, before the given rules are written. Not written by this command: the baseline with its landings and winders; the subelements (treads, risers, structures) take the per-part settings above and cannot be written one by one through the API; the boundaries and the walking lines GetDetailsOfElements reads, which Archicad lays out itself from the baseline and the flight width and which the API cannot write (here, in CreateStairs and in RecreateStairs an item that gives one is refused with an error that says so).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyStairs

Parameters:

- `stairsWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Stair elements to modify, with the settings to change. Only the given settings are changed; the baseline, the position and the omitted settings are kept.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `flightWidth` (number): The width of the flights.
  - `totalHeight` (number): The height of the stair relative to its bottom.
  - `stepNum` (integer): The number of steps (risers).
  - `riserHeight` (number): The height of each riser.
  - `treadDepth` (number): The length of each going. Pinned as a fixed going in the stair rules, as CreateStairs pins it: the going's minimum and maximum are both set to it and applied, and the standard's combined riser/going rules (2R+G, R+G, R/G) are no longer applied to this stair, so Archicad lays the steps out with this going (#2525).
  - `relativeTopStory` (integer): Links the top of the stair to a story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above); 0 unlinks it. With a top link Archicad computes totalHeight from the story levels and topOffset, so a totalHeight given in the same call is not kept. Archicad does not return the link when the stair is read, so GetDetailsOfElements does not report it; read the resulting totalHeight back instead.
  - `topOffset` (number): The offset of the top of the stair from the level of the linked top story (for example -0.15 for 15 cm below it). Only used when the stair's top is linked (relativeTopStory not 0).
  - `rules` (StairRules): The Rules and Standards of the stair: only the given limits and applied flags are written, the others are kept. Archicad lays the steps out within the applied limits, so read the riser count and going back with GetDetailsOfElements. In CreateStairs and ModifyStairs a treadDepth pins the going limits and releases the 2R+G, R+G and R/G rules first; the rules given here are written after that. An unknown key is refused, and ModifyStairs reads the given rules back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `headroom` (StairHeadroom): The headroom of the stair (Stair Settings > Headroom): only the given fields are written, the others are kept. An unknown key is refused, and ModifyStairs reads the given fields back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `treadDepthLocked` (boolean): Whether the going lengths are locked.
  - `totalHeightLocked` (boolean): Whether the total height is locked.
  - `finishVisible` (boolean): Whether the tread and riser finishes of the stair are shown; false models only the structure (e.g. a monolith). The treads and risers of each part can also be switched on and off with treads and risers.
  - `extraTopTread` (boolean): Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top.
  - `extraBottomTread` (boolean): Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom.
  - `walkingLinePosition` (string ("Left", "Right", "Center", "Auto")): Where the walking line runs on the flight: offset from the left or the right side (walkingLineOffset), centered, or placed by Archicad (Auto).
  - `walkingLineOffset` (number): The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names (Left or Right); not used with Center and Auto.
  - `walkingLineSymbolPosition` (string ("Auto", "Center", "Custom")): Where the symbol of the walking line is placed (API_StairType::walkLineSymbPos): by Archicad (Auto), centered, or where it was placed by hand (Custom).
  - `numberingType` (string ("Treads", "Risers")): Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers.
  - `inputDirection` (string ("Upward", "Inverse")): The walking direction along the baseline: upward from its first point, or inverse (downward).
  - `uniformFinish` (boolean): Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.
  - `uniformMonolithAttributes` (boolean): Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.
  - `uniformDrainings` (boolean): Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.
  - `structureVisibility` (boolean): Whether the structure of the stair is shown.
  - `stairDisplayType` (string ("Custom", "ByModelViewOptions")): Whether the floor plan display of the stair is set in the stair itself (Custom) or comes from the Model View Options (ByModelViewOptions). While it is ByModelViewOptions, Archicad may show the stair by the Model View Options instead of floorPlanLayout and reflectedCeilingPlanLayout; give Custom in the same call to use them.
  - `floorPlanLayout` (StairLayoutSettings): The floor plan display of the stair: the stories it is shown on, its visible components, the symbol on each story, the break line and the line type, pen and fill overrides. Independent of reflectedCeilingPlanLayout.
  - `reflectedCeilingPlanLayout` (StairLayoutSettings): The reflected ceiling plan display of the stair: the stories it is shown on, its visible components, the symbol on each story, the break line and the line type, pen and fill overrides. Independent of floorPlanLayout.
  - `structureSymbols` (array of StairStructureSymbolSettings): The line types, pens and fills of the structure symbol, per structure type (UnderStructure, Stringer) and view (FloorPlan, CeilingPlan), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given fields of the given items are changed; ModifyStairs reads them back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `monolithStructureSymbols` (array of StairMonolithStructureSymbolSettings): The line types, pens and fills of the monolithic structure's symbol, per view (FloorPlan, CeilingPlan) and part (Visible, Hidden), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given fields of the given items are changed; ModifyStairs reads them back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `structureVisibilityOnStories` (array of StairStructureVisibilitySettings): Which structure symbols are shown on which of the stair's relevant stories, per view (FloorPlan, CeilingPlan), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements returns: whether one representation is used on every story, and per story range the visible structures, fills and monolithic parts. Only the given fields of the given items are changed; ModifyStairs reads them back and reports one Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `treads` (array of object): The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back in treads.
  - `risers` (array of object): The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing). Only the given fields of the given parts are changed. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back in risers.
  - `structures` (array of object): The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side: the left and right side structures and the structure under the stair, with the keys GetDetailsOfElements reads in structures. Only the given fields of the given parts and sides are changed. ModifyStairs reads the given monolith and sideStair data back and reports a value Archicad did not apply as an error.
  - `leftBoundary` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the left boundary of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `rightBoundary` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the right boundary of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `walkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `customWalkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the custom walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `centerWalkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the center walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyStairsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyStairs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyStairs.py): Creates a straight stair, then changes its width, its walking line, its tread thickness, its structure and its floor plan display with ModifyStairs. Makes the flights monolithic with a smooth underside, numbers the steps on the risers, shows the stair on its home story only in the floor plan without the walking line, with the full symbol and no break mark on its bottom story, a break line 0.1 m wide at the floor plan cut plane and pen 7 for its lines, and on its home story and one story up in the reflected ceiling plan without the structure. Draws the hidden lines of the structure under the stair with pen 3 in the floor plan, and the contour of the hidden part of the monolithic structure with pen 3 too, and hides the hidden monolithic structure on the stories above the stair in the floor plan. Reads the stair back with GetDetailsOfElements, then deletes the stair it created.

### RecreateCurtainWalls

Recreates Curtain Wall elements on a new reference line with more or fewer segments, as CreateCurtainWalls takes it, because ModifyCurtainWalls can only keep the number of segments; or with a new height or slant angle, which Archicad does not apply to an existing slanted curtain wall through ACAPI_Element_Change (seen in Archicad 29). Without coordinates the old reference line is kept. The new curtain wall is created with the old one as templateElementId, so it gets its frame and panel classes, pattern, surfaces, boundary and corner frames, height, home story and base, layer and slant angle, unless height or angle is given; it also gets its Element ID, renovation status, classifications, element categories, property values, solid element operations and trims, and the old curtain wall is then deleted. Each curtain wall is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for that curtain wall. The result lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group). Frames and panels changed one by one on the old curtain wall are generated again from its classes and pattern, as when it is drawn again in Archicad.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateCurtainWalls

Parameters:

- `curtainWalls` (array of object, required): The curtain walls to recreate on a new reference line, with a new height or with a new slant. Give at least one of coordinates, height and angle.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The curtain wall to recreate.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D): Optional new reference line on the floor plan, as CreateCurtainWalls takes it: one segment per pair of consecutive points, so more or fewer points than the old curtain wall has add or remove segments. A slanted curtain wall needs exactly 2 points. When omitted, the old curtain wall's reference line is kept, the points GetDetailsOfElements returns as its referenceLine.
  - `height` (number): Optional new height, as CreateCurtainWalls takes it: the vertical height, also of a slanted curtain wall. When omitted, the old curtain wall's height is kept. Archicad does not apply a new height to a slanted curtain wall through ACAPI_Element_Change (seen in Archicad 29), so it is given here.
  - `angle` (number): Optional new slant angle in degrees, as CreateCurtainWalls takes it and GetDetailsOfElements returns it: 90 is vertical, less than 90 leans to the left of the reference line (seen from its first point), more than 90 to the right. The vertical height and the elevation of the reference line are kept. A slanted curtain wall needs a reference line of exactly 2 points. When omitted, the old curtain wall's slant is kept. Archicad does not change the slant of an existing curtain wall through ACAPI_Element_Change, so it is given here.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input curtain wall: the new curtain wall, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that curtain wall. Its labels are deleted with it, dimensions measuring it lose those witness points or are deleted, and it leaves its group.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateCurtainWalls.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateCurtainWalls.py): Gives a curtain wall a new reference line with a second segment, and a slanted curtain wall a new height and slant, with RecreateCurtainWalls, keeping their settings and Element IDs. ModifyCurtainWalls keeps the number of segments of a curtain wall, and Archicad does not apply a new height or slant to a slanted curtain wall through it. So RecreateCurtainWalls creates the curtain wall again with the old one as templateElementId (CreateCurtainWalls takes it too) and deletes the old one: the result gives the new curtain wall and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group). Without coordinates the old reference line is kept; height is the vertical height.

### RecreateRailings

Recreates Railing elements on a new reference line - with more or fewer nodes and segments, in 2D as CreateRailings takes it or with an elevation per node and arcs as CreateRailingsFromPolyline takes it - because the Archicad API cannot change the reference line of an existing railing. The new railing is created with the old one as templateElementId, so it gets its node and segment settings, posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters, story visibility, pens, layer, home story and bottom offset; it also gets its Element ID, renovation status, classifications, element categories, property values, solid element operations and trims, and the old railing is then deleted. Each railing is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for that railing. The result lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group). Settings given to single segments, nodes or posts of the old railing are not carried over: the new ones are generated from the railing's defaults, as when it is drawn again in Archicad.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateRailings

Parameters:

- `railings` (array of object, required): The railings to recreate on a new reference line.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The railing to recreate.
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D): The new reference line on the floor plan, as CreateRailings takes it: one node per point, one segment per pair of consecutive points. The railing keeps its bottom offset. Give this or polylineCoordinates.
  - `polylineCoordinates` (array of Coordinate3D): The new reference line with an elevation per node, as CreateRailingsFromPolyline takes it (z relative to the railing's home story). Give this or coordinates.
  - `polylineArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional arc segments of polylineCoordinates, as CreateRailingsFromPolyline takes them.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input railing: the new railing, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that railing. Its labels are deleted with it, dimensions measuring it lose those witness points or are deleted, and it leaves its group. The link of a railing to the slab or stair it was placed on cannot be read through the Archicad API, so it is not listed in notCarriedOver: the new railing has none.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateRailings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateRailings.py): Creates a straight railing, then gives it a new reference line with two more nodes with RecreateRailings, keeping its settings and Element ID. The Archicad API cannot change the reference line of an existing railing, so RecreateRailings creates it again with the old one as template and deletes the old one: the result gives the new railing and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group). coordinates is a 2D reference line as CreateRailings takes it; polylineCoordinates (with polylineArcs) gives each node its own elevation.

### RecreateStairs

Recreates Stair elements on a new baseline (with its landings, winders and curved edges, as CreateStairs takes it), because the Archicad API cannot change the baseline of an existing stair. The new stair gets the old one's settings (everything ModifyStairs writes, its baseline position, rules and top link), Element ID, layer, home story and base offset, renovation status, classifications, element categories and property values, and its solid element operations (on Archicad 27 without their link flags, which the API cannot read there) and roof or shell trims; the old stair is then deleted. Each stair is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for that stair. The new stair has a new GUID: the result maps the old GUID to the new one and lists what could not be carried over (associative labels, dimensions of the current database that measured the old stair, and the group it was in). Archicad lays out the boundaries and the walking lines of the new stair again from its baseline and flight width, so boundaries or a walking line edited by hand on the old stair are not carried over; the API cannot write them, so an item that gives one is refused and the stair is left as it was.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateStairs

Parameters:

- `stairs` (array of object, required): The stairs to recreate on a new baseline.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The stair to recreate.
  - `baseLinePoints` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The new baseline, as CreateStairs takes it and GetDetailsOfElements returns it. The old stair's baseline position and offset are kept.
  - `baseLineEdges` (array of StairBaseLineEdge): Optional. The segment type of each edge of the new baseline (baseLinePoints.length - 1 items), as in CreateStairs. Give it, with baseLineVertices, to keep the landings of an L or U stair.
  - `baseLineVertices` (array of StairBaseLineVertex): Optional. The turn at each point of the new baseline (baseLinePoints.length items), as in CreateStairs.
  - `baseLineArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional. The curved edges of the new baseline, as in CreateStairs and as GetDetailsOfElements returns them (0-based indices, endIndex = begIndex + 1). Without it every edge of the new baseline is straight, also when the old stair was curved.
  - `leftBoundary` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the left boundary of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `rightBoundary` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the right boundary of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `walkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `customWalkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the custom walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.
  - `centerWalkingLine` (StairOutlineNotWritable): Not writable: the center walking line of the stair. An item with it is refused.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input stair: the new stair, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that stair. Labels of the old stair are deleted with it; dimensions measuring it lose those witness points or are deleted.

Grasshopper: `RecreateStairsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateStairs.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateStairs.py): Creates a U-shaped stair, then moves the end of its second flight with RecreateStairs. The Archicad API cannot change the baseline of an existing stair, so RecreateStairs creates the stair again on the new baseline with the settings, Element ID, classifications, categories and properties of the old one, and deletes the old one. The result maps the old GUID to the new one and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions). The new stair is read back, then deleted.

### RecreateWindows

Recreates Window elements in another wall (ownerWallId, optionally at a new centerOffset along it), because Archicad does not move a window into another wall through ACAPI_Element_Change: it keeps its owner (seen in Archicad 29). The new window is created as CreateWindows creates one, from the Window tool defaults with the tool's marker, with the old window's settings (size, sill, anchor, reveal, sides, pens, line types, surfaces and the rest of API_WindowType), library part and GDL parameters, layer and renovation status; its marker gets the old marker's parameters when both are of the same marker library part. It also gets the old window's Element ID, classifications, element categories and property values, and the old window is then deleted. Each window is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for that window. The new window has a new GUID: the result maps the old GUID to the new one and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions of the current database that measured the old window, group).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateWindows

Parameters:

- `windows` (array of object, required): The windows to recreate in another wall.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The window to recreate.
  - `ownerWallId` (ElementId, required): The wall to place the new window in, as CreateWindows takes it: a wall that is not polygonal. It may also be the window's own wall.
  - `centerOffset` (number): Optional position of the center of the new window along the wall, from the wall's beginning (API_WindowType::objLoc), as CreateWindows and ModifyWindows take it and GetDetailsOfElements returns it. When omitted, the old window's centerOffset is kept.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input window: the new window, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that window. Labels of the old window are deleted with it, dimensions measuring it lose those witness points or are deleted, and it leaves its group.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateWindows.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateWindows.py): Creates two walls and a window in the first one, then moves the window into the second wall with RecreateWindows. Archicad does not move a window into another wall through ModifyWindows (ACAPI_Element_Change keeps its owner), so RecreateWindows creates it again in ownerWallId, at centerOffset along it (or at its old centerOffset), with the old window's settings, library part and GDL parameters, and deletes the old one. The result gives the new window and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group); the new window keeps the Element ID, classifications and property values.

### RecreateDoors

Recreates Door elements in another wall (ownerWallId, optionally at a new centerOffset along it), because Archicad does not move a door into another wall through ACAPI_Element_Change: it keeps its owner (seen in Archicad 29). The new door is created as CreateDoors creates one, from the Door tool defaults with the tool's marker, with the old door's settings (size, sill, anchor, reveal, sides, pens, line types, surfaces and the rest of API_DoorType), library part and GDL parameters, layer and renovation status; its marker gets the old marker's parameters when both are of the same marker library part. It also gets the old door's Element ID, classifications, element categories and property values, and the old door is then deleted. Each door is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for that door. The new door has a new GUID: the result maps the old GUID to the new one and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions of the current database that measured the old door, group).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateDoors

Parameters:

- `doors` (array of object, required): The doors to recreate in another wall.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The door to recreate.
  - `ownerWallId` (ElementId, required): The wall to place the new door in, as CreateDoors takes it: a wall that is not polygonal. It may also be the door's own wall.
  - `centerOffset` (number): Optional position of the center of the new door along the wall, from the wall's beginning (API_WindowType::objLoc), as CreateDoors and ModifyDoors take it and GetDetailsOfElements returns it. When omitted, the old door's centerOffset is kept.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input door: the new door, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that door. Labels of the old door are deleted with it, dimensions measuring it lose those witness points or are deleted, and it leaves its group.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateDoors.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateDoors.py): Creates two walls and a door in the first one, then moves the door into the second wall with RecreateDoors, keeping its position along the wall. Archicad does not move a door into another wall through ModifyDoors (ACAPI_Element_Change keeps its owner), so RecreateDoors creates it again in ownerWallId with the old door's settings, library part and GDL parameters, and deletes the old one. Without centerOffset the door keeps its old position along the wall. The result gives the new door and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group).

### RecreateSkylights

Recreates Skylight elements on another roof or shell (ownerId, optionally at a new anchorPosition on it), because Archicad does not move a skylight onto another roof or shell through ACAPI_Element_Change: it keeps its owner (seen in Archicad 29). The new skylight is created as CreateSkylights creates one, from the Skylight tool defaults, with the old skylight's settings (size, anchor point, fix mode, azimuth, pens, line types, surfaces and the rest of API_SkylightType), library part and GDL parameters, layer and renovation status; Archicad sets its plane, level and elevation angle from the new owner. It also gets the old skylight's Element ID, classifications, element categories and property values, and the old skylight is then deleted. Each skylight is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for that skylight. The new skylight has a new GUID: the result maps the old GUID to the new one and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions of the current database that measured the old skylight, group).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateSkylights

Parameters:

- `skylights` (array of object, required): The skylights to recreate on another roof or shell.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The skylight to recreate.
  - `ownerId` (ElementId, required): The roof (single- or multi-plane) or shell to place the new skylight in, as CreateSkylights takes it. It may also be the skylight's own roof or shell.
  - `anchorPosition` (Coordinate2D): Optional global XY coordinates of the new skylight's anchor point, as CreateSkylights and ModifySkylights take them and GetDetailsOfElements returns them. Archicad places the skylight on its owner at this point, so it has to lie on the new owner. When omitted, the old skylight's anchorPosition is kept.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input skylight: the new skylight, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that skylight. Labels of the old skylight are deleted with it, dimensions measuring it lose those witness points or are deleted, and it leaves its group.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateSkylights.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateSkylights.py): Creates two roofs and a skylight in the first one, then moves the skylight onto the second roof with RecreateSkylights. Archicad does not move a skylight onto another roof or shell through ModifySkylights (ACAPI_Element_Change keeps its owner), so RecreateSkylights creates it again on ownerId, at anchorPosition (or at its old one), with the old skylight's settings, library part and GDL parameters, and deletes the old one. The result gives the new skylight and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group).

### RecreateZones

Recreates automatic Zone elements as manual zones (makeManual), because Archicad does not turn an automatic zone into a manual one through ACAPI_Element_Change (seen in Archicad 29). The new manual zone has the polygon the old zone has now (with its arcs and holes, as GetDetailsOfElements returns it), so it no longer follows its boundaries when the zones are updated; it gets the old zone's category, name, number, stamp library part, stamp position and stamp parameters, levels, contour, cover fill, surface and the rest of API_ZoneType, layer and renovation status, and its Element ID, classifications, element categories and property values. The old zone is deleted first, since a new zone with its polygon would overlap it; a new zone that would overlap another zone of the story is refused, as CreateZones refuses it, unless allowOverlap is true. Each zone is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for that zone. The new zone has a new GUID: the result maps the old GUID to the new one and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions of the current database that measured the old zone, group).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateZones

Parameters:

- `zones` (array of object, required): The zones to recreate as manual zones.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The automatic zone to recreate.
  - `makeManual` (boolean, required): Must be true: the new zone is a manual zone (isManual in GetDetailsOfElements) with the polygon the old zone has now (its polygonOutline, polygonArcs and holes), so it no longer follows its boundaries when the zones are updated. Archicad does not turn an automatic zone into a manual one through ACAPI_Element_Change (seen in Archicad 29). A zone that is manual already is refused, as there is nothing to change.
  - `allowOverlap` (boolean): Optional, defaults to false. As in CreateZones: a new zone that would overlap another zone of the same story (not the old zone, which is deleted first) fails with an error naming that zone, instead of risking Archicad's modal overlap warning, which blocks the API. Set it to true to create the zone anyway; the dialog may then appear.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input zone: the new manual zone, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that zone. Labels of the old zone are deleted with it, dimensions measuring it lose those witness points or are deleted, and it leaves its group.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateZones.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateZones.py): Builds a room of four walls with an automatic zone in it, then turns the zone into a manual zone with RecreateZones. Archicad does not make an automatic zone manual through ModifyZones (ACAPI_Element_Change keeps it automatic), so RecreateZones creates a manual zone with the polygon the zone has now and its category, name, number, stamp and other settings, Element ID, classifications and property values, and deletes the old zone. The manual zone no longer follows its walls when the zones are updated. The result gives the new zone and lists what could not be carried over (labels, dimensions, group).

### RecreateAngleDimensions

Recreates Angle Dimension elements on new lines with a new arc position (firstLine, secondLine and arcPosition, as CreateAngleDimensions takes them), because Archicad does not move the lines or the arc of an angle dimension through ACAPI_Element_Change (seen in Archicad 29). The new angle dimension is static, as CreateAngleDimensions creates it, and is created in the current database, where the old one has to be. It gets the old one's settings (pen, inner or outer arc, markers, witness lines, text pen, size, font, style, position and direction, custom text and the rest of API_AngleDimensionType), layer, story and renovation status, and its classifications, element categories and property values, and its Element ID where Archicad gives angle dimensions one (Archicad 29 refuses an Element ID on them, so there is none to carry); the text goes back to its automatic place on the new arc. The old angle dimension is then deleted. Each angle dimension is recreated in its own undo step, and when any step fails nothing is changed for it. The new angle dimension has a new GUID: the result maps the old GUID to the new one and lists what could not be carried over (the group it was in).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RecreateAngleDimensions

Parameters:

- `angleDimensions` (array of object, required): The angle dimensions to recreate on new lines, with a new arc position.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): The angle dimension to recreate. It has to be in the current database (the floor plan, or the section, elevation, interior elevation, worksheet or detail whose window is active), where the new one is created.
  - `firstLine` (AngleDimensionLine, required): The new first measured line, as CreateAngleDimensions takes it.
  - `secondLine` (AngleDimensionLine, required): The new second measured line, as CreateAngleDimensions takes it. It must not be parallel to the first one.
  - `arcPosition` (Coordinate2D, required): A point the new dimension arc passes through, as CreateAngleDimensions takes it: its distance from the intersection of the two lines is the radius of the arc, and the side it lies on chooses which of the angles between the lines is measured.

Returns:

- `results` (RecreatedElementsOrErrors, required): One item per input angle dimension: the new angle dimension, or an error. After an error nothing was changed for that angle dimension. The old one leaves its group.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateAngleDimensions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RecreateAngleDimensions.py): Dimensions a 30 degree roof pitch with CreateAngleDimensions, then moves the dimension onto a 45 degree pitch with RecreateAngleDimensions. Archicad does not move the lines or the arc of an angle dimension through ACAPI_Element_Change, so RecreateAngleDimensions creates it again on the new lines and arc position (as CreateAngleDimensions takes them) with the old one's pens, text, markers and inner or outer arc, classifications and property values, and deletes the old one. The result gives the new angle dimension. Archicad 29 gives angle dimensions no Element ID, so there is none to carry.

### ChangeTextContent

Replaces a range of the content of Text elements and text Labels, keeping the styles of the runs and the autotexts in the rest of the content.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeTextContent

Parameters:

- `contentChanges` (array of TextContentChange, required): The content changes, applied in order (several changes of one element see the content as the previous one left it). Unlike ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels, the rest of the content is not rebuilt: the other runs, their styles and any autotext in them stay as they are, and the inserted piece takes the style of the character at 'from'.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ChangeTextContentComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeTextContent.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ChangeTextContent.py): Creates the text 'Hello World', then replaces 'World' with 'Tapir' with ChangeTextContent. from is the character position, range the number of characters replaced (0 inserts). The styles of the rest of the content and the autotexts in it are kept. A range must stay within one line.

### ModifyZones

Modifies Zone elements: name, number, category, zone stamp, stamp pen, height, base offset, top link, floor thickness, letter size (roomLSize, in millimetres), contour line, cover fill, 3D surface (one surface on all sides, or the surfaces of the bounding walls), polygon display (gross or net) and area reduction - the same settings as CreateZones, applied by the same helpers. Only the given fields are changed. geometry replaces the polygon (outline, arcs and holes) of a manual zone in place, so the zone keeps its GUID, properties and other settings; a new polygon that would overlap another zone on the same story is refused unless allowOverlap is true. The reference point of an automatic zone cannot be changed here (SetDetailsOfElements moves it).

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyZones

Parameters:

- `zonesWithDetails` (array of object, required): Array of Zone elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed and the omitted fields are kept; the polygon is kept unless geometry is given. The same fields as the ZoneSettings of SetDetailsOfElements, plus geometry and allowOverlap.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `name` (string): Name of the zone.
  - `numberStr` (string): Zone number.
  - `categoryAttributeId` (AttributeId): The identifier of the zone category attribute.
  - `stampPosition` (Coordinate2D): Position of the origin of the zone stamp.
  - `stampAngle` (number): Rotation angle of the zone stamp in radians.
  - `fixedStampAngle` (boolean): If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.
  - `height` (number): Height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height), so do not combine it with relativeTopStory in the same call: whichever is applied last wins.
  - `bottomOffset` (number): Base level of the zone relative to its home story level.
  - `topOffset` (number): Offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.
  - `relativeTopStory` (number): Non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not set together with height in the same call, see the note on height.
  - `floorThickness` (number): Thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.
  - `roomLSize` (number): Letter size of the zone (roomLSize of the Archicad API) in millimetres, not in metres like the other lengths. The zone stamps of the current Archicad libraries size their texts with their own parameters (GetGDLParametersOfElements, SetGDLParametersOfElements), so this value may not change how the stamp looks.
  - `contourLine` (ZoneContourLine): Contour line of the zone. Only the given fields are changed.
  - `coverFill` (ZoneCoverFill): Cover fill of the zone. Only the given fields are changed.
  - `surface` (ZoneSurface): 3D surface of the zone (the Model panel). Only the given fields are changed.
  - `polygonDisplay` (ZonePolygonDisplay)
  - `stampPen` (ZoneStampPen): Pen of the zone stamp. Only the given fields are changed.
  - `reducePercent` (ZoneReducePercent)
  - `geometry` (ManualZoneGeometry): Optional new polygon of a manual zone (isManual true in GetDetailsOfElements): its outline, arcs and holes, the same geometry as a manual zone of CreateZones. The whole polygon is replaced and the zone keeps its GUID, properties and other settings; the stamp stays where it is unless stampPosition is given too. Refused for an automatic zone, whose polygon Archicad computes from its boundaries (see UpdateZones).
  - `allowOverlap` (boolean): Optional, defaults to false, only used with geometry. As in CreateZones: a new polygon that would overlap another zone on the same story fails with an error naming that zone instead of risking Archicad's modal overlap warning, which blocks the API. Set it to true to change the polygon anyway.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyZonesComponent`, `ZonesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyZones.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/ModifyZones.py): Renames and renumbers the first zone and changes its contour line pen with ModifyZones, reads it back, then restores them. Needs at least one Zone. Only the given fields change; the polygon is kept unless geometry is given (the new polygonCoordinates, polygonArcs and holes of a manual zone, as in CreateZones). ModifyZones takes the same settings as CreateZones, contourLine and coverFill included.

### MeasureTexts

Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#MeasureTexts

Parameters:

- `texts` (array of any or any, required): The texts to measure, each with the font, style and height it would be placed with. Nothing is created.
  - `text` (string, required): The text to measure. Newlines separate lines, each measured on its own; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are treated as LF.
  - `fontIndex` (integer): The index of the font, as GetDetailsOfElements and GetFontsByName report it in fontIndex. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.
  - `fontName` (string): Name of the font as Archicad's font list carries it (GetDetailsOfElements reports it in fontName), which is not always the operating system's font name; GetFontsByName tells whether a name is found. Resolved to the font's index (exact match first, then case-insensitive, then Archicad's font search as GetFontsByName does, so a family name such as 'Arial' finds 'Arial Western'); the text fails when no loaded font has the name. Takes precedence over fontIndex if both are given. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.
  - `height` (number, required): The character height in millimetres, as a Text's height.
  - `bold` (boolean): Bold style. Optional, default false.
  - `italic` (boolean): Italic style. Optional, default false.
  - `underline` (boolean): Underline style. Optional, default false.
  - `slant` (number): The slant angle of the characters in radians; pi/2 (the default) is upright text.
  - `inModelUnits` (boolean): When true, Archicad applies the drawing scale correction and the lengths are model distances at the current drawing scale; when false (the default), they are lengths on paper in millimetres.

Returns:

- `measurements` (array of TextMeasurement or ErrorItem, required): One item per input text, in the same order. The measurement takes no width factor or character spacing into account.

Grasshopper: `MeasureTextsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/MeasureTexts.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/MeasureTexts.py): Measures the length of each line of a two-line text in Arial 2.5 mm, on paper and in the model, with MeasureTexts. Creates nothing. Model lengths use the drawing scale of the current window.
