### SetElementNotificationClient

Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.2.8. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetElementNotificationClient

Parameters:

- `host` (string): The host address of the notification client. If not provided, localhost is used.
- `port` (integer, required): The port number of the notification client.
- `notifyOnNewElement` (boolean): Notify on creation of a new element. Optional parameter, by default true.
- `notifyOnModificationOfAnElement` (boolean): Notify on modification/deletion of an element. The observed elements are the ones ACAPI_Element_GetElemList returns, for API_ZombieElemID or, with elementTypesToObserve, for each of those types, when the first client asking for these notifications of them is registered, and every element of the observed types created after that, plus the elements listed in elementsToObserve. Archicad does not report the changes made by Tapir's own commands, so Tapir reports them itself for SetDetailsOfElements, SetPropertyValuesOfElements, MoveElements, RotateElements, MirrorElements (not for the copies they make, which are new elements), DeleteElements, DeleteSelectedElements, the Modify<Tool> commands (ModifyWalls, ModifyBeams, ModifySlabs, ModifyColumns, ModifyWindows, ModifyDoors, ModifyOpenings, ModifyMorphs, ModifyRoofs, ModifyShells, ModifyMeshes, ModifyObjects, ModifyLamps, ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels, ModifyCurtainWalls, ModifyCurtainWallFrames, ModifyZones, ModifySections, ModifyDetailMarkers, ModifyRailings, ModifyStairs, ModifyPolylines, ModifyHatches, ModifyChangeMarkers), ChangeTextContent, SetGDLParametersOfElements, RunParameterScriptOfElements (only when the script changed the element), SetMarkerParametersOfElements, SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements, ChangeLibraryPartOfElements, SetClassificationsOfElements, SetCategoryValuesOfElements, ModifyPropertyValueOfElements, SetElementInfoStrings, SetURLReferencesOfElements, SetIFCAttributesOfElements, SetIFCPropertiesOfElements, RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements, SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements, LockElements, UnlockElements, SetOpeningDetails, SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, SetOpeningSymbolParameters, CreateGroups and UngroupElements (the grouped elements), MoveElementsToDesignOptions, CreateSolidElementLinks, RemoveSolidElementLinks, CreateSolidOperations (the target and operator when the operation changed or deleted them; the results are new elements), TrimElements, RemoveElementTrims, MergeElements, UnmergeElements, ModifyMEPRoutingElements, ModifyMEPPorts (the element owning the port), ConnectMEPElements, ModifyMEPElements, SetMEPRoutingParameters, ModifyElectricalPanels, ModifyElectricalDevices and ConnectToElectricalCircuits. Of the elements these commands change, only the given ones are reported: an element deleted together with its owner (a door or window of a deleted wall) is not. UpdateZones is not reported by Tapir, because Archicad updates the Zones after the command has returned. When the user moves, rotates, mirrors, elevates, resizes or stretches elements in Archicad, each of their changedElements items also has a transformation: {"type": ..., ...}, where type is "Drag" (with displacement: {"x", "y", "z"}), "Elevate" (with displacement, only z is not 0), "Rotate" (with origin: {"x", "y"} and angle, in radians, counterclockwise), "Mirror" (with origin, a point of the mirror axis, and axisDirection: {"x", "y"}, its unit vector), "Resize" (with origin and ratio), "Stretch", "VerticalStretch", "PreservedHeightStretch", "PreservedDirectionStretch" or "General"; the changes made by Tapir's own commands and by undo or redo have no transformation. Optional parameter, by default true. Archicad attaches an observer to each element to observe (see elementTypesToObserve and elementsToObserve) when the first client asks for this, and detaches them when the last one stops, and it is blocked meanwhile: one element at a time (the Archicad API has no call for many elements or a whole type), about 10 elements per second on a large project, and the time grows faster than the number of elements. Count the elements first (GetAllElements with IncludeSubElemObjects, or GetElementsByType) and limit the types, or list the elements with elementsToObserve, on large projects.
- `elementTypesToObserve` (array of ElementType): Only modifications/deletions of elements of these types are observed and notified to this client, together with the elements of elementsToObserve. Optional parameter, by default (when neither elementTypesToObserve nor elementsToObserve is given) every element (including the parts of curtain walls, stairs and railings, which are most of the elements of large projects). Registering the same client again with other types changes them; only the elements of types no client observed before get an observer then. Does not limit the other notifications.
- `elementsToObserve` (Elements): Only modifications/deletions of these elements are observed and notified to this client, together with the elements of the types of elementTypesToObserve. Only these elements get an observer, so registering takes time in proportion to their number, not to the size of the project (#2493). Unlike elementTypesToObserve, it does not cover the elements created later: with elementsToObserve alone, the changes of a new element are not notified (notifyOnNewElement still reports its creation); register the client again with the new element in the list to observe it. A listed element that does not exist fails the command, and the client is then not registered or changed. Registering the same client again with another list changes it; only the elements no client observed before get an observer then, and the ones no client needs any more lose theirs. Optional parameter, by default every element (see elementTypesToObserve). Does not limit the other notifications.
- `notifyOnReservationChanges` (boolean): Notify on reservation changes of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.
- `notifyOnSelectionChange` (boolean): Notify when the selection changes. The message is {"selectedElements": [...]}: the whole current selection, each item an elementId as in the response of GetSelectedElements, an empty list when nothing is selected. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnWindowChange` (boolean): Notify when the current (active) window changes or the user switches to another story. The message is {"windowChanged": {"event": "Window" or "Floor", "windowType": ..., "databaseId": ..., "storyIndex": ...}}: windowType and databaseId describe the new current window as in the response of GetCurrentWindowType (databaseId is missing when that response has none), storyIndex is the active story, missing when it cannot be read. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnProjectEvents` (boolean): Notify on project events. The message is {"projectEvent": ...}, one of "New", "NewAndReset", "Open", "Close", "Quit", "SendChanges" (a Teamwork send is about to start) and "ReceiveChanges" (Teamwork changes were received). The client stays registered when the project is closed or another one is opened. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnAttributeReplacement` (boolean): Notify when attributes are deleted and replaced by other attributes of the same type (for example Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager). The message is {"replacedAttributes": [{"attributeType": ..., "oldIndex": ..., "newIndex": ..., "newAttributeId": ...}, ...]}: attributeType is one of the type names of GetAttributesByType ("Layer", "Line", "Fill", "Composite", "Surface", "LayerCombination", "ZoneCategory", "Profile", "PenTable", "MEPSystem", "OperationProfile", "BuildingMaterial", or "Unknown"), oldIndex is the index of the replaced attribute and newIndex the index of the attribute that replaces it, newAttributeId is the attributeId of that attribute, missing when it cannot be found. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnToolChange` (boolean): Notify when the user switches to another tool in the Toolbox. The message is {"toolChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type of the new tool, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), "None" for the Arrow and the Marquee, and "Unknown" for a tool Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnViewEvents` (boolean): Notify when an item of the Project Navigator or the Organizer is inserted (for example a view is saved or a layout is created), modified (for example renamed), deleted or opened. The message is {"viewEvent": {"event": ..., "navigatorMapId": ..., "navigatorItemId": {"guid": ...}}}: event is one of "Inserted", "Modified", "Deleted" and "Opened", navigatorMapId is the navigator map of the item, one of "ProjectMap", "PublicViewMap", "MyViewMap", "LayoutBook" and "PublisherSets" (as navigatorMapId of GetNavigatorItemTree), and navigatorItemId is the guid of the navigator item, as in the response of GetNavigatorItemTree (a deleted item no longer exists). Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnLockableReservationChanges` (boolean): Notify when a Teamwork lockable object set (the non-element things Teamwork reserves: the attributes of a type, favorites, model view options, project info, project preferences, ...) is reserved or released, by anyone, including the current user. The message is {"lockableReservationChanged": {"event": ..., "objectSetId": {"guid": ...}, "objectSetName": ..., "reservedBy": ..., "reservedByUserId": ...}}: event is "Reserved" or "Released", objectSetId is the guid of the object set, objectSetName its name as objectSetName of ReserveLockableObjectSet (for example "Composites", "LayerSettingsDialog" or "Favorites"), missing when it is not one of the documented sets, and reservedBy and reservedByUserId are the name and the Teamwork user id of the member who reserved it, only for "Reserved". Element reservations are notified by notifyOnReservationChanges. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnToolDefaultChanges` (boolean): Notify when the default settings of a tool change (for example the user changes the settings of the Wall tool with no wall selected), so a client can read the new defaults. The message is {"toolDefaultsChanged": {"elementType": ...}}: elementType is the element type whose defaults changed, as in elementTypesToObserve (for example "Wall" or "Column"), and "Unknown" for a type Tapir has no type name for. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnAttributeChanges` (boolean): Notify when attributes (layers, fills, composites, surfaces, building materials, ...) are created, modified or deleted. The message is {"attributesChanged": {"event": ..., "attributeIds": [{"attributeId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and attributeIds are the attributes, as in the response of GetAttributesByType (a deleted attribute no longer exists). Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnClassificationChanges` (boolean): Notify when classification systems or classification items are created, modified or deleted. The messages are {"classificationSystemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationSystemIds": [{"classificationSystemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"classificationItemsChanged": {"event": ..., "classificationItemIds": [{"classificationItemId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllClassificationSystems and GetAllClassificationsInSystem. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnPropertyDefinitionChanges` (boolean): Notify when property groups or property definitions are created, modified or deleted (property values of elements are notified as changedElements by notifyOnModificationOfAnElement). The messages are {"propertyGroupsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyGroupIds": [{"propertyGroupId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}} and {"propertyDefinitionsChanged": {"event": ..., "propertyIds": [{"propertyId": {"guid": ...}}, ...]}}: event is "Created", "Modified" or "Deleted", and the ids are as in the response of GetAllProperties. Not available in Archicad 25: setting it to true there fails. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOnMarqueeChange` (boolean): Notify when the marquee is drawn, changed or removed. The message is {"marqueeChanged": {"type": ..., "multiStory": ...}}: type is "rectangle", "rotatedRectangle", "polygon" or, when the marquee was removed, "none", as type of GetMarquee, which returns the shape of the marquee; multiStory is missing for "none". Available from Archicad 27: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.
- `notifyOn3DSettingsChanges` (boolean): Notify when the settings of the 3D window change (projection, Filter and Cut Elements in 3D, 3D window settings). The message is {"view3DSettingsChanged": {}}; read the new settings with the commands of the 3D window. The changes made while navigating in 3D are not notified. Available from Archicad 30: setting it to true in an earlier version fails. Optional parameter, by default false.


Grasshopper: `SetElementNotificationClientComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetElementNotificationClient.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/SetElementNotificationClient.py): Prints the element events Archicad sends to a local HTTP server registered with SetElementNotificationClient. Creates a column to trigger a notification, moves it to trigger a change notification, then removes the client again. Archicad posts each event as JSON to http://<host>:<port>/element_notification. Modifications are observed only for the columns (elementTypesToObserve) and for the listed elements (elementsToObserve, here the first wall of the project, if there is one): attaching an observer to every element blocks Archicad for minutes on a project with thousands of elements, while a list of elements takes time only for the listed ones.

### RegularizePolygons

Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RegularizePolygons

Parameters:

- `polygons` (array of PolygonRegularizationData, required): The polygons to regularize, in the format of CreateSlabs (polygonCoordinates, polygonArcs, holes). For CreateHatches, pass the outline of a result as its coordinates and arcs.
- `withAncestry` (boolean): Also return for every vertex and edge of the results which input vertex or edge it came from. Optional, false by default.

Returns:

- `results` (array of RegularizedPolygons or ErrorItem, required): One item per input polygon, in the order of the request.

Grasshopper: `RegularizePolygonsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolygons.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolygons.py): Regularizes a self-intersecting (bow tie) outline with a repeated point with RegularizePolygons. The results are in the format of CreateSlabs; nothing is created.

### RegularizePolylines

Regularizes polylines with Archicad's own polyline regularization: removes repeated consecutive points. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RegularizePolylines

Parameters:

- `polylines` (array of PolylineRegularizationData, required): The polylines to regularize, in the format of CreatePolylines.
- `withAncestry` (boolean): Also return for every point and segment of the results which input point or segment it came from. Optional, false by default.

Returns:

- `results` (array of RegularizedPolyline or ErrorItem, required): One item per input polyline, in the order of the request.

Grasshopper: `RegularizePolylinesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolylines.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/RegularizePolylines.py): Removes the repeated points of a polyline with RegularizePolylines, and reports which input point each result point came from. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines; nothing is created.

### GetSplineMaxDistances

Measures how far the given 2D coordinates are from a segment of a Spline element, between two of its fit points, with its own Bezier handles: returns the largest distance, for example to check how well a polyline follows the spline. The output is aligned with the input array. Changes nothing in the project.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSplineMaxDistances

Parameters:

- `splines` (array of object, required): The spline segments to measure and the coordinates to measure from them.
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): A Spline element.
  - `segmentIndex` (integer, required): The segment of the spline between its fit points segmentIndex and segmentIndex + 1, from 0 to the number of fit points - 2 (the fit points are the coordinates GetDetailsOfElements returns for the spline).
  - `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates to measure from the segment.

Returns:

- `results` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The result of each input item, in the same order, or an error.

Grasshopper: `GetSplineMaxDistancesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSplineMaxDistances.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSplineMaxDistances.py): GetSplineMaxDistances measures how far coordinates are from a segment of a Spline element (between its fit points segmentIndex and segmentIndex + 1), with the spline's own Bezier handles, and returns the largest distance. Here a spline is created and the midpoint of the straight line between its first two fit points is measured from its first segment.

### GetProfileValuesOfElements

Returns the custom profiles walls, beams and columns use, with the values the element gives them: the width and height of the stretched profile and the value of each profile modifier, measured on the stretched profile of the element (one per Profile wall, one per Profile segment of a beam or column). Read only: the Archicad API has no function that writes an element's modifier values or stretch.

Group: Element Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetProfileValuesOfElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (array of ElementIdArrayItem, required)

Returns:

- `profileValuesOfElements` (array of ElementProfileValuesOrError, required)

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetProfileValuesOfElements.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetProfileValuesOfElements.py): Reads the profile values of every wall, beam and column with a custom profile: the size of the stretched profile and the value of each profile modifier on that element. The values are measured on the stretched profile each element uses, so a profile stretched by the element, or a modifier the element changed, reads with the element's own value. Writing them is not possible: the Archicad API has no function for an element's modifier values or stretch.

## Shared schema definitions

Types that parameters and results refer to by name.

### Elements

array of ElementIdArrayItem: A list of elements.

### ElementIdArrayItem

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)

### ElementIdOrError

ElementIdArrayItem or ErrorItem: An element identifier or an error.

### ElementIdsOrErrors

array of ElementIdOrError: A list of element identifiers or errors.

### ElementId

object: The identifier of an element.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### AttributeIdArrayItem

object
- `attributeId` (AttributeId, required)

### AttributeId

object: The identifier of an attribute.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### ProfileModifier

object: An offset modifier of the profile (Profile Manager, Modifiers): it moves edges of the profile's skins by the distance its dimension measures between two anchors. Its value is a live geometric measurement matching what the Profile Editor's dimension shows.
- `modifierId` (string): Identifier of the modifier, stable for the lifetime of the profile. Pass it to CreateProfiles' renameProfileModifiers to rename the modifier.
- `name` (string): User-authored label, e.g. 'Largeur support'. Present only if the profile's author assigned one.
- `value` (number): Present only when the parameter's dimension anchors could be resolved to concrete positions.
- `edges` (array of ProfileModifierEdge): The edges the modifier moves.
- `begin` (ProfileModifierAnchor): The anchor the modifier's dimension starts at.
- `end` (ProfileModifierAnchor): The anchor the modifier's dimension ends at.
- `projectionAngle` (number): The direction, in radians from the x axis, the dimension is measured along. Present only when the dimension has one; otherwise it is measured along its nominal direction.

### ProfileModifierEdge

object: An edge of a profile skin that an offset modifier moves. Edge i of a skin runs from its outlineCoords[i] to outlineCoords[i + 1] (GetProfiles' skins[].outlineCoords, field skinOutlines); 0 and the last index are not edges of the drawn shape.
- `skinId` (string, required): The skin, from GetProfiles' skins[].skinId.
- `edgeIndex` (integer, required): The edge of the skin, the same position as in GetProfiles' skins[].edges.
- `direction` (string ("Left", "Right")): Which way Archicad moves the edge for a growing value, as it stores it. CreateProfiles works it out from the shape when it is omitted.

### ProfileModifierAnchor

object: One end of an offset modifier's dimension. Fixed: a point (position). Vertex: a vertex of a skin (skinId, vertexIndex: a position in GetProfiles' skins[].outlineCoords, 1 or more). Edge: an edge of a skin (skinId, edgeIndex, as in ProfileModifierEdge), measured perpendicular to it. The other types follow the profile's bounding box corners or stretch zone limits and need nothing else.
- `type` (string ("Fixed", "Vertex", "Edge", "BoundingBoxUpperLeft", "BoundingBoxUpperRight", "BoundingBoxLowerLeft", "BoundingBoxLowerRight", "StretchZoneLeft", "StretchZoneRight", "StretchZoneBottom", "StretchZoneTop", "Undefined"), required)
- `position` (Coordinate2D): The point of a Fixed anchor, in the coordinates of skins[].outlineCoords.
- `skinId` (string): The skin of a Vertex or Edge anchor, from GetProfiles' skins[].skinId.
- `vertexIndex` (integer): The vertex of a Vertex anchor: its position in the skin's outlineCoords.
- `edgeIndex` (integer): The edge of an Edge anchor: edge i runs from outlineCoords[i] to outlineCoords[i + 1].
- `positiveSideOnRight` (boolean): Edge anchor: whether the dimension grows to the right of the edge, seen from its start to its end. CreateProfiles sets it so the value grows as the edge moves away from the other anchor when it is omitted.

### ElementProfileValues

object: The profile values of one wall, beam or column, measured on the stretched profile the element uses: the profile after the element's own stretch and modifier values.
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)
- `profiles` (array of ElementProfileValue, required): One item per custom profile of the element: one for a Profile wall, one per Profile segment of a beam or column. Empty when the element uses no custom profile.

### ElementProfileValue

object: A custom profile as one element, or one segment of a beam or column, uses it.
- `segmentIndex` (integer): The segment of the beam or column, 0-based in the order GetDetailsOfElements lists the segments. Absent for a wall.
- `profileId` (AttributeIdArrayItem): The profile attribute. Absent when it could not be resolved.
- `width` (number, required): Width of the stretched profile (its bounding box): the element's own width where the profile stretches horizontally.
- `height` (number, required): Height of the stretched profile (its bounding box): the element's own height where the profile stretches vertically.
- `profileModifiers` (array of ProfileModifier, required): The offset modifiers of the profile with the values this element has, measured on its stretched profile the way GetProfiles measures them on the profile attribute. Empty when the stretched profile Archicad returns carries no modifiers. A modifier whose dimension crosses a stretch zone includes the stretch.

### ElementProfileValuesOrError

ElementProfileValues or ErrorItem: The profile values of one element, or an error.

### Guid

string: A Globally Unique Identifier (or Universally Unique Identifier) in its string representation as defined in RFC 4122.

### HotlinkNodeId

object: The identifier of a hotlink node - the reference to a module source file, which instances are placed from.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### HotlinkDetails

object: Details of a placed hotlink instance: which node it comes from and where it sits.
- `hotlinkType` (HotlinkType, required)
- `hotlinkNodeId` (HotlinkNodeId, required)
- `origin` (Coordinate3D, required)
- `rotationAngle` (number, required): Counter-clockwise rotation about the origin, in radians.
- `mirrored` (boolean, required): True when the module's local X axis is reflected.
- `floorDifference` (integer)
- `skipNested` (boolean)
- `suspendFixAngle` (boolean)
- `ignoreTopFloorLinks` (boolean)
- `relinkWallOpenings` (boolean)
- `adjustLevelDiffs` (boolean)

### SetGDLParameterArray

array of SetGDLParameterDetails: The list of GDL parameters.

### GDLParameterArray

array of GDLParameterDetails: The list of GDL parameters.

### GDLParameterList

object: The list of GDL parameters.
- `parameters` (GDLParameterArray, required)

### PossibleStringValues

array of string: The possible string values of a GDL parameter.

### PossibleNumericValues

array of object: The possible numeric values of a GDL parameter.

### GDLParameterDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `displayName` (string, required): The display name of the parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `type` (string, required): The type of the parameter.
- `dimension1` (integer): The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `dimension2` (integer): The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `value` (any, required): The value of the parameter. For an array parameter it is a flat list of all items row by row: dimension1 rows of dimension2 items each. SetGDLParametersOfElements accepts the same flat list back.
- `valueDescription` (string): The value description for numeric parameter.
- `isLocked` (boolean, required): The parameter is locked; i.e. the user cannot modify it
- `flags` (array of string ("Hidden", "HiddenFromScript", "Disabled", "Child", "Unique", "Fixed", "BoldName", "Open"), required): The flags of the parameter.
- `possibleValues` (PossibleStringValues or PossibleNumericValues)
- `canHaveCustomValue` (boolean): The parameter can have a custom value.
- `itemDescriptions` (array of string): Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter (API_AddParType.arrayDescriptions), one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.

### SetGDLParameterByNameDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `index1` (integer): Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.
- `index2` (integer): Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.
- `value` (any, required): The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

### SetGDLParameterByIndexDetails

object: Details of a GDL parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `index1` (integer): Optional 1-based first index for changing a single item of an array parameter. Only valid for array parameters and only together with a single (non-list) value.
- `index2` (integer): Optional 1-based second index for changing a single item of a two-dimensional array parameter. Only valid together with index1. Defaults to 1.
- `value` (any, required): The new value of the parameter, in the unit GetGDLParametersOfElements reports it in (Angle parameters in radians). For array parameters provide a list of values for one-dimensional arrays (e.g. [1, 2, 3]) or a list of lists for two-dimensional arrays (e.g. [[11, 12], [21, 22]]); the list must contain exactly as many values as the parameter has items, resizing an array parameter is not supported. A two-dimensional array can also be given as a flat list of all its dimension1 x dimension2 items row by row, the layout GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Alternatively provide index1 (and optionally index2) together with a single value to change one item of the array. Within one command call whole-array (list) values are applied after all single-value changes.

### SetGDLParameterDetails

SetGDLParameterByNameDetails or SetGDLParameterByIndexDetails

### MorphPolygonHole

object
- `vertexIds` (array of integer, required)

### BeamHoleType

string ("Rectangular", "Circular")

### MorphPolygon

object
- `vertexIds` (array of integer, required): Counterclockwise outer-loop vertex indices for this face.
- `filled` (boolean): Defaults to true. Set to false to create only this loop's edges (a wireframe outline, e.g. a bare rectangle with no surface fill) without an actual face - holes/surfaceId are ignored in that case, since there is no fill for them to apply to.
- `holes` (array of MorphPolygonHole): Optional hole loops cut out of this face, each a clockwise list of vertex indices.
- `surfaceId` (AttributeId): Optional per-face surface (render material) override. Uses the Morph's default surface (the morph's own surfaceId) when omitted, and takes precedence over it when given. Ignored in Archicad 25 and 26.

### MeshSubline

object
- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The 3D coordinates of the leveling subline of the mesh.

### CurtainWallPattern

object: The column (primary) or row (secondary) pattern of a curtain wall segment: the sizes of the columns/rows of one pattern unit and how the unit is repeated along the segment.
- `sizes` (array of number, required): The sizes (widths of the columns or heights of the rows) of the pattern unit in meters, in order from the start of the segment or from the bottom. The unit is repeated to fill the segment.
- `logic` (CurtainWallPatternLogic)
- `origin` (CurtainWallPatternOrigin)
- `flexibleIndices` (array of integer): Zero-based indices of the columns/rows of the pattern unit that 'BestDivision' may stretch. When omitted, all of them are flexible. Ignored by 'FixedSizes'.

### CurtainWallPatternCell

object: The panel and frame classes of one cell of the pattern unit of a curtain wall segment. Panel classes are numbered as Archicad numbers them: 0 is no panel (the cell is left empty), 1 is the first panel class of the curtain wall (as listed in the Curtain Wall Settings, from the favorite or the tool defaults), 2 the second and so on. Frame classes: 0 is no frame (the cell is merged with its neighbour), 1 the Division frame, 2 the Corner frame, 3 the Boundary frame, 4 the first custom frame class of the curtain wall, 5 the second and so on. Fields not given keep the default assignment of the cell.
- `columnIndex` (integer, required): Zero-based column of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the start of the segment.
- `rowIndex` (integer, required): Zero-based row of the cell within the pattern unit, counted from the bottom.
- `panelClassIndex` (integer): The panel class of the cell. 0 leaves the cell without a panel (Archicad keeps a hidden 'deleted panel' subelement there). With a crossing frame it is the class of the left (or lower) half; see rightPanelClassIndex for the other half.
- `rightPanelClassIndex` (integer): The panel class of the right (or upper) half of a cell with a crossing frame. Defaults to panelClassIndex.
- `leftFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the frame on the left edge of the cell (the grid line at the start of the column).
- `bottomFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the frame on the bottom edge of the cell (the grid line at the bottom of the row).
- `crossingFrameType` (CurtainWallCrossingFrameType)
- `crossingFrameClassIndex` (integer): The frame class of the diagonal frame of the cell. Only used when crossingFrameType is not 'None'.

### BeamHole

object
- `holeId` (number, required)
- `type` (BeamHoleType, required)
- `showContour` (boolean)
- `centerX` (number, required)
- `centerZ` (number, required)
- `width` (number, required)
- `height` (number)

### BeamHoleModification

object
- `type` (BeamHoleType, required)
- `showContour` (boolean)
- `centerX` (number, required)
- `centerZ` (number, required)
- `width` (number, required)
- `height` (number): Only used for the Rectangular type.

### LinkToSettings

object: Mode of linking an element to its home story.
- `homeStoryDifference` (integer): Difference of the home story from the current story.
- `newCreationMode` (boolean): Controls home-story selection during element creation. If true, homeStoryDifference selects the home story relative to the current story and the element's absolute floor index is ignored. If false, the absolute floor index is used and Archicad fills homeStoryDifference. This is a creation instruction, not a persistent linking mode.

### CoverFillOrientation

object: Orientation/distortion of the floor plan cover fill.
- `type` (HatchOrientationType)
- `origo` (Coordinate2D): Origin of the fill relative to the project origin.
- `matrix00` (number): X component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the cosine of the fill angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix10` (number): Y component of the primary distortion (direction) vector - the sine of the fill angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix01` (number): X component of the secondary distortion vector - the cosine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.
- `matrix11` (number): Y component of the secondary distortion vector - the sine of the normal vector's angle, if not distorted.
- `innerRadius` (number): Radius for circular fill distortion (type Centered only).

### PolyArc

object: Representation of an arc segment of a two dimensional polygon/polyline.
- `begIndex` (integer, required): Node index of one end point of the arc.
- `endIndex` (integer, required): Node index of the other end point of the arc.
- `arcAngle` (number, required): Angle of the arc; it is positive, if the arc is on the right-hand side of the straight segment.

### Coordinate2D

object: 2D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.

### Coordinate3D

object: 3D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.
- `z` (number, required): Z value of the coordinate.

### CoordinateSystem3D

object: A coordinate system in 3D: an origin and three axes. What is left out keeps its default; give all three axes together or none.
- `origin` (Coordinate3D): The origin of the coordinate system.
- `xAxis` (Coordinate3D): The X axis of the coordinate system.
- `yAxis` (Coordinate3D): The Y axis of the coordinate system.
- `zAxis` (Coordinate3D): The Z axis of the coordinate system.

### ShellEdgeTrim

object: How a shell edge is cut.
- `trimType` (string ("Vertical", "Perpendicular", "Horizontal", "CustomAngle"), required): Vertical, Perpendicular or Horizontal to the shell, or at 'angle' (CustomAngle).
- `angle` (number): The trim angle in radians. Only CustomAngle uses it; pi/2 by default.

### RoofEdgeTrim

object: How an edge of a roof's polygon (a single-plane roof's outline or a multi-plane roof's contour) is cut (the edge's cut in the roof's Custom Edge Settings).
- `trimType` (string ("Vertical", "Perpendicular", "Horizontal", "CustomAngle", "AlignWithCut")): Vertical, Perpendicular to the roof plane, Horizontal, or at 'angle' (CustomAngle). AlignWithCut is only reported, for shell edges; it cannot be written to a roof.
- `angle` (number): The angle of the edge cut in radians, as Archicad stores it. Only CustomAngle uses it.

### SlabEdgeTrim

object: The Edge Angle of a slab edge (Geometry and Positioning panel of Slab Settings): vertical, or at a custom angle.
- `trimType` (string ("Vertical", "Perpendicular", "Horizontal", "CustomAngle", "AlignWithCut")): Vertical (the default, perpendicular to the slab), or at 'angle' (CustomAngle). ModifySlabs writes only these two; the others are only reported, should Archicad store one on a slab.
- `angle` (number): The angle of the edge in radians, as Archicad stores it (the dialog shows it in degrees). Only CustomAngle uses it.

### RoofEdgeType

string ("Undefined", "Ridge", "Valley", "Gable", "Hip", "Eaves", "Peak", "SideWall", "EndWall", "RoofTransitionDome", "RoofTransitionHollow"): The Edge Type of an edge of a single-plane roof (its Custom Edge Settings), used only for listing: Undefined (not set, the default), Ridge, Valley, Gable, Hip, Eaves, Peak, SideWall, EndWall, RoofTransitionDome or RoofTransitionHollow.

### ShellProfile

object: A profile polyline of a shell, in the XY plane of its coordinate system.
- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The points of the polyline.
- `arcs` (array of PolyArc): Arc segments of the polyline, with indices into coordinates; index len(coordinates) is the first point again, which closes the polyline.
- `closed` (boolean): Whether the segment from the last point back to the first one is part of the profile. False by default.

### ShellCutPolygon

object: A closed polygon cutting a shell: its clipping contour or a hole.
- `coordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The points of the polygon, in the XY plane of 'plane'.
- `arcs` (array of PolyArc): Arc segments of the polygon, with indices into coordinates.
- `plane` (CoordinateSystem3D): The plane of the polygon, in the coordinates of the shell's base plane: a hole is extruded from it along its Z axis. The base plane itself by default.
- `depth` (number): Required for holes, ignored for the clipping contour: how far the cutting body is extruded from the polygon's plane, along its Z axis (negative values cut downwards).

### Dimensions3D

object: Dimensions in 3D.
- `x` (number, required): X dimension.
- `y` (number, required): Y dimension.
- `z` (number, required): Z dimension.

### ColorRGB

object: RGB color.
- `red` (number, required): Red value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `green` (number, required): Green value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `blue` (number, required): Blue value between 0.0 and 1.0

### Error

object: The details of an error.
- `code` (integer, required): The code of the error.
- `message` (string, required): The error message.

object

object: The result of a successful execution.

### FailedExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of the execution.

### ExecutionResults

array of ExecutionResult: A list of execution results.

### DryRun

boolean: If true, the command makes all the checks of a real run and resolves the same targets, with the same errors, but changes nothing in the project and creates no undo step. The response is that of a real run with "dryRun": true added, and says for each target what the real run would do. Default is false.

### DryRunFlag

boolean (true): Present, and true, only in the response of a dry run (the dryRun input was true): nothing was changed in the project.

### ElementFieldValue

number or integer or boolean or string or ElementFieldOptionalValue: The value of a field of an element's struct in the Archicad API, by the field's kind (see GetElementFieldDefinitions): a number, an integer, a boolean or a string, or for an optional pen or attribute (kinds OverriddenPen and OverriddenAttribute) an object with hasValue and value.

### ElementFieldOptionalValue

object: An optional pen or attribute of an element's struct (API_OverriddenPen or API_OverriddenAttribute in the Archicad API, e.g. cutFillPen or refMat of a wall, leftMaterial of a beam segment): value is used only when hasValue is true; otherwise the element uses its own setting (e.g. the pen or the surface of its building material). In SetElementFields and SetFieldsOfElementDefaults a member left out keeps its value, and a value given without hasValue sets hasValue to true.
- `hasValue` (boolean): Whether value replaces the element's own setting.
- `value` (integer): The pen index (OverriddenPen) or the attribute index (OverriddenAttribute, e.g. of a surface). It means nothing while hasValue is false.

### WouldDeleteExecutionResult

object: The result of a dry run for a target that passed every check: a real run would delete it.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)
- `wouldDelete` (boolean (true), required)

### DeletionExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or WouldDeleteExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of a deletion for one target. On a dry run a target that passed every check gets wouldDelete instead of being deleted.

### DeletionExecutionResults

array of DeletionExecutionResult: A list of deletion results.

### WouldChange

object: What a real run would change on a target. Each command says what its oldValue and newValue are; either is left out when it cannot be told cheaply.
- `oldValue` (any): The target's value now, before the change.
- `newValue` (any): The value a real run would write.

### WouldChangeExecutionResult

object: The result of a dry run for a target that passed every check: a real run would change it as wouldChange says.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)
- `wouldChange` (WouldChange, required)

### ChangeExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or WouldChangeExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of a change for one target. On a dry run a target that passed every check gets wouldChange instead of being changed.

### ChangeExecutionResults

array of ChangeExecutionResult: A list of change results.

Note: elements hidden by the design option combination of the current view (Archicad 29 or newer) fail IsVisibleByRenovation and pass IsOverriddenByRenovation even when the project has no renovation filter; use GetDesignOptionForElements and GetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews to tell them apart.

### CurtainWallPatternLogic

string ("FixedSizes", "BestDivision"): How the pattern unit fills the segment: 'FixedSizes' keeps the given sizes and repeats the unit, which may leave a partial unit at the end (Archicad: Fixed Size); 'BestDivision' stretches the flexible columns/rows so that whole units fill the segment with the least stretching (Archicad: Best Division).

### CurtainWallPatternOrigin

string ("StartWithPattern", "StartFromCenter", "AlignToCenter", "EndWithPattern"): Where the pattern unit is anchored on the segment: at its start, centered with a unit starting at the center, centered with a unit centered on the center, or at its end.

### CurtainWallCrossingFrameType

string ("None", "FromBottomLeftToTopRight", "FromTopLeftToBottomRight"): The diagonal frame of a pattern cell: none, or from the bottom left to the top right corner, or from the top left to the bottom right corner.

### BeamAnchorPoint

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): Anchor point of the beam cross section on a 3x3 grid.

### ColumnCoreAnchor

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): Anchor point of the column core on a 3x3 grid.

### SlabReferencePlaneLocation

string ("Top", "CoreTop", "CoreBottom", "Bottom"): Location of the slab reference plane.

### WallReferenceLineLocation

string ("Outside", "Center", "Inside", "CoreOutside", "CoreCenter", "CoreInside"): The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall (structureType) - a Basic wall has no core skin, and Archicad falls back to the nearest non-core equivalent (e.g. CoreCenter becomes Center).

string ("ByLayout", "ByViewId", "CustomNumber"): How the drawing's title ID is assigned (Identification tabpage of the Drawing Settings dialog).

string ("OriginalColors", "BlackAndWhite", "Grayscale"): How the drawing's pens are output (API_DrawingType::colorMode).

### DrawingAnchorPoint

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): The node of the drawing's bounding box the drawing is placed by (API_DrawingType::anchorPoint). Used only when useOwnOriginAsAnchor is false.

### DrawingStatus

string ("UpToDate", "Modified", "Unknown"): The Drawing Manager's Status column: UpToDate (OK) when the drawing matches its source, Modified when the source changed since the drawing was last updated, Unknown when the status cannot be determined (e.g. a missing external source).

### DrawingLinkType

string ("InternalView", "ExternalView", "Drawing", "DXF_DWG", "PDF", "Image", "PlotMaker", "AddOn", "Unknown", "Other"): The kind of source a drawing is linked to (the Drawing Manager's Source column): a view of this project (InternalView), a view of another Archicad project file (ExternalView), a drawing file, a DWG/DXF file, a PDF, an image, a PlotMaker file, an Add-On generated drawing, or an unknown/other source.

### HotlinkType

string ("Module", "XRef"): Module or XRef.

### Justification

string ("Left", "Center", "Right", "Full"): Text justification.

### LabelClass

string ("Text", "Symbol"): Whether this is a textual or a symbol label.

### TextBoxAnchor

string ("LeftTop", "MiddleTop", "RightTop", "LeftMiddle", "MiddleMiddle", "RightMiddle", "LeftBottom", "MiddleBottom", "RightBottom"): Anchor point of the text box.

### LabelLeaderLineAnchorPoint

string ("Middle", "Top", "Bottom", "Underlined"): How the leader line connects to the label text.

### LabelTextDirection

string ("Parallel", "Horizontal", "Vertical", "General"): Direction of a label's text (API_LabelType textWay), the same for Text and Symbol labels: 'Parallel' follows the labelled element, 'Horizontal' and 'Vertical' are fixed, 'General' is a custom angle (for a Text label style.angle, with style.fixedAngle keeping it when the element is rotated). The Archicad API offers no other direction for labels (it documents only these four), so there is no 'Perpendicular'.

### AssociativeWitnessPoint

object: A witness point of a dimension. Give elementId (with line, inIndex, special, nodeType, nodeStatus and nodeId as needed) for a point associated with an element, or only coordinate for a static point that is not associated with any element, like a point added by hand on empty space. elementId together with coordinate gives an associative point at that location on the element. Points on wall faces (line true) only work on a dimension whose direction is perpendicular to the faces: Archicad rejects or removes a dimension that is even slightly oblique to them (#2505).
- `elementId` (ElementId)
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D): Without elementId: the position of a static (non-associative) witness point; the other fields are ignored for a static point. With elementId: the location of the associative point on the referenced element (written to its base location), e.g. where the dimension line crosses a long or oblique wall face; without it Archicad chooses the point, e.g. the middle of a wall edge. Archicad does not keep it on wall faces (line true): it moves the point to the middle of the face (reported in Archicad 30, #2505). Whether it is kept on other kinds of base is not verified.
- `line` (boolean)
- `inIndex` (integer)
- `special` (integer)
- `nodeType` (integer)
- `nodeStatus` (integer)
- `nodeId` (number)

### CoordinateWitnessPoint

object
- `coordinate` (Coordinate2D)
- `coordinate3D` (Coordinate3D)
- `dimensionPosition` (Coordinate2D)
- `dimensionValue` (number)
- `witnessForm` (string ("None", "Small", "Large", "Fix", "Unknown"))
- `witnessVal` (number)
- `baseElementId` (ElementId)
- `line` (boolean): True when the witness point lies on an edge of the base element rather than at a node (API_Base line).
- `inIndex` (integer): Subindex of the base element's node (API_Neig inIndex).
- `special` (integer): Non-zero for special references such as a wall plane, a beam, window or door hole, or a mesh ridge (API_Base special).
- `nodeType` (integer): Reserved by Archicad for section dimensions (API_Base node_typ).
- `nodeStatus` (integer): Reserved by Archicad for section dimensions (API_Base node_status).
- `nodeId` (number): Polygon vertex id of the base element, from its memo's vertexIDs, for elements with a polygon.
- `textHeight` (number): Character height of the dimension text in mm, as the creation commands take it.
- `textPen` (integer): Pen index of the dimension text.
- `textFrame` (boolean): Whether the dimension text has a frame.
- `textStyle` (DimensionTextStyle): The font and style of the dimension text.
- `content` (string ("MeasuredValue", "CustomText")): Whether the witness point shows the measured value or its custom text (API note contentType), as ModifyAssociativeDimensions' witnessPointTexts takes it.
- `customText` (string): The custom text of the witness point (API note contentUStr), with {MeasuredValue} where the measured value autotext is (Archicad 26 and later). Kept, but not shown, while content is MeasuredValue.
- `superscript` (boolean): Whether the text is superscript (API note effectBits, APIEffect_SuperScript).
- `textPositionFixed` (boolean): Whether the text was moved by hand from its automatic position (API note fixPos); ModifyAssociativeDimensions' resetTextPosition sets it back to false, its textPosition to true.
- `textPosition` (Coordinate2D): Where the text is (API note pos, its left bottom as Archicad keeps it), in the coordinates of the witness points; ModifyAssociativeDimensions' witnessPointTexts[].textPosition takes the same coordinates. Compare them across dimensions to find texts that overlap.

### ElementLinkReference

object: A directional link from one element to another.
- `fromElementId` (ElementId, required): The element the link starts from.
- `toElementId` (ElementId, required): The element the link points to.

### ElementLinkData

object: A directional link from one element to another, with the flags stored on it.
- `fromElementId` (ElementId, required): The element the link starts from.
- `toElementId` (ElementId, required): The element the link points to.
- `flags` (integer): A 32-bit integer stored on the link, free for the script's own use (for example to tell apart the kinds of links it creates). Default is 0.

### ElementLinksOrError

ElementLinks or ErrorItem: The links starting from an element, or an error.

### PropertyId

object: The identifier of a property.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### ElementPropertyObjects

object
- `propertyObjects` (array of ElementPropertyObject, required): The property objects (library parts of the old listing system) of the element, linked to it by criteria or individually. Empty when the element has none.

### ElementPropertyObject

object
- `libraryPartIndex` (integer, required): The index of the property object's library part, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.
- `name` (string): The name of the library part. Absent when the library part cannot be read.
- `guid` (string): The guid of the library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when the library part cannot be read.
- `isIndividuallyAssigned` (boolean, required): True when the property object is assigned to the element individually, false when it is linked by criteria.

### ElementDescriptors

object
- `descriptors` (array of ElementDescriptor, required): The descriptors in the property objects of the element. Empty when the element has none.

### ElementDescriptor

object
- `libraryPartIndex` (integer, required): The index of the library part that declares the descriptor, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.
- `name` (string): The name of the library part. Absent when the library part cannot be read.
- `guid` (string): The guid of the library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when the library part cannot be read.
- `setIndex` (integer, required): The index of the listing database set of the descriptor. Meaningful only when status is Normal.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the descriptor in the listing database set when status is Normal, in the library part when status is Local.
- `status` (ElementDescriptorStatus, required)

### ElementDescriptorStatus

string ("Normal", "Deleted", "Local", "Unknown"): Normal: the descriptor exists in the listing database. Deleted: it is referenced, but deleted from the database. Local: it is defined in the library part. Unknown for a value this version of Tapir does not name.

### ElementLinkedPropertyObjects

object
- `linkByCriteria` (boolean, required): True when the property objects matching their criteria are linked to the element.
- `individualLibraryPartIndex` (integer, required): The index of the library part of the individually assigned property object, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 when no property object is assigned individually.
- `individualLibraryPartName` (string): The name of the individually assigned library part. Absent when there is none or it cannot be read.
- `individualLibraryPartGuid` (string): The guid of the individually assigned library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when there is none or it cannot be read.
- `criteriaPropertyObjects` (array of CriteriaPropertyObject, required): The linked property objects whose criteria match the element.

### CriteriaPropertyObject

object
- `libraryPartIndex` (integer, required): The index of the property object's library part, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.
- `name` (string): The name of the library part. Absent when the library part cannot be read.
- `guid` (string): The guid of the library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when the library part cannot be read.

### BoundingBox3D

object: A 3D bounding box of an element.
- `xMin` (number, required): The minimum X value of the bounding box.
- `yMin` (number, required): The minimum Y value of the bounding box.
- `zMin` (number, required): The minimum Z value of the bounding box.
- `xMax` (number, required): The maximum X value of the bounding box.
- `yMax` (number, required): The maximum Y value of the bounding box.
- `zMax` (number, required): The maximum Z value of the bounding box.

### BoundingBox3DArrayItem

object: A wrapper containing a 3D bounding box.
- `boundingBox3D` (BoundingBox3D, required)

### BoundingBox3DOrError

BoundingBox3DArrayItem or ErrorItem: A 3D bounding box or an error.

### BoundingBoxes3D

array of BoundingBox3DOrError: A list of 3D bounding boxes.

### BoundingBox2DArrayItem

object: A wrapper containing a 2D bounding box.
- `boundingBox2D` (BoundingBox2D, required)

### BoundingBox2DOrError

BoundingBox2DArrayItem or ErrorItem: A 2D bounding box or an error.

### BoundingBoxes2D

array of BoundingBox2DOrError: A list of 2D bounding boxes.

### Body3D

object: One solid body of an element's 3D model: a flat vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces referencing it. The faces are not triangulated: a face is a closed loop of vertex indices (counterclockwise seen from outside the body) plus the loops of its holes.
- `vertices` (array of Coordinate3D, required): The vertices of the body in world coordinates (meters, absolute Z).
- `polygons` (array of object, required): The faces of the body.
  - `vertexIds` (array of integer, required): The outer contour of the face: 0-based indices into vertices.
  - `holes` (array of object): The holes in the face, each a closed loop of 0-based indices into vertices.
  - `surfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface attribute of the face. Left out when the face's material is not a project attribute (for example one defined by a GDL script).

### LibPartUnId

object
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### LibPartDetails

object
- `name` (string, required)
- `parentUnID` (LibPartUnId, required)
- `ownUnID` (LibPartUnId, required)

### StoredGDLParameter

object: A GDL parameter as it is stored with a marker or a Favorite, read without a parameter interface (so without isLocked and possibleValues).
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `displayName` (string, required): The display name of the parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `type` (string, required): The type of the parameter.
- `dimension1` (integer): The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `dimension2` (integer): The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `value` (any): The value of the parameter.
- `valueDescription` (string): The value description for numeric parameter.
- `itemDescriptions` (array of string): Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter, one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.
- `flags` (array of string ("Hidden", "HiddenFromScript", "Disabled", "Child", "Unique", "Fixed", "BoldName", "Open"), required): The flags of the parameter.

object

object: The identifier of a database
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### Hole2D

any or any: A 2D hole in an element defined by closed polylines. The outline is given in 'polygonOutline'; 'polygonCoordinates' is accepted as a legacy alias.
- `polygonOutline` (array of Coordinate2D): The 2D coordinates of the edge of the hole.
- `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D): Legacy alias of polygonOutline.
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Polygon outline arcs of the hole.

### Holes2D

array of Hole2D: A list of 2D holes in an element defined by closed polylines

object: A 3D hole in an element defined by closed polylines
