### CurtainWallDetails

object
- `height` (number, required): The height setting stored on the curtain wall element.
- `actualHeight` (number): The height of the curtain wall as calculated by Archicad (ACAPI_CurtainWall_GetCWHeight). Omitted when Archicad cannot calculate it.
- `zCoordinate` (number, required): The absolute elevation of the bottom of the curtain wall's reference line: its home story's level plus its base level from it (API_CurtainWallType::storyRelLevel, which follows a change of the base offset in Archicad; less offset * cos (angle) on a slanted curtain wall, whose panels the offset lifts), as CreateCurtainWalls and ModifyCurtainWalls take it.
- `referenceLine` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan, one more than its segments (each pair of consecutive coordinates is one segment), as CreateCurtainWalls and ModifyCurtainWalls take them in coordinates. Empty when Archicad cannot return it.
- `flipped` (boolean, required): The side of the reference line the curtain wall is on (API_CurtainWallType::flipped), as ModifyCurtainWalls takes it.
- `offset` (number): The offset of the panels from the reference line (API_CurtainWallType::offset), as ModifyCurtainWalls takes it.
- `nominalWidth` (number): The nominal width (thickness) of the curtain wall (API_CurtainWallType::nominalWidth), as ModifyCurtainWalls takes it.
- `primaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): The column pattern of the curtain wall (the primary grid), as CreateCurtainWalls and ModifyCurtainWalls take it in primaryPattern, so it can be written back as it is. It is the curtain wall's own pattern (API_ElementMemo::cWSegPrimaryPattern of the curtain wall): those commands write one pattern for the whole curtain wall, and Archicad builds every segment from it. A segment whose scheme was changed on its own in Archicad may differ, and writing this pattern back applies it to every segment again. flexibleIndices is always given, because those commands rewrite it each time. Omitted when the pattern has no sizes or uses the number-of-divisions logic, which those commands cannot write; writing the details back without it keeps the pattern.
- `secondaryPattern` (CurtainWallPattern): The row pattern of the curtain wall (the secondary grid, from the bottom up), as CreateCurtainWalls and ModifyCurtainWalls take it in secondaryPattern, so it can be written back as it is. It is the curtain wall's own pattern (API_ElementMemo::cWSegSecondaryPattern of the curtain wall): those commands write one pattern for the whole curtain wall, and Archicad builds every segment from it. A segment whose scheme was changed on its own in Archicad may differ, and writing this pattern back applies it to every segment again. flexibleIndices is always given, because those commands rewrite it each time. Omitted when the pattern has no sizes or uses the number-of-divisions logic, which those commands cannot write; writing the details back without it keeps the pattern.
- `cells` (array of CurtainWallPatternCell): The panel and frame classes of every cell of the pattern unit, as CreateCurtainWalls and ModifyCurtainWalls take them in cells, so they can be written back as they are: one item per cell (the columns of the primary pattern times the rows of the secondary pattern), row by row from the bottom row, each row from the start of the segment. Read from the curtain wall's own cells (API_ElementMemo::cWSegPatternCells of the curtain wall), like the patterns. A class index those commands would refuse (outside the panel and frame classes of the curtain wall, e.g. a customized cell) is left out of its item, so writing the cell back keeps it. Omitted when Archicad returns fewer cells than the pattern unit has.
- `angle` (number, required): The slant angle of the curtain wall plane in degrees, measured from the horizontal (API_CurtainWallType::angle): 90 is vertical, less than 90 leans to the left of the reference line, more than 90 to the right, as CreateCurtainWalls takes it.
- `displayOption` (DisplayOption, required)
- `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation, required)
- `visibility` (StoryVisibility, required)
- `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean, required): When true, Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the curtain wall's vertical extent.
- `cutProjectionMode` (ElemProjectionMode, required): Projection mode of the cut part of the curtain wall on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::cutProjectionMode).
- `uncutProjectionMode` (ElemProjectionMode, required): Projection mode of the uncut part (below the cut plane) of the curtain wall on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::uncutProjectionMode).
- `overheadProjectionMode` (ElemProjectionMode, required): Projection mode of the overhead part (above the cut plane) of the curtain wall on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::overheadProjectionMode).
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen, required): Cut fill foreground pen; the building material's pen can be overridden on the element level. Before Archicad 27 always reported as not overridden.
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen, required): Cut fill background pen; the building material's pen can be overridden on the element level. Before Archicad 27 always reported as not overridden.
- `frameCutLinePen` (integer, required): Pen index of the cut part of the frames on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::frameCutLinePen).
- `frameCutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut part of the frames on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::frameCutLineType). Omitted when not set.
- `panelCutLinePen` (integer, required): Pen index of the cut part of the panels on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::panelCutLinePen).
- `panelCutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut part of the panels on the floor plan (API_CurtainWallType::panelCutLineType). Omitted when not set.
- `useFrameTypesAttributes` (boolean, required): The frames use the attributes of their frame types instead of frameCutLinePen/frameCutLineTypeId.
- `usePanelTypesAttributes` (boolean, required): The panels use the attributes of their panel types instead of panelCutLinePen/panelCutLineTypeId.
- `pen` (integer, required): The pen index of the curtain wall (API_CurtainWallType::pen).
- `belowViewLinePen` (integer, required): Pen index of the curtain wall's view below the cut plane on the floor plan, the uncut lines (API_CurtainWallType::uncutLinePen).
- `belowViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the curtain wall's view below the cut plane on the floor plan, the uncut lines (API_CurtainWallType::uncutLineType). Omitted when not set.
- `aboveViewLinePen` (integer, required): Pen index of the curtain wall's view above the cut plane on the floor plan, the overhead lines (API_CurtainWallType::overheadLinePen).
- `aboveViewLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the curtain wall's view above the cut plane on the floor plan, the overhead lines (API_CurtainWallType::overheadLineType). Omitted when not set.

object

### MeshSkirtType

### MeshModificationData

object: The fields to modify on the Mesh. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.
- `floorIndex` (integer)
- `level` (number): The Z reference level of coordinates.
- `skirtType` (MeshSkirtType)
- `skirtLevel` (number): The height of the skirt.
- `ridges` (MeshRidges)
- `showLines` (boolean): Whether to show secondary mesh lines on plan.
- `contourPen` (integer): Pen attribute index for the mesh contour line.
- `levelPen` (integer): Pen attribute index for the mesh level lines.
- `lineTypeIndex` (integer): Line type attribute index for the mesh contour.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): The building material of the mesh. The surface overrides are kept; send topMaterial, sideMaterial and bottomMaterial with overridden false to show the building material's own surfaces.
- `topMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): Overrides the surface of the top of the mesh; overridden false clears the override.
- `sideMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): Overrides the surface of the sides (skirt) of the mesh; overridden false clears the override.
- `bottomMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): Overrides the surface of the bottom of the mesh; overridden false clears the override.
- `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surface overrides are chained (the chain button of the Model panel).
- `visibility` (StoryVisibility): The stories the contour of the mesh is shown on. Only the given fields change.
- `fillVisibility` (StoryVisibility): The stories the cover fill of the mesh is shown on. Only the given fields change.
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the pen of the cut fill (shown on solid meshes); overridden false clears the override.
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen): Overrides the background pen of the cut fill (shown on solid meshes); overridden false clears the override.
- `sectionContourPen` (integer): Pen of the contour of the mesh where it is cut in sections.
- `floorFill` (MeshFloorFill): The cover fill of the mesh in the floor plan. Only the given fields change.
- `polygonCoordinates` (array of Coordinate3D): The 3D coordinates of the outline polygon of the mesh. Replaces the existing boundary entirely; the existing outline arcs are removed unless polygonArcs is also given, and the existing holes are kept unless holes is also given. Where a level line (sublines) crosses the new outline or a hole, Archicad adds a point; each given point keeps its own z, and an added point gets the z interpolated along the edge between the given points next to it.
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Polygon outline arcs of the mesh. Replaces the existing outline arcs; when given without polygonCoordinates, they apply to the existing outline.
- `holes` (array of Hole3D): The 3D holes of the mesh. Replaces all existing holes; an empty array removes them. When given without polygonCoordinates, the existing outline is kept.
- `sublines` (array of MeshSubline): The leveling sublines inside the polygon of the mesh. Replaces existing sublines entirely.

### StoryVisibility

object: Per-story visibility settings (API_StoryVisibility): the home story, plus how many stories above/below also show this element.
- `showOnHome` (boolean): Show on the home story.
- `showAllAbove` (boolean): Show on all stories above the home story.
- `showAllBelow` (boolean): Show on all stories below the home story.

- `showRelBelow` (integer): Show this many stories below the home story (ignored when showAllBelow is true).

### MorphBody

object: A Morph's full body geometry: an indexed vertex list plus one entry per face (polygon). Shared shape between GetDetailsOfElements' output and CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs' input - what Get reports is what Create/Modify accept back. There is no fillet/chamfer operation in the Archicad API - a caller wanting rounded geometry must supply the already-tessellated facets here; edgeOverrides only controls how an existing straight edge is DISPLAYED (hidden/visible/smooth-shaded), not its shape.
- `bodyType` (string ("Solid", "Surface")): Whether the body is a closed solid or an open surface shell. Reported accurately on Get; on Create/Modify this is set on the element but a confirmed Archicad SDK bug means it may not take effect (bodyType has been observed always coming back Solid regardless of what was requested - see edgeOverrides' note).
- `isClosed` (boolean): READ-ONLY, Get output only (ignored if sent to Create/Modify). Geometrically computed from the body's edges: true if every edge in the body has exactly two adjacent faces (a watertight/manifold volume), false if any edge borders only one face (an open shell / has holes or gaps). Distinct from bodyType, which is the caller's declared INTENT (Solid vs Surface) rather than the actual computed geometry - a body can be declared bodyType 'Solid' yet still be geometrically open if a face is missing.
- `edgeDefault` (string ("HardVisible", "HardHidden", "SoftHidden")): Default display status for every edge that has no entry in edgeOverrides. Reported accurately on Get. On Create/Modify it takes effect from Archicad 29 on, where it is applied to every edge of the element with ACAPI_Element_ChangeMorphEdgeType right after the element is created or changed (e.g. 'HardHidden' hides all edges of a triangulated body). The Morph's layer must be shown and unlocked: on a hidden or locked layer CreateMorphs creates no Morph and returns an error. On Archicad 28 and earlier it is set on the element but does not take effect due to the same confirmed Archicad SDK bug as edgeOverrides (element.morph.edgeType is silently discarded by ACAPI_Element_Create/Change).
- `vertices` (array of Coordinate3D, required): Flat, indexed vertex list, local to the Morph's own placement (not world coordinates). A Solid body needs at least 4 (a tetrahedron, the minimum closed volume); a Surface body has no closedness requirement at all - the minimum is 2 vertices joined by a single wireEdge (a lone vertex with no edge at all is rejected by Archicad itself, confirmed live) - enforced with a bodyType-aware error message, not by this minItems floor alone.
- `polygons` (array of MorphPolygon): One entry per face loop (into `vertices`), counterclockwise as seen from outside the body. Optional - a body made entirely of wireEdges (see below) needs none. Set "filled": false on an entry to create only that loop's edges (e.g. the outline of a pyramid's side faces) without an actual filled face.
- `wireEdges` (array of object): Standalone edges that belong to no face at all (e.g. a bare rectangle outline, or a pyramid with a filled base but wireframe-only sides - set "filled": false on a polygons entry for a whole closed loop like that instead, this is for individual edges not already covered by any polygon loop). Reported accurately by GetDetailsOfElements (every edge with zero adjacent faces); accepted back by CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs. Identifies an edge by the (unordered) pair of vertex indices it connects - reuses whatever edge already exists between those two vertices if the polygons above happen to share it.
  - `vertexIds` (array of integer, required)
- `edgeOverrides` (array of object): READ-ONLY in practice: reported accurately by GetDetailsOfElements (reflecting whatever Archicad itself currently has), but CreateMorphs/ModifyMorphs silently ignore this field on input - per-edge display status cannot be set by an add-on due to a confirmed, still-unresolved Archicad SDK bug (element.morph.edgeType/bodyType are silently discarded by ACAPI_Element_Create/Change; see the GRAPHISOFT community forum thread 'Help with setting morph's hidden edges in the API'). To hide or smooth ALL edges of a Morph use edgeDefault, which does take effect from Archicad 29 on. Sparse when present - only edges whose display status differs from edgeDefault get an entry. Identifies an edge by the (unordered) pair of vertex indices it connects.
  - `vertexIds` (array of integer, required)
  - `hidden` (boolean): Hide this edge's line entirely.
  - `smooth` (boolean): Shade the two adjacent faces smoothly across this edge instead of as a hard crease - the 'aide a la courbe' rounded-look hint. Does not change actual geometry.
  - `silhouetteOnly` (boolean): Show this edge's line only where it forms a silhouette/contour from the current viewpoint.

### MorphDetails

object
- `origin` (Coordinate3D, required): Translation component of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's origin column).
- `xAxis` (Coordinate3D): X axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's first column). Omit on Create to get an identity rotation; give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.
- `yAxis` (Coordinate3D): Y axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's second column). Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.
- `zAxis` (Coordinate3D): Z axis of the Morph's placement transform (tranmat's third column). Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together or none at all.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): The Morph's building material - a single, whole-volume property (what the mass is 'made of', governing cut-fill/quantity takeoff), NOT settable per face. Per-face appearance is controlled separately by each polygon's own surfaceId (see MorphBody) - confirmed live these are two independent, unrelated attributes (a Morph can have one uniform building material while showing a different Surface finish on each face).
- `surfaceId` (AttributeId): The Morph's own default Surface (element.morph.material) - used for any face that has no per-face surfaceId override of its own (see MorphBody polygons[].surfaceId). Distinct from buildingMaterialId (the whole-volume material). Confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this specific field when set through ACAPI_Element_Create alone (reproduced identically on Archicad 27 and 29 - not a version-specific issue, unlike polygons[].surfaceId below); CreateMorphs works around this transparently with an internal follow-up Change right after Create, so this field behaves correctly end-to-end despite the underlying quirk.
- `body` (MorphBody, required)
- `castShadow` (boolean): Whether the body casts shadow in 3D.
- `receiveShadow` (boolean): Whether the body receives shadow in 3D.
- `isAutoOnStoryVisibility` (boolean): When true, the per-story visibility (showContour/showFill) is calculated automatically from the Morph's vertical extent instead of using the explicit values.
- `showContour` (StoryVisibility): Which stories display this Morph's contour. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Create/Modify do not reliably apply it (showAllBelow/showRelAbove/showRelBelow silently come back reset even when explicitly set and isAutoOnStoryVisibility is false) - the same class of confirmed Archicad SDK write bug as bodyType/edgeType (see MorphBody's notes). Set on the element regardless since doing so is harmless and forward-compatible.
- `showFill` (StoryVisibility): Which stories display this Morph's floor plan fill. Same write-reliability caveat as showContour.
- `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
- `displayOption` (DisplayOption)
- `viewDepthLimitation` (ViewDepthLimitation)
- `cutFillPen` (integer): Overridden cut fill foreground pen (otherwise inherited from the building material). Omit to leave uninherited/unset.
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (integer): Overridden cut fill background pen (otherwise inherited from the building material). Omit to leave uninherited/unset.
- `cutLineType` (AttributeId): Line type of the cut contour.
- `cutLinePen` (integer): Pen of the cut contour.
- `uncutLineType` (AttributeId): Line type of the (uncut) contour.
- `uncutLinePen` (integer): Pen of the (uncut) contour.
- `overheadLineType` (AttributeId): Line type of the overhead part (floor plan only).
- `overheadLinePen` (integer): Pen of the overhead part (floor plan only).
- `useCoverFillType` (boolean): Use a dedicated floor plan fill instead of the one from the building material.
- `outlineContourDisplay` (boolean): Outline contour display.
- `coverFillType` (AttributeId): Floor plan fill type (only used when useCoverFillType is true).
- `coverFillPen` (integer): Floor plan fill foreground pen.
- `coverFillBGPen` (integer): Floor plan fill background pen.
- `use3DHatching` (boolean): Derive the floor plan fill from the 3D material instead of coverFillType.
- `coverFillOrientation` (CoverFillOrientation)
- `useDistortedCoverFill` (boolean): Show the floor plan hatching as if projected onto a plane.
- `textureProjectionType` (TextureProjectionType)
- `textureProjectionCoords` (array of Coordinate3D): Texture projection coordinate system: origin, then 3 axis endpoints.
- `level` (number): Height of the Morph's origin (the z of its placement transform) above its home story. Archicad works it out from the placement; CreateMorphs and ModifyMorphs take it and place the Morph's origin at this height.

### DrawingDetails

object
- `pos` (Coordinate2D, required): Position of the drawing on the layout, in meters. Without a clip polygon it is the lower left corner of the drawing (before rotation); with one it is where the origin of the source view lands (a modelOffset can move it by modelOffset * drawingScale).
- `offset` (Coordinate2D): Output only (API_DrawingType::offset). Equal to pos when isCutWithFrame is true; otherwise the subvector of pos and the anchorPoint's coordinate on the drawing's bounding box. Unlike pos, this is always where the source view's model origin lands on the layout, regardless of anchorPoint/useOwnOriginAsAnchor.
- `angle` (number, required): Rotation angle of the drawing in radians.
- `ratio` (number, required): Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view.
- `drawingScale` (number, required): The scale of the drawing, taken from its source view (e.g. 0.01 for 1:100).
- `modelOffset` (Coordinate2D, required): Offset of the model origin within the drawing, in model meters. Used only by clipped drawings; Archicad then adds modelOffset * drawingScale (times ratio, rotated by angle) to pos.
- `isCutWithFrame` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing is clipped by a custom polygon (see clipPolygon) instead of showing the full auto-fit extent.
- `bounds` (BoundingBox2D, required): Bounds of the drawing on the layout.
- `clipPolygon` (array of Coordinate2D): Polygon used to clip the drawing view, in layout coordinates (meters on the layout, the same coordinate system as pos and bounds - not the coordinates of the source view's model). Archicad stores it as is; pos, angle, ratio and modelOffset are not applied to it. Present only when isCutWithFrame is true.
- `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): Archicad's internal identifier of this Drawing's link (API_DrawingType::drawingGuid as Archicad reports it). This is NOT the navigator item id of the source view: CreateDrawings passes the source view in this field, but once the Drawing is created Archicad reports its own identifier, which is different for every Drawing (even two Drawings of the same view), is neither the source view nor the Drawing's item in the Layout Book, and is not accepted by navigator commands such as GetViewSettings. To find the source view of a placed Drawing, use the sourceNavigatorItemId of its DrawingItem in the Layout Book tree (GetNavigatorItemTree). Read-only: Archicad has no API to relink a Drawing to a different source (see ChangeDrawingLink).
- `nameType` (DrawingNameType, required)
- `customName` (string): The drawing's custom title name. Present only when nameType is CustomName.
- `numberingType` (DrawingNumberingType, required)
- `customNumber` (string): The drawing's custom title ID. Present only when numberingType is CustomNumber.
- `isInNumbering` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing is included in the automatic drawing numbering sequence.
- `isScaleIncludedInAutotextAndIndex` (boolean, required): The 'Include scale in Autotext and index' checkbox of Drawing Settings (API_DrawingType::includeInAutoTextsAndIES): whether the drawing's scale is included in the 'Drawing Scale' and 'Original Scale' Autotexts and in indexes.
- `hasBorderLine` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing shows a printable border (Drawing Settings > Frame > Add Printable Border).
- `borderLineTypeIndex` (integer, required): Attribute index of the line type of the drawing's border.
- `borderPenIndex` (integer, required): Pen index of the drawing's border.
- `borderSize` (number, required): Border size of the drawing (API_DrawingType::borderSize), in meters.
- `penTableUsageMode` (DrawingPenTableUsageMode, required)
- `penTableIndex` (integer, required): Attribute index of the pen set the drawing uses when penTableUsageMode is PenTableIndex (API_DrawingType::penTableIndex).
- `colorMode` (DrawingColorMode, required)
- `isTransparentBackground` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing's background is transparent (API_DrawingType::isTransparentBk).
- `rasterizeDPI` (number, required): The resolution, in dots per inch, a PDF drawing is rasterized at (API_DrawingType::rasterizeDPI).
- `anchorPoint` (DrawingAnchorPoint, required)
- `useOwnOriginAsAnchor` (boolean, required): Whether the drawing is placed by its own origin instead of anchorPoint (API_DrawingType::useOwnOrigoAsAnchor).
- `manualUpdate` (boolean, required): The Drawing Manager's Update Type: true for Manual, false for Automatic. Read-only.
- `storedInProject` (boolean, required): The Drawing Manager's Stored in Project column: whether the drawing's content is stored in the project file. Read-only.
- `status` (DrawingStatus): The Drawing Manager's Status column. Read-only; absent when Archicad could not check the drawing.
- `linkType` (DrawingLinkType): The Drawing Manager's Source column: what kind of source the drawing is linked to. Read-only; absent when the link could not be read.
- `linkPath` (string): Path of the drawing's external source file (the Drawing Manager's Path column). Present only when the source is a file (external view, DWG/DXF, PDF, image, ...). Read-only.
- `sourceNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId): The navigator item (view or viewpoint) the drawing shows, as the sourceNavigatorItemId of its Layout Book item; GetViewSettings accepts it. Absent when the source is not a navigator item (external file). Read-only.
- `titleLibraryPartIndex` (number, required): Library part index of the drawing title (API_DrawingTitle::libInd). A negative/invalid index means no title object is instantiated; setting it to a valid index (e.g. copied from another drawing) makes Archicad create the title's own placed element.
- `titleElementId` (ElementId): Id of the drawing title, itself a placed GDL object element (font/pen/size aside, its own settings are reachable like any other element, e.g. with GetGDLParametersOfElements/SetGDLParametersOfElements). Absent if the drawing has no title object.

### LabelDetails

object
- `libPart` (LibPartDetails)
- `ownerElementId` (ElementId)
- `ownerElementType` (ElementType)
- `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `midCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `hasLeaderLine` (boolean, required)
- `labelClass` (LabelClass, required)
- `leaderLine` (LabelLeaderLineDetails, required)
- `textWay` (LabelTextDirection): The label's text direction, for a Text or a Symbol label (a Symbol label also reports it in symbolStyle.textWay).
- `style` (TextStyleDetails): Present only when labelClass is 'Text'.
- `symbolStyle` (LabelSymbolStyleSettableDetails): Present only when labelClass is 'Symbol'.
- `text` (string): Present only when labelClass is 'Text'.
- `rawText` (string): Present only when labelClass is 'Text' and Archicad's autotext flag could be switched for the read: the text content read with that flag turned off, so an autotext shows its key (e.g. '<PROJECTNUMBER>') instead of its value.
- `paragraphCount` (integer): Present only when labelClass is 'Text'. Read-only: number of paragraphs in the memo (Tapir's own Create/Modify commands write one paragraph per line of the content).
- `lines` (array of string): Present only when labelClass is 'Text' and Archicad reports the line starts. Read-only: the lines as Archicad lays the text out, the breaks of a wrapped text included, each without the line-end characters that end it.
- `lineStarts` (array of integer): Present with 'lines'. Read-only: the offset in 'text' of the first character of each entry of 'lines'.
- `runs` (array of TextRunDetails): Present only when labelClass is 'Text' and the content has paragraphs (always for content Tapir created): one entry per styled run, a single run too.

### DimensionOrigin

string ("ProjectZero", "ReferenceLevel1", "ReferenceLevel2", "StoredOrigin", "Altitude"): The origin a level dimension measures from.

### LayeredElementDimensions

object: The automatic dimensioning of layered (composite) elements, from the Dimension Details panel of the Dimension Settings (API compAutoThick).
- `total` (boolean): Dimension the total thickness.
- `core` (boolean): Dimension the core.
- `referenceLine` (boolean): Dimension the reference line.

### LevelDimensionDetails

object
- `position` (Coordinate2D, required): The location of the marker.
- `level` (number, required): The level the dimension shows in meters: the height of the owner element at the position for an associative level dimension, the floor level or the static value otherwise.
- `staticLevel` (boolean, required): The Static checkbox as Archicad reports it; ModifyLevelDimensions switches it. A level dimension created with a fixed 'level' and no parent keeps that value although Archicad has been seen to read this flag as false for it.
- `ownerElementId` (ElementId): Present when the level dimension has an owner element: the element it measures. ModifyLevelDimensions takes it back with the same key.
- `ownerElementType` (ElementType): Present when the level dimension has an owner element. Only read.
- `dimForm` (integer, required): Marker type 0-19.
- `needPlus` (boolean, required)
- `pen` (integer, required)
- `textHeight` (number, required): Height of the dimension text in millimeters.
- `textPen` (integer, required)
- `markerSize` (number, required): Size of the marker in millimeters.
- `angle` (number, required): Rotation angle of the marker in radians.
- `origin` (DimensionOrigin, required)
- `fontIndex` (integer, required): Font attribute index of the dimension text.
- `fontName` (string): The name of the font fontIndex refers to, as the Font attributes carry it. Absent when no loaded font has that index.
- `bold` (boolean, required): Bold dimension text.
- `italic` (boolean, required): Italic dimension text.
- `underline` (boolean, required): Underlined dimension text.
- `hideWithBaseElem` (boolean): Hide the dimension together with its associated element. Read from Archicad 29; absent on earlier versions.
- `textContent` (string ("Measured", "Custom"), required): Content of the dimension text: 'Measured' (the level value) or 'Custom' (customText).
- `customText` (string): The custom content of the dimension text, with its Autotext keys as keys (read with the autotext flag off), in the form CreateLevelDimensions and ModifyLevelDimensions take. Present when textContent is 'Custom'.
- `secondTextContent` (string ("Measured", "Custom"), required): Content of the second text, shown by the marker types with two texts: 'Measured' or 'Custom' (secondCustomText).
- `secondCustomText` (string): The custom content of the second text, as customText. Present when secondTextContent is 'Custom'.

### AngleDimensionLine

object: A line measured by an angle dimension, given by two of its points. The angle is measured between the two lines (they are extended to their intersection, the center of the dimension arc).
- `begCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
- `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)

### AngleDimensionDetails

object
- `firstLine` (AngleDimensionLine, required): The first measured line: its first two reference points.
- `secondLine` (AngleDimensionLine, required): The second measured line: its last two reference points.
- `arcPosition` (Coordinate2D, required): The point the dimension arc was fitted to.
- `arcCenter` (Coordinate2D, required): The center of the dimension arc, the intersection of the two lines.
- `radius` (number, required): The radius of the dimension arc.
- `measuredAngle` (number, required): The angle the dimension measures, in radians.
- `smallArc` (boolean, required): Whether the smaller angle between the lines is measured (inner dimension) rather than the larger one.
- `pen` (integer, required): Pen index of the dimension and witness lines.
- `textHeight` (number, required): Height of the dimension text in millimeters.
- `textPen` (integer, required): Pen index of the dimension text.

### DimensionDetails

object: The settings of a linear dimension (the Dimension tool), with the names ModifyAssociativeDimensions takes, and the texts of its witness points. The witness points themselves are read with GetDimensionData.
- `appearance` (string ("Linear", "Cumulative", "Baseline", "Elevation"), required): The dimension type, as in the Dimension Settings.
- `elevationOrigin` (DimensionOrigin, required): The level an Elevation dimension measures from (kept for the other types too).
- `elevationMarker` (DimensionElevationMarker, required): The marker of an Elevation dimension, always with all of its fields (kept for the other types too).
- `dimensionLinePosition` (Coordinate2D, required): A point of the dimension line.
- `direction` (Coordinate2D, required): The direction of the dimension line.
- `witnessPointCount` (integer, required): The number of witness points.
- `linePen` (integer, required): The pen of the dimension and witness lines.
- `marker` (DimensionMarker, required): The marker at the witness points, always with its type, pen and size.
- `textPlacement` (DimensionTextPlacement, required): The text placement method of the dimension texts, always with all of its fields.
- `textHeight` (number, required): The text height of the dimension's settings in millimeters. Each witness point keeps its own (GetDimensionData).
- `textPen` (integer, required): The text pen of the dimension's settings. Each witness point keeps its own (GetDimensionData).
- `textFrame` (boolean, required): The text frame of the dimension's settings. Each witness point keeps its own (GetDimensionData).
- `textStyle` (DimensionTextStyle, required): The font and style of the texts of the dimension's settings. Each witness point keeps its own (GetDimensionData).
- `defaultWitnessForm` (string ("None", "Small", "Large", "Fix", "Unknown"), required): The witness line form of the dimension's settings; each witness point has its own witnessForm.
- `defaultWitnessVal` (number, required): The value that goes with defaultWitnessForm, in meters. Each witness point has its own witnessVal.
- `staticDimension` (boolean, required): The Static dimension checkbox of the Dimension Settings (API defStaticDim).
- `onlyDimensionText` (boolean, required): Whether only the dimension texts are shown, without the dimension and witness lines (API onlyDimensionText).
- `openingHeightsInChain` (boolean, required): Whether the opening heights are shown in the dimension chain (Dimension Details panel, API detailedHoleDim).
- `openingHeightsNominal` (boolean, required): Whether the opening heights are the nominal heights, without the oversize (API nominalHoleDim; false: with the oversize).
- `layeredElementDimensions` (LayeredElementDimensions, required)
- `witnessPointTexts` (array of DimensionWitnessPointText): The text of every witness point, in the order GetDimensionData returns them, with the keys ModifyAssociativeDimensions' witnessPointTexts takes, so the list read can be sent back as it is. Missing when the witness points cannot be read.

### DimensionWitnessPointText

object: The text of one witness point of a linear dimension, as the dimension text of a selected witness point in Archicad: the measured value or a custom text, superscript, and the text's position. ModifyAssociativeDimensions writes the given fields of the given witness points (witnessPointTexts); GetDetailsOfElements reads it for every witness point with the same keys (index, content, superscript, customText for a custom text and textPosition for a text moved by hand).
- `index` (integer, required): The witness point whose text is changed, counted from 0 in the order GetDimensionData returns them.
- `content` (string ("MeasuredValue", "CustomText")): Optional: show the measured value or the custom text (API note contentType).
- `customText` (string): Optional custom text of the witness point (API note contentUStr). Write {MeasuredValue} where the measured value goes, e.g. "{MeasuredValue} ok" (Archicad 26 and later; Archicad 25 refuses it). A line break is \r (Archicad shows \n on one line). Without content the witness point shows the custom text. GetDetailsOfElements reads it only while content is CustomText; GetDimensionData also reads the custom text a witness point keeps while it shows the measured value.
- `superscript` (boolean): Optional: show the text superscript (API note effectBits, APIEffect_SuperScript).
- `resetTextPosition` (boolean): Optional: true puts a text that was moved by hand back to its automatic position (API note fixPos false); false changes nothing. Cannot be given with textPosition. Only written: GetDetailsOfElements leaves out textPosition for a text at its automatic position instead.
- `textPosition` (Coordinate2D): Optional: moves the text there and fixes it, as dragging it by hand does (API note pos, fixPos true). In the coordinates GetDimensionData returns the witness points and the textPosition of each text in, so a text can be moved relative to where it is. GetDetailsOfElements reads it only for a text that was moved by hand (fixed), so the texts read can be sent back without fixing the automatic ones.

### ChangeMarkerComponent

string ("HeadOnly", "CloudOnly", "HeadAndCloud"): Which parts a Change Marker shows: only the marker head, only the cloud, or both.

### ChangeMarkerDetails

object: A Change Marker: the revision Change it is linked to, the parts it shows and its geometry.
- `linkType` (string ("Linked", "Unlinked", "NewChange", "Unknown"), required): Whether the marker is linked to a Change. NewChange is the value a marker is created with to make a new Change.
- `markerComponent` (ChangeMarkerComponent, required)
- `changeId` (string, required): The ID of the linked Change (empty when not linked).
- `changeDescription` (string, required): The description (short name) of the linked Change.
- `position` (Coordinate2D, required): The point the Change Marker points to.
- `polygon` (array of Coordinate2D): The outline of the cloud, with the closing point. Present only when the marker has a polygon.
- `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): The curved edges of polygon. Present only when it has any.
- `markerId` (ElementId): The GUID of the marker head's library part element. Present only when the marker has one.
- `angle` (number, required): The rotation angle of the marker head in radians.
- `horizontalMarker` (boolean, required): Whether the marker head is always horizontal.

### DimensionTextStyle

object: The font and style of the texts of a linear dimension, as in the Dimension Settings' text panel (API_NoteType noteFont, faceBits, widthFactor, spacingFactor). Taken as textStyle by CreateAssociativeDimensions, CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection, CreateWallThicknessDimensions and ModifyAssociativeDimensions, where only the fields given are changed, and returned by GetDetailsOfElements and, per witness point, by GetDimensionData.
- `fontIndex` (integer): Font attribute index, as GetFontsByName reports it. On input it must be the index of a loaded font; fontName wins when both are given.
- `fontName` (string): Name of the font, as the Font attributes carry it, e.g. 'Arial'. On input resolved to the font's index like a Text style's fontName, taking precedence over fontIndex, and failing when no loaded font has the name; on read-back the name of the font fontIndex refers to, absent when no loaded font has that index.
- `bold` (boolean)
- `italic` (boolean)
- `underline` (boolean)
- `widthFactor` (number): Width scale of the characters (1 is 100 %).
- `spacingFactor` (number): Spacing scale between the characters (1 is 100 %).

### DimensionMarker

object: The marker at the witness points of a linear dimension (API_MarkerData). CreateAssociativeDimensions and the other dimension commands take any of its fields; GetDetailsOfElements and GetDimensionData always return all three.
- `type` (string ("CrossLine", "EmptyCircle", "SlashLine60", "OpenArrow30", "ClosedArrow30", "FullArrow30", "SlashLine45", "CrossCircle", "OpenArrow90", "ClosedArrow90", "FullArrow90", "FullCircle", ...)): The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.
- `pen` (integer): The pen of the marker.
- `size` (number): The marker size, the API's markerData.markerSize, which the DevKit calls the size in millimeters at the drawing scale. Compare it with the marker size of the Dimension Settings before relying on it: on Archicad 29 a linear dimension whose dialog showed 1.0 read 2.5 here.

### DimensionTextPlacement

object: The text placement method of a linear dimension's texts, as in the Dimension Settings (API dimLayout, placeUnderEnabled, pushNeighborEnabled). The dimension commands take any of its fields; GetDetailsOfElements and GetDimensionData always return all three.
- `method` (string ("Classic", "Flexible", "Centered", "Off", "Unknown")): Classic (the API's API_Legacy, the placement of Archicad 18 and before), Flexible, Centered, or Off (every text in the middle of its segment, without collision detection). Unknown is only returned, for a value this version of Tapir does not know.
- `placeBelowLine` (boolean): Flexible method: a text that does not fit may be placed below the dimension line (API placeUnderEnabled).
- `pushNeighbors` (boolean): Flexible method: a text may push its neighbouring texts aside (API pushNeighborEnabled).

### DimensionElevationMarker

object: The marker an Elevation dimension (appearance Elevation, e.g. a height chain in a section) draws at its witness points, set under Elevation dimension in the Dimension Settings (API ed_dimForm, ed_arrowAng, ed_arrowFill, ed_arrowUp, ed_needPlus). The dimension commands take any of its fields; GetDetailsOfElements and GetDimensionData always return all five, for the other dimension types too.
- `form` (integer): The marker form as Archicad stores it (API ed_dimForm; the DevKit does not list the values, the commands take 0 to 19, as for the Level Dimension tool's dimForm): read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an Elevation dimension that has the wanted marker.
- `arrowAngle` (integer (30, 45, 60)): The angle of the half arrow in degrees (API ed_arrowAng 0, 1, 2).
- `arrowFilled` (boolean): Whether the arrow is filled (API ed_arrowFill).
- `arrowUp` (boolean): Whether the arrow points up (API ed_arrowUp; false: down).
- `plusSign` (boolean): Whether positive values get a "+" sign (API ed_needPlus).

### RadialDimensionDetails

object: A radial dimension, as Archicad stores it. The Archicad API does not document how the measured arc is stored (the meaning of basePoint and ownerElementInIndex), so these are the raw values; ownerArcCenter is read from the measured arc or circle.
- `basePoint` (Coordinate2D, required): The base point of the dimension as Archicad stores it (API_RadialDimensionType base.loc).
- `dimensionLineEnd` (Coordinate2D, required): The end of the radial dimension line.
- `radius` (number, required): The radius the dimension measures, in meters.
- `ownerElementId` (ElementId): Present only when the dimension is linked to an element: the element it measures.
- `ownerElementType` (ElementType): Present only when the dimension is linked to an element.
- `ownerElementInIndex` (integer): Present only when the dimension is linked to an element: the index of the measured part of that element, as Archicad stores it.
- `ownerElementLine` (boolean): Present only when the dimension is linked to an element: whether the dimension is linked to a line or arc of that element rather than to a node, as Archicad stores it.
- `ownerArcCenter` (Coordinate2D): Present only when the measured element is an arc or a circle: its centre.
- `ownerArcRadius` (number): Present only when the measured element is an arc or a circle: its radius in meters.
- `linePen` (integer, required): The pen of the dimension line.
- `marker` (object, required): The marker at the end of the dimension line.
  - `type` (string ("CrossLine", "EmptyCircle", "SlashLine60", "OpenArrow30", "ClosedArrow30", "FullArrow30", "SlashLine45", "CrossCircle", "OpenArrow90", "ClosedArrow90", "FullArrow90", "FullCircle", ...), required): The marker type, named after API_MarkerID.
  - `pen` (integer, required): The pen of the marker.
  - `size` (number, required): The size of the marker as Archicad stores it, in millimeters.
- `textHeight` (number, required): The height of the dimension text in millimeters.
- `textPen` (integer, required): The pen of the dimension text.
- `textPosition` (string ("Above", "In", "Below", "Unknown"), required): Where the text is, relative to the dimension line.
- `textDirection` (string ("Horizontal", "Vertical", "Radial", "Unknown"), required): The direction of the text.
- `textContent` (string ("Measured", "Custom"), required): Whether the text shows the measured radius or a custom text.
- `showOrigin` (boolean, required): Whether the centre of the arc is marked.
- `onlyDimensionText` (boolean, required): Whether only the dimension text is shown, without the dimension line.

### TextDetails

object
- `text` (string, required): The text content. Newlines separate the lines.
- `rawText` (string): The text content as read with Archicad's autotext flag turned off, so an autotext shows its key (e.g. '<PROJECTNUMBER>') instead of its value. Present only when the flag could be switched for the read.
- `position` (Coordinate2D, required): The placement position of the text. ModifyTexts takes it back with the same key (and as coordinate with a z).
- `angle` (number, required): The rotation angle in radians (same as style.angle).
- `height` (number, required): The character height in millimeters (same as style.height).
- `pen` (integer, required): The pen attribute index (same as style.penIndex).
- `justification` (Justification, required): Same as style.justification.
- `zCoordinate` (number, required): The level of the text's floor.
- `width` (number): The wrap width in mm, as CreateTexts and ModifyTexts write it with the same key: the box width (style.boxWidth) while word wrap is on (style.nonBreaking false), 0 for an auto-width text.
- `style` (TextStyleDetails, required): The flat fields above are the subset SetDetailsOfElements takes back.
- `paragraphCount` (integer, required): Read-only: number of paragraphs in the memo (Tapir's own Create/Modify commands write one paragraph per line of the content).
- `lines` (array of string): Read-only: the lines as Archicad lays the text out, the breaks of a wrapped text (style.nonBreaking false) included, each without the line-end characters that end it. Present when Archicad reports the line starts.
- `lineStarts` (array of integer): Read-only: the offset in 'text' of the first character of each entry of 'lines'.
- `runs` (array of TextRunDetails): The styled runs of the content, present whenever the content has paragraphs (always for content Tapir created); one entry per run, a single run too, as a run may carry a pen, font, face or size of its own. Concatenating the runs' text in order gives the full content.

### StairTreadDetails

object: A tread of a stair (API_StairTreadType), as GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists them in stairTreads. Its GDL parameters are read by GetGDLParametersOfElements.
- `role` (string ("Run", "Landing"), required): Whether the tread is on a flight (Run) or a landing.
- `visible` (boolean, required): Whether the tread is shown.
- `isCustom` (boolean, required): Whether the tread has its own settings instead of those of the stair.
- `nosingType` (string ("ByValue", "BySlanting"), required): How the nosing is defined: by a value (nosingValue) or by slanting the riser (nosingSlant).
- `nosingValue` (number, required): The nosing length.
- `nosingSlant` (number, required): The slant of the nosing.
- `offset` (number, required): The offset of the tread (API_StairTreadType::offset).
- `thickness` (number, required): The thickness of the tread.
- `zOffset` (number, required): The vertical offset of the tread (API_StairTreadType::zOffset).
- `stairId` (ElementId, required): The stair the tread belongs to.

### StairRiserDetails

object: A riser of a stair (API_StairRiserType), as GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists them in stairRisers. Its GDL parameters are read by GetGDLParametersOfElements.
- `role` (string ("Run", "Landing"), required): Whether the riser is on a flight (Run) or a landing.
- `visible` (boolean, required): Whether the riser is shown.
- `riserPosition` (string ("OnTread", "BehindTread"), required): Whether the riser stands on the tread below or behind it.
- `crossSection` (string ("Simple", "Slanted"), required): The cross section of the riser.
- `angle` (number, required): The slant angle of a slanted riser (API_StairRiserType::angle).
- `offset` (number, required): The offset of the riser (API_StairRiserType::offset).
- `thickness` (number, required): The thickness of the riser.
- `stairId` (ElementId, required): The stair the riser belongs to.

### StairDetails

object: The settings of a Stair element: the ones CreateStairs takes, and its floor plan and section display (stairDisplayType and the fields after it), of which CreateStairs and ModifyStairs write stairDisplayType, structureVisibility and, in floorPlanLayout and reflectedCeilingPlanLayout, storyVisibility and the show... switches. The finishes and the structure are modeled by the Stair's subelements (risers, treads and structures), which GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements lists; structures gives the structure settings they are built from, and GetDetailsOfElements reads a StairStructure subelement with the same keys.
- `stepNum` (integer, required): Number of risers (steps).
- `riserHeight` (number, required): Height of each riser.
- `treadDepth` (number): The going (the length of each tread), measured along the walking line: its length divided by the number of treads. The going stored in the Stair's settings (API_StairType::treadDepth) is not used, since Archicad does not keep it in step with the modeled treads (a placed stair reads 0 or 1 there). Not given for a stair with a landing, whose walking line runs across the landing too; take its going from the geometry of its treads or risers (Get3DGeometryOfElements).
- `flightWidth` (number, required): Width of the stair flight.
- `totalHeight` (number, required): Total height of the stair. With a top link (set by relativeTopStory in CreateStairs and ModifyStairs) Archicad computes it from the story levels and topOffset. Archicad does not return the top link itself when the stair is read, so it is not reported here.
- `topOffset` (number, required): The offset of the top of the stair from the level of the linked top story (for example -0.15); only used when the top is linked.
- `treadDepthLocked` (boolean, required): Whether the going lengths are locked.
- `totalHeightLocked` (boolean, required): Whether the total height is locked.
- `rules` (StairRules, required): The Rules and Standards the stair is laid out by, as stored in the stair: every limit with whether it is applied.
- `extraTopTread` (boolean): Whether the stair has an extra tread at its top, as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take it.
- `extraBottomTread` (boolean): Whether the stair has an extra tread at its bottom, as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take it.
- `walkingLinePosition` (string ("Left", "Right", "Center", "Auto")): Where the walking line runs on the flight, as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take it.
- `walkingLineOffset` (number): The offset of the walking line from the side walkingLinePosition names, as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take it.
- `walkingLineSymbolPosition` (string ("Auto", "Center", "Custom")): Where the symbol of the walking line is placed (API_StairType::walkLineSymbPos), as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take it.
- `numberingType` (string ("Treads", "Risers")): Whether the steps are numbered on their treads or on their risers, as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take it.
- `uniformFinish` (boolean): Whether the flights and the landings share one finish setting.
- `uniformMonolithAttributes` (boolean): Whether the monolithic structures of the flights and the landings share one set of attributes.
- `uniformDrainings` (boolean): Whether the flights and the landings share one draining setting.
- `treads` (array of StairTreadPartSettings): The tread settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), the stair's own per-part defaults its treads are built from (API_StairType::tread), as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take them. The treads themselves are subelements (GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements).
- `risers` (array of StairRiserPartSettings): The riser settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), the stair's own per-part defaults its risers are built from (API_StairType::riser), as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take them.
- `headroom` (StairHeadroom): The headroom of the stair (Stair Settings > Headroom), as stored in the stair. Whether the headroom body is shown is a Model View Option, not part of the stair.
- `level` (number, required): Height of the stair base above the home story level.
- `zCoordinate` (number, required): Absolute elevation of the stair base.
- `finishVisible` (boolean, required): Whether the tread/riser finishes are modeled. If false only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is.
- `baseLinePoints` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The baseline polyline the stair is placed along, in model coordinates, as given to CreateStairs.
- `baseLineArcs` (array of PolyArc): The curved segments of the baseline, present only when it has any.
- `baseLineEdges` (array of object): The segment type of each baseline edge, one item per edge (edge i runs from baseLinePoints[i] to baseLinePoints[i + 1]), as CreateStairs takes them.
  - `segmentType` (string ("Flight", "Landing", "DividedLanding", "Unknown"), required)
- `baseLineVertices` (array of object): The turn at each baseline point, one item per point, as CreateStairs takes them. A stair whose turns Archicad decided itself reports Landing at every point, also at the first and last.
  - `turnType` (string ("None", "Landing", "Winder", "DividedLanding", "Unknown"), required)
  - `landingStartEdgeOffset` (number, required): The lead edge offset of the landing as Archicad calculated it.
  - `landingEndEdgeOffset` (number, required): The trail edge offset of the landing as Archicad calculated it.
  - `minLandingStartEdgeOffset` (number, required): The minimal lead edge offset.
  - `minLandingEndEdgeOffset` (number, required): The minimal trail edge offset.
- `basePlane` (CoordinateSystem3D): The stair's own coordinate system (API_StairType::basePlane), in model coordinates. Archicad keeps the baseline, the boundaries and the walking lines in it; the points reported here are already transformed by it (origin + x * xAxis + y * yAxis). A rotated stair has turned axes, a mirrored one axes of the other handedness (isMirrored).
- `isMirrored` (boolean): Whether the stair was mirrored, as its basePlane tells (xAxis and yAxis of the other handedness). Its left boundary is then on the right seen along the baseline, and its arcs bend the other way in its own coordinate system; the arcs reported are already turned back to model coordinates.
- `baselinePosition` (string ("Left", "Right", "Center", "Auto", "Unknown")): The edge of the flight the baseline runs on, as CreateStairs takes it (API_StairType::baselinePosition).
- `baselineOffset` (number): The offset of the baseline from that edge (API_StairType::baselineOffset).
- `inputDirection` (string ("Upward", "Inverse")): The walking direction along the baseline, as CreateStairs and ModifyStairs take it. Upward: baseLinePoints run from the bottom of the stair to its top. Inverse: they run from the top down. The walking lines and the boundaries run from the bottom up either way (seen on a stair drawn in Archicad 27); Archicad 29 creates and keeps stairs Upward even when Inverse is given.
- `leftBoundary` (StairBoundary): Read only. The left boundary line of the stair (the memo's stairBoundary[0]), seen along the baseline. Given when Archicad has calculated it. Archicad lays it out from the baseline and the flight width; the API cannot write it (see StairOutlineNotWritable).
- `rightBoundary` (StairBoundary): Read only. The right boundary line of the stair (the memo's stairBoundary[1]), seen along the baseline. Given when Archicad has calculated it. Archicad lays it out from the baseline and the flight width; the API cannot write it (see StairOutlineNotWritable).
- `walkingLine` (StairPolyline): Read only. The walking line of the stair (the memo's stairWalkingLine), the one Archicad lays the goings out along. Given when Archicad has calculated it. Archicad lays it out from the baseline and the flight width; the API cannot write it (see StairOutlineNotWritable).
- `customWalkingLine` (StairPolyline): Read only. The custom walking line of the stair (the memo's stairCustomWalkLine). Archicad 29 fills it on every stair: on a stair whose walking line was not edited it is the same as walkingLine. The API cannot write it (see StairOutlineNotWritable).
- `centerWalkingLine` (StairPolyline): Read only. The center walking line of the stair (the memo's stairCenterWalkLine). Archicad 29 fills it on every stair: on a stair with a centered walking line it is the same as walkingLine. Archicad lays it out from the baseline and the flight width; the API cannot write it (see StairOutlineNotWritable).
- `linkToSettings` (LinkToSettings)
- `uniformLeftRightSideSupports` (object): Whether the left and right side supports of the flights (run) and of the landings (landing) share their settings (API_StairType::uniformLeftRightSideSupports).
  - `run` (boolean, required)
  - `landing` (boolean, required)
- `stairDisplayType` (string ("Custom", "ByModelViewOptions", "Unknown")): Whether the floor plan display of the stair is set in the stair itself (Custom) or comes from the Model View Options (ByModelViewOptions) (API_StairType::stairDisplayType).
- `floorPlanLayout` (StairLayout): The floor plan display of the stair's components (API_StairType::fpdLayout).
- `reflectedCeilingPlanLayout` (StairLayout): The reflected ceiling plan display of the stair's components (API_StairType::rcpdLayout).
- `structureVisibility` (boolean): Whether the structure of the stair is shown on the floor plan (API_StairType::structureVisibility).
- `structureSymbols` (array of object): The symbol lines and fills of the stair's structure, one item per structure type and view (API_StairType::structSymbData).
  - `structureType` (string ("UnderStructure", "Stringer", "Unknown"), required)
  - `view` (StairSymbolView, required)
  - `visibleLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the visible structure lines; left out when not set.
  - `visibleLinePen` (integer, required)
  - `hiddenLineTypeId` (AttributeId): Line type of the hidden structure lines; left out when not set.
  - `hiddenLinePen` (integer, required)
  - `visibleFillId` (AttributeId): Fill type of the visible structure; left out when not set.
  - `visibleFillPen` (integer, required)
  - `visibleFillBackgroundPen` (integer, required)
  - `hiddenFillId` (AttributeId): Fill type of the hidden structure; left out when not set.
  - `hiddenFillPen` (integer, required)
  - `hiddenFillBackgroundPen` (integer, required)
- `monolithStructureSymbols` (array of object): The symbol lines and fills of a monolithic structure, one item per view and visible or hidden part (API_StairType::monolithStructureSymbolData).
  - `view` (StairSymbolView, required)
  - `part` (StairSymbolPart, required)
  - `goingLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `goingLinePen` (integer, required)
  - `goingNosingLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `goingNosingLinePen` (integer, required)
  - `connectionLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `connectionLinePen` (integer, required)
  - `connectionDetailLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `connectionDetailLinePen` (integer, required)
  - `drainingFillId` (AttributeId)
  - `drainingFillPen` (integer, required)
  - `drainingFillBackgroundPen` (integer, required)
  - `contourLineTypeId` (AttributeId)
  - `contourLinePen` (integer, required)
- `structureVisibilityOnStories` (array of object): Which structure symbols are shown on which of the stair's relevant stories, one item per view (API_StairType::structureVisibilityOnStories).
  - `view` (StairSymbolView, required)
  - `uniformSymbolRepresentationEnabled` (boolean, required)
  - `stories` (array of object, required): One item per story range relative to the stair's relevant stories (API_StairStructSymbRelevantStoriesID).
- `structures` (array of StairStructureDetails): The structure settings of the flights (Run) and of the landings (Landing), for each side (API_StairType::structure), in the order Run LeftSide, RightSide, UnderSide, then Landing LeftSide, RightSide, UnderSide. These are the settings Archicad builds the StairStructure subelements from.

### StairPolyline

object: A polyline of a stair, such as its walking line, in model coordinates (the coordinates of baseLinePoints).
- `points` (array of Coordinate2D, required)
- `arcs` (array of PolyArc, required): The curved segments of the polyline, with 0-based indices into points; empty when every segment is straight.

### StairBoundary

object: A side boundary line of a stair: an open polyline along that side of the flights and landings, in model coordinates (the coordinates of baseLinePoints). The left boundary, the right boundary reversed and the two segments joining their ends make the outline of the stair in plan.
- `isCustom` (boolean, required): Whether the boundary was edited by hand.
- `points` (array of Coordinate2D, required)
- `arcs` (array of PolyArc, required): The curved segments of the boundary, with 0-based indices into points; empty when every segment is straight.
- `edges` (array of object, required): One item per segment: edge i runs from points[i] to points[i + 1].
  - `visible` (boolean, required): Whether the part of the stair this segment describes is visible.

### StairOutlineNotWritable

object: Not writable: a boundary or a walking line of a stair, as GetDetailsOfElements reads it (leftBoundary, rightBoundary, walkingLine, customWalkingLine, centerWalkingLine). Archicad lays them out itself from the baseline and the flight width, and the API keeps none given: ACAPI_Element_Change refuses a stair memo that holds them (APIERR_GENERAL, also when it is unchanged) or ignores them, ACAPI_Element_ChangeExt does not take stairs (APIERR_BADID), and ACAPI_Element_Create lays them out again, whatever the memo holds (checked on Archicad 29). The walking line stays in the middle of the flight: Archicad 29 keeps walkingLinePosition Center and walkingLineOffset half the flight width whatever is written. An item that gives one is refused with an error, before anything is changed. Change the baseline instead (CreateStairs, RecreateStairs), or flightWidth (ModifyStairs), which moves the boundaries and keeps the walking line in the middle.

### StairStructureDetails

object: The settings of one structure of a stair: of one part (Run or Landing) and side in the stair's structures, or of a StairStructure subelement, whose values are the ones Archicad solved for that part (API_StairStructureType). monolith is given for a Monolith structure and sideStair for a Side structure; beam supported and cantilevered structures have no extra data.
- `role` (string ("Run", "Landing", "Unknown"), required): Whether the structure belongs to the flights (Run) or to the landings (Landing).
- `side` (string ("LeftSide", "RightSide", "UnderSide", "Unknown"), required): Where the structure supports the steps: from the left, from the right or from under.
- `visible` (boolean, required): Whether the structure is modeled.
- `structureType` (string ("Side", "Monolith", "BeamSupport", "CantileveredSupport", "Unknown"), required): The type of the structure: side stringers, monolithic, beam supported or cantilevered.
- `bottomType` (string ("Stepped", "Flat", "Smooth", "Unknown"), required): The bottom of the structure: stepped along with the steps, flat under the steps, or smooth.
- `thickness` (number, required): The thickness of the structure.
- `horizontalThickness` (number, required): The horizontal thickness of the structure.
- `monolith` (StairMonolithStructure)
- `sideStair` (StairSideStructure)

### StairMonolithStructure

object: The data of a monolithic stair structure (API_MonolithStairStructData). An attribute that is not set is left out.
- `thinning` (boolean, required): Whether the structure is thinned.
- `monolithThickness` (number, required): The thickness of the monolith.
- `bottomOversize` (number, required): The size of the horizontal bottom.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): The building material of the structure.
- `sideFillId` (AttributeId): The fill of the building material.
- `materialsChained` (boolean, required): Whether the surfaces of the structure are chained.
- `topMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial, required): The top surface of the structure.
- `leftMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial, required): The left side surface of the structure.
- `rightMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial, required): The right side surface of the structure.
- `bottomMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial, required): The bottom surface of the structure.
- `surfaceMaterialId` (AttributeId): The surface material of the structure.
- `cutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): The line type of the cut parts' 2D representation.
- `cutLinePen` (integer, required): The pen of the cut parts' 2D representation.
- `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): The line type of the 2D representation.
- `pen` (integer, required): The pen of the 2D representation.
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen, required): The cut fill pen of the structure.
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen, required): The cut fill background pen of the structure.
- `uniformDrainings` (boolean, required): Whether the drainings on the left and the right side are the same.
- `drainings` (array of StairStructureDraining, required): The drainings of the structure, on the left and on the right side.

### StairStructureDraining

object: The draining of one side of a monolithic stair structure (API_StairStructureDrainingData).
- `side` (string ("Left", "Right"), required)
- `enabled` (boolean, required): Whether the draining is modeled.
- `width` (number, required): The width of the draining.
- `offset` (number, required): The offset of the draining from the boundary.
- `horizontalDepth` (number, required): The horizontal depth of the draining.
- `verticalDepth` (number, required): The vertical depth of the draining.
- `material` (OverriddenMaterial, required): The surface of the draining.
- `surfaceType` (string ("Stepped", "Smooth"), required): Whether the draining is stepped or smooth.

### StairSideStructure

object: The data of a side (stringer) stair structure (API_SideStairStructData).
- `width` (number, required): The width of the stringer.
- `heightAboveTread` (number, required): The height of the stringer above its tread.
- `heightMeasure` (string ("Perpendicular", "Vertical"), required): How the height above the tread is measured: perpendicular to the stair or vertically.

### StairMonolithStructureSettings

object: The data of a monolithic stair structure that CreateStairs and ModifyStairs write (API_MonolithStairStructData), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements reads in StairMonolithStructure. Only the given fields are changed. An attribute is given by the id of an existing attribute of its type; an unknown id is refused.
- `thinning` (boolean): Whether the structure is thinned.
- `monolithThickness` (number): The thickness of the monolith. Archicad 26 and 28 were seen to keep 0 here for a Smooth structure, whose thickness is the structure's thickness; ModifyStairs then reports it as not applied.
- `bottomOversize` (number): The size of the horizontal bottom. Archicad 26 and 28 were seen to keep 0 here for a Smooth structure; ModifyStairs then reports it as not applied.
- `buildingMaterialId` (AttributeId): The building material of the structure.
- `sideFillId` (AttributeId): The fill of the building material.
- `materialsChained` (boolean): Whether the surfaces of the structure are chained. While they are, Archicad was seen to give the top the surface of another side, so give false with a surface of one side.
- `topMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): The top surface of the structure.
- `leftMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): The left side surface of the structure.
- `rightMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): The right side surface of the structure.
- `bottomMaterial` (OverriddenMaterial): The bottom surface of the structure.
- `surfaceMaterialId` (AttributeId): The surface material of the structure.
- `cutLineTypeId` (AttributeId): The line type of the cut parts' 2D representation.
- `cutLinePen` (integer): The pen of the cut parts' 2D representation.
- `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): The line type of the 2D representation.
- `pen` (integer): The pen of the 2D representation.
- `cutFillPen` (OverriddenPen): The cut fill pen of the structure.
- `cutFillBackgroundPen` (OverriddenPen): The cut fill background pen of the structure.
- `uniformDrainings` (boolean): Whether the drainings on the left and the right side are the same.
- `drainings` (array of StairStructureDrainingSettings): The drainings of the structure to change, each named by its side. Only the given fields of the given sides are changed.

### StairStructureDrainingSettings

object: The draining of one side of a monolithic stair structure that CreateStairs and ModifyStairs write (API_StairStructureDrainingData). Only the given fields are changed.
- `side` (string ("Left", "Right"), required): The side of the draining.
- `enabled` (boolean): Whether the draining is modeled.
- `width` (number): The width of the draining.
- `offset` (number): The offset of the draining from the boundary.
- `horizontalDepth` (number): The horizontal depth of the draining.
- `verticalDepth` (number): The vertical depth of the draining.
- `material` (OverriddenMaterial): The surface of the draining.
- `surfaceType` (string ("Stepped", "Smooth")): Whether the draining is stepped or smooth.

### StairSideStructureSettings

object: The data of a side (stringer) stair structure that CreateStairs and ModifyStairs write (API_SideStairStructData), with the keys GetDetailsOfElements reads in StairSideStructure. Only the given fields are changed.
- `width` (number): The width of the stringer.
- `heightAboveTread` (number): The height of the stringer above its tread.
- `heightMeasure` (string ("Perpendicular", "Vertical")): How the height above the tread is measured: perpendicular to the stair or vertically.

### StairSymbolView

string ("FloorPlan", "CeilingPlan", "Unknown"): The view a stair structure symbol setting belongs to (API_StairStructSymbViewID).

### StairSymbolPart

string ("Visible", "Hidden", "Unknown"): Whether a stair structure symbol setting is for the visible or the hidden part of the structure (API_StairStructSymbPartID).

### StairTreadPartSettings

object: The tread settings of the flights (Run) or of the landings (Landing) of a stair (API_StairType::tread[role]). CreateStairs and ModifyStairs change only the given fields of the given part.
- `role` (string ("Run", "Landing"), required): The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).
- `visible` (boolean): Whether the treads are present.
- `thickness` (number): The thickness of the treads.
- `offset` (number): The offset of the treads.
- `nosingType` (string ("ByValue", "BySlanting")): Whether the nosing is given by its length (nosingValue) or by the slant of the riser (nosingSlant).
- `nosingValue` (number): The length of the nosing.
- `nosingSlant` (number): The slant of the nosing in radians.

### StairRiserPartSettings

object: The riser settings of the flights (Run) or of the landings (Landing) of a stair (API_StairType::riser[role]). CreateStairs and ModifyStairs change only the given fields of the given part.
- `role` (string ("Run", "Landing"), required): The part of the stair: the flights (Run) or the landings (Landing).
- `visible` (boolean): Whether the risers are present.
- `thickness` (number): The thickness of the risers.
- `offset` (number): The offset of the risers.
- `crossSection` (string ("Simple", "Slanted")): The cross section of the risers.
- `angle` (number): The angle of a slanted riser in radians.
- `position` (string ("OnTread", "BehindTread")): Whether the risers stand on the treads or behind them.

### StairRules

object: The Rules and Standards of a Stair (API_StairRulesData): each limit as a value and whether it is applied (the check box of the rule). Archicad lays the steps out within the applied limits, so a stair can get another riser count and going than the ones given. GetDetailsOfElements and SolveStairBaseline return every field; CreateStairs and ModifyStairs write only the given ones.
- `riserHeightMinValue` (number): Minimum riser height.
- `riserHeightMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum riser height is applied.
- `riserHeightMaxValue` (number): Maximum riser height.
- `riserHeightMaxApplied` (boolean): Whether the maximum riser height is applied.
- `treadDepthMinValue` (number): Minimum going length.
- `treadDepthMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum going length is applied.
- `treadDepthMaxValue` (number): Maximum going length.
- `treadDepthMaxApplied` (boolean): Whether the maximum going length is applied.
- `ruleMinValue` (number): Minimum of 2 risers + going (2R+G).
- `ruleMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum 2R+G is applied.
- `ruleMaxValue` (number): Maximum of 2 risers + going (2R+G).
- `ruleMaxApplied` (boolean): Whether the maximum 2R+G is applied.
- `riserPlusGoingMinValue` (number): Minimum of riser height + going (R+G).
- `riserPlusGoingMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum R+G is applied.
- `riserPlusGoingMaxValue` (number): Maximum of riser height + going (R+G).
- `riserPlusGoingMaxApplied` (boolean): Whether the maximum R+G is applied.
- `riserGoingRatioMinValue` (number): Minimum ratio of riser height to going (R/G).
- `riserGoingRatioMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum R/G is applied.
- `riserGoingRatioMaxValue` (number): Maximum ratio of riser height to going (R/G).
- `riserGoingRatioMaxApplied` (boolean): Whether the maximum R/G is applied.
- `stairPitchMinValue` (number): Minimum stair pitch, as Archicad stores it.
- `stairPitchMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum stair pitch is applied.
- `stairPitchMaxValue` (number): Maximum stair pitch, as Archicad stores it.
- `stairPitchMaxApplied` (boolean): Whether the maximum stair pitch is applied.
- `landingLengthMinValue` (number): Minimum length of an automatic landing.
- `landingLengthMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum automatic landing length is applied.
- `walkingLineOffsetMinValue` (number): Minimum offset of an automatic landing (API_StairRulesData::walkingLineOffsetMinValue).
- `walkingLineOffsetMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum automatic landing offset is applied.
- `winderTurnOffsetMinValue` (number): Minimum winder width.
- `winderTurnOffsetMinApplied` (boolean): Whether the minimum winder width is applied.

### StairHeadroom

object: The headroom of a Stair (API_StairHeadroomData, Stair Settings > Headroom): the clear space above the flights that Archicad checks against the elements above the stair. GetDetailsOfElements returns every field; CreateStairs and ModifyStairs write only the given ones.
- `method` (string ("RightAngleToSlope", "VerticallyToSlope", "Unknown")): How the headroom is generated: at right angle to the slope of the stair (APIHM_RightAngleToSlope) or vertically to it (APIHM_VerticallyToSlope). GetDetailsOfElements returns Unknown for a value it does not know; CreateStairs and ModifyStairs refuse Unknown.
- `height` (number): The height of the headroom.
- `leftOffset` (number): The offset of the headroom from the left side of the stair.
- `rightOffset` (number): The offset of the headroom from the right side of the stair.

### StairLayoutSettings

object: The floor plan or reflected ceiling plan display settings of a Stair that CreateStairs and ModifyStairs write (API_StairLayoutData without its visibility and isAutoOnStoryVisibility, which storyVisibility sets): the shown stories and components, the symbol on each story, the break line and the line type, pen and fill overrides. Only the given fields are changed; GetDetailsOfElements reads them back in floorPlanLayout and reflectedCeilingPlanLayout, with the same keys.
- `storyVisibility` (string ("HomeStoryOnly", "HomeAndOneStoryUp", "HomeAndOneStoryDown", "HomeAndOneStoryUpAndDown", "OneStoryUp", "OneStoryDown", "AllStories", "AllRelevantStories", "AllRelevantAndOneStoryUp", "AllRelevantAndOneStoryDown")): The stories the stair is shown on. The AllRelevant... values let Archicad work out the relevant stories from the stair's height (isAutoOnStoryVisibility true); the others set the shown stories (visibility) to match and isAutoOnStoryVisibility false.
- `showWalkingLine` (boolean): Whether the walking line is shown.
- `showNumbering` (boolean): Whether the step numbering is shown.
- `showUpDownText` (boolean): Whether the up/down text (walking direction label) is shown.
- `showDescription` (boolean): Whether the stair description is shown.
- `showStructure` (boolean): Whether the stair structures are shown.
- `gridTypeAbove` (StairGridType): The symbol shown on the stories above the stair's relevant stories (Unknown is refused).
- `gridTypeTop` (StairGridType): The symbol shown on the top relevant story (Unknown is refused).
- `gridTypeMiddle` (StairGridType): The symbol shown on the middle relevant stories (Unknown is refused).
- `gridTypeBottom` (StairGridType): The symbol shown on the bottom relevant story (Unknown is refused).
- `gridTypeBelow` (StairGridType): The symbol shown on the stories below the stair's relevant stories (Unknown is refused).
- `breakLineAngleType` (string ("AngleToVertical", "AngleToHorizontal", "NumberOfGoings")): How the angle of the break line is given: by breakLineAngle to the vertical or to the horizontal, or worked out from breakLineAngleNumberOfGoings.
- `breakLineAngle` (number): The angle of the break line, used when breakLineAngleType is AngleToVertical or AngleToHorizontal.
- `breakLineAngleNumberOfGoings` (integer): The number of goings the break line crosses, used when breakLineAngleType is NumberOfGoings.
- `breakLineDistance` (number): The gap of the break line.
- `breakLinePositionType` (string ("FloorPlanCutPlaneHeight", "CustomHeight", "AtNthRiser")): Where the break line is: at the floor plan cut plane height, at a custom height or at a given riser.
- `upperBreakLineCustomPosition` (number): The height of the upper break line, used when breakLinePositionType is CustomHeight.
- `lowerBreakLineCustomPosition` (number): The height of the lower break line, used when breakLinePositionType is CustomHeight.
- `upperBreakLineNthRiserPosition` (integer): The riser of the upper break line, used when breakLinePositionType is AtNthRiser.
- `lowerBreakLineNthRiserPosition` (integer): The riser of the lower break line, used when breakLinePositionType is AtNthRiser.
- `overrideLineType` (boolean): Whether lineTypeId overrides the line types of the stair's components.
- `lineTypeId` (AttributeId): The override line type: a line type of the project.
- `overridePen` (boolean): Whether pen overrides the line pens of the stair's components.
- `pen` (integer): The override line pen.
- `overrideSymbolFill` (boolean): Whether symbolFillId and its pens override the symbol fills of the stair's components.
- `symbolFillId` (AttributeId): The override symbol fill: a fill type of the project.
- `symbolFillPen` (integer): The foreground pen of the override symbol fill.
- `symbolFillBackgroundPen` (integer): The background pen of the override symbol fill.

### StairStructureSymbolSettings
